title: [iOS 26] iPhone 16 / Pro Max: Fix Not Charging Issue
transcription: If your iPhone 16, 16 Pro, Pro Max or the Plus is not charging. So in this video, I will show you how you can fix this issue. First of all, just check the charging cable of your iPhone and check if it is damaged or not. If the charging cable of your iPhone is damaged, just replace it with a new one. Also check the adapter of your iPhone and make sure that you're using Apple's original charger with your iPhone. Now, if the issue is not in the charger of your iPhone, then for the next step, just check the charging port of your iPhone and check if it is blocked by any dust or debris. Because in many cases, this issue appears when you have dust stuck in your charging port. So just clean the charging port of your iPhone and check if this fixes your issue or not. Now, if this also did not fix your issue, then for the next step, just force restart your iPhone. For that, just press and release the volume up button and the volume down button. Then press and hold the side button on your iPhone until the screen of your iPhone goes black and the Apple logo appears on the screen. Once the Apple logo appears on the screen, just release the side button. Now, if the charging of your iPhone stops at a specific percentage, let's say if it stops at 80 or 90%, then just go to settings and tap on battery. Under the battery settings, just tap on charging. And over here, just check if you have set any charging limit or not. Let's say if you have selected 90%, then the charging of your iPhone will stop at the percentage which you have set. So make sure you set it at 100%. Tap on set limit to 100%. But if this also did not fix your issue, then this could be a software glitch. For that, just go back to the main settings page and tap on general. Under the general settings, just tap on software update and check if you have any software update available. If you have any software update available, just update the software of your iPhone. But if this also did not work, then you might have enabled a setting which might be causing this issue. For that, just go back to general. Now this time, just tap on transfer or reset iPhone. Then tap on reset and from this pop-up menu, just select reset all settings. Then enter your lock screen pin and tap on reset all settings. Now, this option will not delete any data of your iPhone. It will just reset all the settings of your iPhone in case if you have enabled a setting which might be causing this issue. But if this also did not work, then you might have a hardware problem with your iPhone. Just take your iPhone to the nearest service center and they will fix your issue. And in the meantime, you can either charge your iPhone using wireless charging or you can charge your iPhone using a MagSafe charger. And this is how you can fix the no charging issue on the iPhone 16, 16 Pro, Pro Max and the Plus. Make sure to like, comment, and subscribe. Thank you for watching.

California's governor and Attorney General said they were demanding answers from XAI earlier Wednesday. That after Musk said he wasn't aware of any naked underage images generated by Groc. title: Tesla Lithium Refinery
transcription: This refinery is the first spodumene to lithium hydroxide refinery in North America. We're deploying a new technology platform that is inherently uh much more environmentally friendly and cleaner. It's a simpler process, it's a less expensive process. I'm Jason Bevan, I'm the site manager for Tesla's Gulf Coast lithium refinery just outside of Corpus Christie, Texas. Spodumene is a lithium-containing ore. It's a hard rock material that is rich in lithium. We sustainably source spodumene and bring it to site, where we then run it through a series of conveyance systems, take it through a kiln and cooler. From there, we take it through an alkaline leech and additional purification steps, take it into crystallization and produce battery-grade lithium hydroxide. Our process is more sustainable than traditional methods and eliminates hazardous byproducts and instead produces a co-product named analcime used in concrete mixes. From breaking ground in 2023 to running rock through the kiln in 2024 to start a full integrated plant startup now in 2025, we've achieved the fastest time to market for this first of its kind technology. By removing many of the traditional stage gate hurdles seen in large projects, we were able to complete feasibility, design, and construction in parallel, significantly accelerating our construction timeline. This refinery really enables us to have access to the critical minerals for energy storage, for battery manufacturing, and ultimately for EV growth. and it enables us to accelerate Tesla's mission by regionalizing supply chains for battery minerals and materials, by providing jobs, by cutting emissions from the transportation network that's required for those supply chains. title: NBA SUSPENDS Dennis Schröder 3 Games For Luka Dončić Confrontation। USA SportsLine
transcription: The NBA has handed down a three-game suspension to Sacramento Kings guard Dennis Schroder for a serious post-game incident. The league announced that Schroder sought out an opposing player, reportedly Dallas star Luka Dončić, in an arena hallway approximately 40 minutes after the Kings' loss to the Lakers on December 28th and initiated a confrontation, attempting to strike him. The suspension is a significant blow for a Kings team already struggling through a dismal season with an 8 and 30 record. Schroder, a veteran of 13 NBA seasons, has been a key contributor, averaging 13 points and nearly six assists per game this year. He will miss the team's next three games against Houston, the Clippers, and New York. This isn't Schroder's first brush with controversy this season, as he was previously suspended one game for throwing his mouth guard at an official. The latest incident, involving a calculated post-game confrontation with another player, has drawn a sterner penalty from the league office. For a Kings franchise mired in a difficult year, losing a veteran leader for three games adds another layer of challenges as they navigate the rest of the season.

title: AMD Just Dropped A Monster Mini-PC: Meet Ryzen AI Halo | CES 2026
transcription:
Hello everyone, Marco Chipetta here behind the camera to give you a super quick look direct from CES 2026 of AMD's AI Halo small form factor system.
AMD's CEO Dr. Lisa Su showed off AI Halo during her keynote to kick off CES 2026. This tiny little machine is powered by AMD's current flagship APU series, the AMD Ryzen AI Max. Um formerly code-named Strix Halo. Now, these chips feature up to 16 Zen 5 CPU cores with a 40 CU RDNA 3.5 integrated GPU and an XDNA 2 NPU. The systems will also feature up to 128 gigs of LP DDR5X memory connected to the APU on a 256-bit interface. And up to 96 gigabytes of that memory is accessible by the GPU, which unlocks some really cool capabilities with larger AI models. AMD's goal with AI Halo is to get AI engineers developing their models and software on AMD hardware. Similar to what Nvidia is doing with its small form factor DGX Spark. No word yet on final availability or pricing, but AMD does expect to significantly undercut Nvidia's DGX Spark. As you can see taking a look around the system, there's not much going on. There's some stylized venting all around the system with AMD logos on the front and on the top. And on the back of the system, you have a power button, full-sized HDMI port, a 10 gig ethernet port and four USB-C ports. Two of those ports are USB 3 and the other two are USB 4 with DisplayPort and one also offers power delivery. And with that, I think I'll wrap this up. transcription: If you are offered a Home Fire safety visit by the London Fire Brigade, here's what you can expect when we visit. Firefiighters will visit at the agreed time and start with a friendly chat about you, your home and your daily routine. Together, you'll walk through your home and look at simple ways to reduce fire risk, including cooking, smoking, heaters, candles, electrics, and charging. We will also check your smoke and heat alarms and test that they are working properly. If you need extra fire detection, firefighters can fit free smoke alarms during the visit and show you how to test them. We will also talk through bedtime safety and help you think about an escape plan so everyone knows what to do if there is a fire. title: Roborock Rover First Look - This is a GAME CHANGER!
transcription: Welcome to Vacuum Wars where we're covering the latest news coming out of CES 2026. And Roborock has just introduced a product that might finally solve one of the biggest limitations in the robot vacuum industry, and it's called the Roborock Seros Rover. And according to the company, it features the world's first robot vacuum with stair climbing legs. At IFA in Berlin last year, we saw brands like Dreamy, Mova and Eufy try to tackle the stair climbing issue with separate climbing modules that carried the robot itself up and down the stairs. But those modules are pretty big and they can't actually vacuum the stairs themselves. The robots just get carried up and down the stairs. The new Seros Rover uses a legs with wheels architecture where each wheel is paired with a leg like mechanism. These can deploy independently to keep the robot's body level on uneven surfaces, slopes, and yes, stairs. Roborock says that this design allows it to raise and lower each wheel independently, execute agile turns and perform movements intended to imitate human mobility. They're using AI algorithms paired with motion sensors and 3D spatial information to make this happen, which is much more in line with what's happening in humanoid robotics lately, and it's pretty exciting to see. This would presumably completely solve the threshold climbing issue, but the biggest win here for the robot vacuum industry is that the Seros Rover doesn't just climb, it cleans every step as it goes. Also, it seems to be significantly smaller than the other prototype stair climbers that we've seen so far. There's also demo footage showing the robot executing small jumps to clear laser obstacles and maintaining its balance while testers throw tennis balls at it. I'm not sure what the application of either of these would be for robot vacuums, but it all suggests that this technology isn't just about climbing, it's about physically reacting to a dynamic environment in a way that we just haven't seen before. Roborock does emphasize that the Seros Rover is currently in development and the launch date is unconfirmed. There are still major questions that we at Vacuum Wars still would like to be answered, and I hope to have some of those answers at least in our full coverage of CES 2026 in a video coming out this Friday. We will also be putting out short form videos on TikTok and YouTube Shorts all this week during CES. So, stay tuned for our big CES coverage video this Friday and be sure to subscribe to Vacuum Wars here on YouTube or TikTok to keep up with all the latest information about CES 2026.

title: How to Create a Slide Deck (Presentation) Automatically for FREE using Google NotebookLM
transcription: Hi everyone, welcome back. In this video, let's learn how to create a slide deck automatically using Google Notebook LM. No PowerPoint design, no manual slide creation, no copy pasting content. Just upload your material and notebook LM builds the presentation for you. Let's start from zero and do this step by step. First, let's open notebook LM in the browser. On the home page, let's click create new. A new notebook opens. At the top, let's rename it. For example, AI concepts slide deck. Now remember this rule, notebook LM creates slide decks only from the sources we add. So let's add our content. On the left side in the sources panel, let's click add sources. We can upload PDFs, add article links, paste copied text or even add YouTube videos. For this demo, let's add a PDF file that contains notes about AI. Click on upload files, select the PDF file and upload it. Once the source is added, notebook LM reads and understands the material. Now let's generate the slide deck. Move to the right side to the studio panel. Here, let's click slide deck. As soon as we click it, notebook LM analyzes our content. It identifies main topics, key points and supporting details. Then it automatically organizes everything into a structured presentation. While it's generating, we can see the customization options. Let's click the pencil icon. Here, we can choose the format. If we want detailed slides with full explanations, let's choose detailed deck. If we want clean slides to present live, let's choose presenter slides. Next, we can select the language. We can also choose the length, short, default or long. And we can add a prompt for example, create slides for beginners with simple examples. Now let's close this and wait for the deck to finish generating. Once it's ready, the slide deck appears inside the studio panel. Let's click to open it. Now we can scroll through the slides, start a full screen slideshow or review each slide one by one. If we want to share it, we can use the share option. And if we want to keep it, we can download it as a PDF file. That's it. We just converted raw content into a complete slide deck using Google Notebook LM. This is perfect for students, teachers and professionals who want fast presentations without extra effort.

title: About 40 killed in New Year’s Eve fire at Swiss Alps bar
transcription: Video from inside the New Year's celebration in the Swiss Alps shows the chaos as the deadly flames spread at a bar popular with young people and tourists. You can hear the screaming, people scrambling for the exit as the flames rip through the confined spaces of the bar Le Constellation. Swiss authorities say about 40 people were killed and more than 100 injured in the fire that began at 1:30 a.m. The cause of the blaze now under investigation, though Swiss officials say they've ruled out terrorism, calling the fire an accident that led to an explosion inside the bar. Just 90 minutes earlier, celebrations on the streets of the upscale ski resort Crans Montana. But what many thought were the sounds of New Year's Eve fireworks were in fact one of the worst tragedies Switzerland has ever experienced, according to the country's president. She let go of his arm and now she says she can't reach him. Officials warn identifying the dead could take days. Many of those killed were from abroad. Witnesses describing the sheer panic as people tried desperately to escape. A lot of people were screaming, trying to escape, and I saw a lot of people on the floor and I think this people was dead. Officials say first responders were on the scene within minutes and the fire was quickly put out. Many so badly burned, they were taken to various hospitals across the country. The grueling work of identifying the dead and notifying their families is now underway. And Danielle joins me now from the scene in Switzerland. Danielle, it is just heartbreaking. There's a lot of speculation about the cause of the fire and if a sparkler might have been involved? Yeah, Kate, some of those who escaped talked about how champagne bottles had lit sparklers in them and that they were waved, some of them pretty high, hitting the ceiling, and then that's how the fire started. title: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra - Official First Look!
transcription: Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra official first look is here. And this time, it's leaked by Samsung itself. Samsung may have unintentionally leaked the design of the Galaxy S26 Ultra ahead of its official launch. The flagship is expected to debut in late February, but an important One UI app has seemingly exposed the phone's official design mockup. The latest Tips app in one UI 8.5 introduces Samsung's new privacy display feature. To explain this feature, the app uses a graphical mockup, and that device strongly resembles the Galaxy S26 Ultra. The upcoming Galaxy S26 Ultra appears to feature more rounded corners compared to the S25 Ultra. Samsung has also reduced the bezel thickness, resulting in a larger visible display area. The display's camera cutout looks slightly bigger than before. This could mean a wider field of view, similar to what Apple introduced on its recent iPhone models. As usual, the left side of the phone's alloy frame remains clean with no buttons. The mockup also suggests that Samsung has further smooth the transition between the frame and the display, likely to improve in-hand comfort. On the right side, there are three buttons, volume up, volume down, and a side key. This side key is multifunctional and can act as a power button or be used to launch an AI assistant. The Galaxy S26 Ultra mockup also matches the recently leaked dummy units. The S Pen slot appears to be pushed as far left as possible, and the S Pen itself now has a rounded top, matching the phone's softer design language. At the bottom, the phone includes a SIM tray, USB Type-C port for charging and data, a primary microphone, and a speaker grill. The top frame houses a secondary microphone. Overall, these changes show Samsung's effort to refine the Galaxy S26 Ultra's design. While the updates are subtle, they could make a noticeable difference in daily use. That said, the final design won't be officially confirmed until Samsung's unpacked event next month. Samsung is expected to launch the Galaxy S26 series on February 25th, 2026. All right, guys, that's everything we know so far about the Galaxy S26 Ultra's leaked design. Let me know in the comments what you think about these subtle changes. Hit or miss? As always, I'll keep you updated with every new leak and confirmation. I'll see you in the next one. Peace out.

Now, if you have done that, and if this also did not fix your issue, then this could be a software glitch. To fix this issue, just go to settings and tap on general. Go to software update. title: Communities rebuild after Los Angeles wildfires
transcription: A catastrophic disaster at the beginning of the year changed the landscape of Southern California forever, leaving scenes of destruction and causing heartbreak for thousands that saw their own homes burnt to the ground. NBC's Liz Kretz visits the catastrophic LA wildfires. This was Southern California on January 7th. Two fires started burning on opposite sides of LA County. The Palisades fire and Eton fire scorched homes and left devastation in their wake. This is a tragedy. I was on the ground on day one. We are in bumper-to-bumper traffic right now as hundreds of people try to get out. You can see flames here on both sides of the road with very little visibility. Fireefighters worked around the clock, battling more than just the flames. Water pressure has been a big issue. We have had hydrants, dead hydrants. One of the biggest challenges in the firefight, the hurricane force Santa Ana winds. Even residents jumped in to try and save their neighborhoods. I can't control any of this, but I can, I can turn on the garden hose, you know. Yeah, Scott definitely saved a lot. What do you want to say to Scott? I think he is a hero. Despite tireless efforts, many people didn't have a home to return to. We lost everything we own, but It doesn't even look like a house anymore. It just looks like a something. For Brianna Navarro, the loss unimaginable. She says her 83-year-old grandmother, Arlene Kelly, died inside her home. It's devastating. We didn't expect to lose her so tragically. Some homes survived the flames. I was shocked that it's still here. But toxic ash from the fires means many residents still haven't been able to go home months later. I mean, my community is pretty much gone. I am very grateful that the house is still there. However, from an insurance standpoint, I think it would have been easier if it had burned. Nine months after the fires, police arrested Jonathan Winderneckt, the 29-year-old accused of starting the Palisades fire. Investigators determining that a different fire he ignited on New Year's Day never fully went out and would reignite a week later into the deadly inferno. We will prove beyond a reasonable doubt that he intentionally started this fire. Rinderneck pleaded not guilty and his lawyer said he's innocent. I did witness one bright spot in all the devastation. Oh my god. The reunion of Casey Colvin and his dog Oreo. Casey had one person he particularly wanted to thank. This guy saved your life. Calfire Battalion Chief, Brent Pasqua. When I first met you, I was in the middle of crisis. I was in the middle of a fire storm. My dogs would have died if not for you. Now, in both the Palisades and Altadena, communities coming together to rebuild. A welcome sign of hope. Liz Kretz, NBC News, Los Angeles.

title: Keir Starmer’s 2026 New Year message
transcription: Things have been tough in Britain for a while. For many, life is still harder than it should be. You long for a bit more money in your pockets, a meal out, a holiday, the chance to make a special family moment extra special. In 2026, the choices we've made will mean more people will begin to feel positive change in your bills, your communities, and your health service. But even more people will feel once again a sense of hope, a belief that things can and will get better. feel that the promise of renewal can become a reality. and my government will make it that reality. More police on the streets by March, energy bills down and the number of new health hubs up in April. More funding for local communities. And with that change, decline will be reversed. That opportunity for you and pride in your community can be restored. I share the frustration about the pace of change. The challenges we face were decades in the making. And renewal is not an overnight job. But putting our country back on a stable footing will become our strength. strength that means we can support you with the cost of living. Rail fares, prescription charges, fuel duty, all frozen. £150 pounds cut from your energy bills. A boost once again to the national minimum wage, a major cut to the cost of childcare. We are getting Britain back on track. By staying the course, we will defeat the decline and division offered by others. For all the times that have been tough, I hope the festive period has brought good moments, precious time with your family, a chance to celebrate what's most important to you. I wish you more of those moments next year, when things start to feel easier, when politics shows it can help again. When Britain turns the corner with our future now in our control. The real Britain will shine through more strongly. Happy New Year.

title: Nvidia’s $5 billion Intel bet just became official
transcription: Nvidia's $5 billion Intel bet just became official. Intel confirmed it completed Nvidia's $5 billion share sale on December 26th after regulatory clearance, formalizing Nvidia's roughly 4% stake. What began as a September announcement now sits as settled cash and issued shares on Intel's balance sheet. Nvidia bought 214,776,632 Intel shares at $23.28 each in a private placement. The long-awaited cash infusion landed as a visible vote of confidence, ending months of future tense speculation and transforming a pending deal into finalized ownership. Nvidia's buy-in price was 36% below Intel's prior Friday close, underlining the leverage of a market heavyweight. Early trading showed Nvidia down about 1.7% while Intel stayed mostly flat, as the headline became a routine regulatory filing. The private placement granted Nvidia no special governance or information rights beyond standard shareholders. Federal Trade Commission early termination of the Hart-Scott-Rodino waiting period on December 18th cleared the final regulatory hurdle, shifting the deal from pending to fully done. Jensen Huang described the partnership as historic, noting teams have co-developed architecture across CPUs, servers and PCs for over a year. He framed the investment as the next step in reinventing computing layers driven by accelerating artificial intelligence demand. Analysts likened the pairing to longtime rivals uniting. Earlier, the federal government engineered a roughly 10% Intel equity stake, signaling industrial policy backing. In President Donald Trump's AI posture, Intel emerged as a corporate vessel for made here ambition. Intel and Nvidia plan to co-develop data center and PC products, including custom X86 CPUs and hybrid system on chips. The deal omits any pledge to move Nvidia GPUs from TSMC. For Intel, the cash and association bolster credibility. For Nvidia, it eases entry into X86 ecosystems.

title: Intel Analog Engineer Technical Interview Question Walkthrough
transcription: Welcome back to Voltage Learning. Let's walk through this Intel analog engineer question because it touches on a very common bring-up issue that trips up even experienced designers. The question asks, during bring-up, an op-amp configured as a voltage follower shows an output that rails high even when the input is at mid-supply. Which condition most commonly causes this behavior? At first glance, this can feel confusing. After all, a voltage follower is supposed to simply mirror the input. But the key insight here is that negative feedback only works if the op-amp is operating within its valid input range. Even though the circuit uses feedback, the op-amp's input pins still must stay within the device's input common mode range. If the input voltage exceeds that range, often because the op-amp is not rail to rail on its inputs, the internal input stage can saturate. When that happens, the feedback loop effectively breaks down. The op-amp can no longer regulate properly, and the output often slams into one of the supply rails, frequently the positive rail during bring-up. Now, let's briefly rule out the other options. High open loop gain is normal and expected. It doesn't cause an output to rail by itself. Slew rate limits how fast the output can move, not where it settles in steady state. And a lighter output load actually makes it easier for the op-amp to drive the correct voltage, not harder. So the correct answer is, the input common mode exceeds the op-amp's valid range. This is exactly the kind of issue that shows up during early lab bring-up and silicon validation. Intel interviewers like this question because it tests whether you understand that data sheet limits still apply, even in seemingly simple configurations like voltage followers. If you want analog explanations grounded in real world debug scenarios, not just textbook theory, that's what Voltage Learning is built to deliver.

questions.question: What is the central problem being discussed in the audio regarding an op-amp circuit?
questions.answer: The problem is a common 'bring-up' issue where an op-amp configured as a voltage follower shows an output that 'rails high' (goes to the positive supply voltage) even when the input is at mid-supply.

questions.question: According to the speaker, what is the most common reason for this op-amp behavior?
questions.answer: The most common reason is that the input voltage has exceeded the op-amp's valid input common-mode range, which causes the internal input stage to saturate and effectively breaks the negative feedback loop.

transcription: Flat-headed cats have been successfully detected and filmed in southern Thailand for the first time in almost 30 years. One of the world's rarest cats, it was last documented here back in 1995, leading some to believe it was possibly extinct. Conservationists, however, thought otherwise. We had heard reports for many years and were confident that the species was still present. Rettapan Padinarinsen, conservation program manager for Panthera Thailand, told IFL Science. What was needed was the right study design to confirm it. The largest ever survey of the species began in 2024, using camera traps from Thailand's Department of National Parks, Wildlife and Plant Conservation, and Panthera Thailand, a global wildcat conservation organization. 13 detections were made in 2024, and a further 16 detections were made in 2025. Most exciting of all, the observations included a female flat-headed cat with her cub. Flat-headed cats are the smallest in Southeast Asia. They weigh half that of a typical domestic cat and have a distinctive flattened forehead and elongated skull. They are small, nocturnal and prefer to occupy dense terrain, making searching for them in the wild that much harder. Even catching them on camera traps can be difficult. But using lessons learned from studying fishing cats, Panthera were able to identify the best sites for camera placement, leading to the successful detection and photographic evidence of the flat-headed cat. It's estimated there are 2,500 flat-headed cats globally, and they're classed as endangered by the IUCN, but in Thailand, it was considered possibly extinct. A new Panthera-led IUCN assessment is now expected in 2026.

Though Hunter also acknowledged some mistakes, calling that consequential debate between President Biden and then candidate Donald Trump a complete and utter disaster. He also said the withdrawal from Afghanistan was a real low point in his father's presidency, saying in the podcast, quote, I think one of the failures was the way in which they executed the withdrawal from Afghanistan. I think it was an obvious effing failure. I think 13 Marines are dead. I think that there was a better way to do it. Adding, quote, my dad always knew this also is that the buck stops with him. He noted that his dad, President Joe Biden did support a bipartisan bill on immigration reform that looked to be gaining enough support to pass in the Senate before then candidate Trump stepped in to kill it. title: India Closes Visa Center in Chattogram After Anti-India Protests
transcription: Hello everyone. Today, we are discussing an important development in South Asia involving India and Bangladesh. Recently, anti-India protests were reported in different parts of Bangladesh. These demonstrations were organized by various groups who raised slogans against Indian policies and actions. During some of these protests, tensions increased and concerns were raised about the safety of Indian institutions and personnel in the country. Following these events, India decided to temporarily shut down its visa application center in Chattogram, one of the major port cities of Bangladesh. This decision was taken as a precautionary security measure. According to Indian officials, the visa center in Chattogram plays an important role, as thousands of Bangladeshi citizens apply for Indian visas every month. These visas are mainly used for medical treatment, education, business, tourism, and family visits. With the closure of the center, many applicants are now facing delays and uncertainty. Indian authorities stated that the decision was not meant to harm people-to-people relations but was necessary to ensure the safety of staff and visitors. They also clarified that the situation is being closely monitored and services may resume once conditions improve. On the other hand, officials in Bangladesh emphasized that they are committed to maintaining law and order and ensuring the security of foreign missions. Bangladesh and India share historically strong diplomatic, cultural, and economic ties, and both countries have worked closely on regional cooperation. Political analysts believe that such incidents highlight the sensitivity of public sentiment and the importance of diplomatic dialogue. While protests are a form of expression, any situation that threatens diplomatic operations can impact bilateral relations and ordinary citizens. Experts are also pointing out that visa services are a crucial link between the two nations. Any disruption affects students, patients, and families who depend on cross-border travel. In conclusion, the closure of the Indian visa center in Chattogram reflects growing concerns over security following recent protest. Both countries are expected to engage in dialogue to reduce tensions and restore normal services as soon as possible. Thank you for watching.

title: One-Third of the City Hit by Massive Blackout | WION Pulse
transcription: A major power outage has plunged large parts of San Francisco into darkness, disrupting daily life for more than 120,000 residents. The blackout began early Saturday afternoon and quickly spread across a large swath of northern San Francisco, including the Richmond and Presidio neighborhoods, as well as areas around Golden Gate Park. At its peak, nearly one-third of the city's customers were without power. City officials say the outage caused widespread traffic chaos, darkened street lights and Christmas decorations, and forced many restaurants and shops to shut their doors temporarily. Pacific Gas and Electric now says the city's power grid has been stabilized and no additional customer outages are expected. Power has been restored for about 95,000 customers in the city. However, the utility company has not confirmed when electricity will be fully restored to all affected areas. Public transport was also hit with uh mini buses and trains bypassing several stations due to the loss of electricity. The San Francisco Department of Emergency Management urged residents to avoid non-essential travel, treat down traffic signals as four-way stops, and call 911 only for life-threatening emergencies. Fire officials later confirmed that at least part of the outage was triggered by a fire inside a power substation near 8th and Mission Street. With power still out in several pockets of the city, authorities say restoration efforts are continuing and residents are being asked to stay alert, conserve energy, and prepare for possible extended disruptions into the night. that the electricity might not come back on for some

title: ByteDance Signs Deal To Divest TikTok U.S. Assets | Asia One News
transcription: Tik Tok's parent company, ByteDance has signed binding agreements to sell most of the app's US assets and form a joint venture with American and international investors, a move aimed at avoiding a potential US ban on the popular video platform. Under the deal, ByteDance will reduce its ownership stake to below 20% while US-based investors including Oracle and Silver Lake will take significant holdings in the new joint venture. Abu Dhabi investment firm, MGX will also join the ownership group with the remaining shares held by existing bytedance investors. This agreement follows repeated delays ordered by US President Donald Trump on enforcing a law that would ban Tik Tok unless its US operations were sold. The transaction is expected to be completed by January 2026, allowing Tik Tok to continue operating in the US where it has more than 170 million users. US lawmakers first approved the ban in 2024 over national security concerns related to data handling and Chinese ownership. The current administration has since worked toward a negotiated sale rather than an outright shutdown of the platform.

title: A Doctor Explains How AI Will Change Medicine Forever
transcription: The combination of medicine and AI is something that we're hearing more and more about. In fact, I once heard somebody say that honestly, you know, AI can diagnose you just as good if if not better than doctors these days. And part of that was exciting to me and part of that was scary. Speak about it for us. Yeah, I mean, as someone who was a doctor not very long ago, it is quite a scary idea that our job can maybe be done better than us by an AI. and it is a job that a lot of doctors take very seriously, are very passionate about and are very good at. But in some ways technology can do certain aspects of it better. I think that when I think about AI in medicine, right now, where the technology is is a very unique place and I think that we will see a lot of changes over the next five years. I think that AI as it currently stands is really good at doing a certain set of tasks or parts of medicine. One of those that I think that we'll see AI used a lot more in is areas of diagnostic support. I think what AI is really amazing at is taking a huge amount of context and information and finding key insights, condensing it down, and narrowing down this, you know, potential plethora of conditions that someone may have and finding the key points that will really point to like the root cause diagnosis for an individual. And I think that humans are very good at this too and it's actually very, very difficult to do. But I think that AI has, number one, the ability to ingest stupidly large amounts of context. So while me as a human doctor might need to read a summary of a patient that another doctor has written, it can actually end up, um an AI is able to ingest maybe 20 years of medical context about someone all at once. And so I'm very bullish on AI actually helping with areas such as diagnosis. And I'm actually very bullish on AI getting very strong in this area of diagnosis. That being said, I think there are areas that people thought AI would be amazing in, but haven't seen as much progress as we would have expected. A common one is everyone thought radiologists were going to be out of business. And so radiologists, um, are the people who will look at x-rays, MRIs, and scans and images and make conclusions or diagnosis from those images. And it seems like something an AI model should be really, really great at doing, but when people actually tried this out and implemented it, it's actually quite complex to do and there's a lot of moving parts. It's very difficult to train models on it. So it's very interesting seeing what's happened over the last 5 10 years because realistically, everyone's been screaming about AI in medicine for quite a while. It's just been a bit quieter than it is now. but it's something it's something that I'm very curious to see develop over the next like two to five years.

title: TikTok to Sell Majority of US Assets to American Investors Amid Security Concerns
transcription: TikTok's Chinese parent company, Bytedance, has signed binding agreements with three major investors to sell just over 80% of its US assets, TikTok CEO Shou Zi Chu announced to employees on Thursday, 18th December. The move is aimed at avoiding a potential US government ban and resolving years of uncertainty over the app's future in America, where more than 170 million users engage with it regularly. The agreements involve Oracle, Silver Lake, and Abu Dhabi-based MGX, which will form a new US entity, TikTok USDS Joint Venture LLC. Oracle, Silver Lake, and MGX will collectively own 45% of the new company, while Bytedance retains 19.9%. Existing Bytedance investors will hold 30.1%. the timeline you gave, will you extend that? We will. I think, look, we have a lot of interest in Tik Tok. Uh, and I China is going to play a role, right? So, hopefully, China will approve of the deal, but they're going to play a role. We have a lot, we have a lot of interest in Tik Tok. The deal mirrors terms disclosed in September when the Trump administration delayed enforcement of a law that would have banned TikTok unless its Chinese owners sold US operations. The joint venture, set to close on 22nd January, is designed to address US national security concerns while allowing Americans to continue using the platform. TikTok said the transaction ensures over 170 million Americans can continue discovering a world of endless possibilities as part of a vital global community. Oracle declined to comment, and the White House referred questions to TikTok. Bytedance had not immediately responded to requests for comment. The data centers are actually under construction, uh the first of them are under construction in Texas. Each building is a half a million square feet. There are 10 buildings currently, yeah, currently being built, but that will expand to 20 and other locations be beyond uh the Abeline location, which is, which is our first location.

title: Major quake in Tokyo area could kill up to 18,000: government estimate
transcription: The Japanese government released on December 19th new damage estimates for a major earthquake that could strike the Tokyo metropolitan area within 30 years with a 70% probability. The calculations assume a worst-case scenario involving a powerful shallow quake directly beneath Tokyo, registering the maximum seismic intensity of seven in the capital, and lower six or above over a wide area. According to the report, the number of fatalities could reach 18,000. Despite progress in earthquake resistance and fire prevention, the government fell short of its goal to halve estimated fatalities from its previous report 12 years ago. The latest figure is just 5,000 lower than the 2013 projection. The estimated economic damage has been set at 83 trillion yen. The report also points out that in Tokyo, in three surrounding prefectures where about 30% of Japan's population lives, there would be limits to administrative response as an extremely large number of people would be affected by the disaster. It recommends that people shelter at home when emergency assistance is not required and notes the need to view disasters as a personal matter and prepare in advance. カメラ撮りはよろしい

title: Get to know Control Center on Apple Vision Pro | Apple Support
transcription: Control Center gives you easy access to the controls you use the most on Apple Vision Pro. We'll show you how to access it and go over some of its unique features. Let's get started. You can access control center anytime. First, look at your hand with your palm facing you. Now turn your hand over so your palm is facing away from you. A status bar appears where you can check your battery level and time at a glance. Tap the status bar to open Control Center. On the left side, you'll find familiar controls like Wi-Fi, volume, and now playing. You can tap the appearance button next to your current environment to switch between light and dark appearance. In the upper right corner, you can tap to open notification center, or spotlight. On the right side, you can scroll to access essential controls. For example, Mac virtual display lets you bring your Mac wirelessly into Apple Vision Pro with an expandable ultrawide display. With guest user, you can let someone else try out your Apple Vision Pro while controlling what apps they can use. And travel mode helps you use Apple Vision Pro as a passenger on a plane, train, car, or bus. To exit control center, tap the close button in the upper left corner. You can change your control center options and settings. While looking at the left side of the settings window, scroll down to control center, and tap to select it. Here, you'll find more controls you can access in control center. Just tap the add button next to an item to add it. You can also change how you open control center if you prefer not to use the default gesture. On the left side of the settings window, look at accessibility, and tap to select it. Scroll down to the physical and motor section. Look at interaction and tap to select it. You can use look upwards for control center, which will give you a button to access control center. Tap to turn it on. and a slider appears that you can use to change the position of the button if you'd like. Now, let's close settings and open control center. You can now look up and tap the control center button, which looks like a small arrow at the top of your view. And that's how to access your most used controls anytime in Control Center on Apple Vision Pro.

title: Malvay Hand Massager Review – Is It Legit or a Scam? (Nuvra 3-in-1 Exposed)
transcription: Have you been seeing ads for the Malvi hand massager, also called the Novra 3 in one hand massager, claiming to relieve arthritis pain, carpal tunnel, and wrist strain in minutes? It promises compression, vibration, and heat therapy all in one device. But the real question is, is this product legit or just another overpriced online scam? In this video, I'll break down the biggest red flags, price discrepancies, and what you should know before buying. According to the official website, the Malvi or Novra hand massager claims to improve blood circulation, reduce stiffness and inflammation, relieve arthritis and carpal tunnel pain, help people who work long hours on computers. all using a single device with compression, vibration, and heat. Sounds impressive, but this is where we need to slow down and look closer. The first red flag is aggressive marketing. They push you to buy it for $119, making it feel like a premium medical grade device. But here's the problem. The same hand massager can be found at eBay for around $51.89. Same design, same features, less than half the price. This raises serious questions. Why is the official website charging more than double? Are you paying for quality or just marketing? Another major concern is the medical style claims. Relieving pain from arthritis, carpal tunnel, repetitive strain injuries. These are medical conditions and reliable treatments usually require professional guidance. Yet there are no clinical studies, no FDA approvals mentioned, and no credible medical endorsements. That's a big red flag. Any product claiming to fix multiple unrelated conditions should be questioned. Arthritis, nerve compression and muscle fatigue are very different problems. A single massager helping temporarily relax muscles is possible, but claiming long-term relief for all these conditions, that's unrealistic. When checking review platforms like Trustpilot, independent blogs and forums, there's a lack of verified customer reviews. Most reviews appear only on sales pages or sponsored articles. No detailed long-term user feedback. No verified buyer experiences. That's another warning sign. So is Malvi or Novra hand massager a scam? It's likely a real product but heavily overpriced and overmarketed. You're not paying for advanced technology, you're paying for aggressive advertising and exaggerated promises. If you've already used the Malvi or Novra hand massager, please leave a comment and share your experience to help others. Don't forget to like, subscribe and stay safe from online product scams.

questions.answer: The speaker's main argument is that the product is heavily overpriced and overmarketed. He points out a significant price discrepancy, noting it's sold for $119 on the official website but can be found for around $51.89 on eBay, suggesting customers are paying for aggressive advertising rather than advanced technology.

title: ER visits for heart attacks surged in aftermath of January's LA County wildfires, study shows
transcription: New at 7:00 a.m. an important health study just released on the direct health effects of the LA fires. Some of it might some of it you might expect, but one huge finding is one researchers have never seen before. Circle of Health reporter Denise Dedor with what these new findings mean for all of us who live here. Oh my gosh. When we pulled up, we saw everything was like gone. Hours after evacuating, Claudine Ang and her children went back to see if their Altadena home was still standing. Fire had engulfed the garages and living quarters next to the main house. The family picked up garden hoses to fight the flames. Don't get too close, guys. It was an all-day battle. Just all the excitement of trying to put this fire out that kind of took over and we kind of didn't really think about our safety. Now, new research reveals you don't have to be that close for that long to experience immediate health effects. And we found that visits to the ER for respiratory illness increased by 24% after the wildfire started. And for 90 days after the fires, heart attacks rose 46%. But Dr. Susan Cheng, director of public health research at Cedar Sinai Smidt Heart Institute says, what scientists found next was peculiar and surprising. We've never seen anything like this before. Researchers tracked a 118% spike in patients with abnormal blood work, all needing emergency care. We can see that these are patients who came in with cough, but their chest x-ray was clear. They came in with dizziness, but there weren't signs of dehydration. They came in with chest pain, but they weren't having a heart attack. What did these abnormal lab results mean and what was the link to all these different unexplained symptoms? The January wildfire exposures seem to have led to some kind of a biochemical metabolic stress on the body that likely affected more than just one organ system. The medical center is located 10 miles from the Palisades fire and 20 miles from the Eton fire. But Dr. Cheng says the results she got at Cedar Sinai's ER could probably be replicated at any other ER here in LA County and maybe even as far south as Orange County. So we know that even beyond LA, many, many people were affected. Dr. Chen says most healthy people with this abnormal blood work appear to have recovered, but what are the potential long-term effects, if any? That needs more study. Meantime, especially on poor air quality days, her advice is to wear a mask and take advantage of air filtration. Those are two now tried and true proven strategies for mitigating and minimizing risk. With all these health concerns, it's really scary. Claudine says she wants to return home, but the findings give her mixed feelings. Happy, but worried at the same time. Especially for my kids. In Altadena, Denise De Dor, ABC 7, I Witness News.

title: OpenAI’s CEO Sam Altman Declares CODE RED
transcription: In early December 2025, Open AI CEO Sam Altman declared an internal code red, signaling a state of existential urgency for the company. This move, reminiscent of Google's own panic following the launch of chat GPT in 2022, was triggered by a sudden and significant loss of market momentum. For the first time, Open AI found its dominance directly threatened by the rapid ascent of Google's Gemini 3, which began outperforming chat GPT on critical benchmarks like humanity's last exam, and seeing 30% growth while chat GPT's user base plateau. The code red directive fundamentally shifted Open AI's operational priorities. To reclaim its lead, the company paused long-term experimental projects, including its push into advertising and the development of specialized AI agents for health and shopping to marshall resources toward the core product. Engineers were reallocated to focus on immediate improvements in reliability, speed, and professional utility. The first major outcome of this mobilization was the fast-tracked release of GPT 5.2 on December 11th, 2025. Marketed as a professional work partner, the new model introduced a tiered system, Instant, thinking and Pro, designed to match Gemini 3's reasoning capabilities. Internal data suggests GPT 5.2 reclaimed the top spot in coding and mathematical reasoning, achieving a perfect 100% on the AME 2025 math benchmark. Beyond the product race, the code red reflects a high stakes financial reality. With projected losses nearing $140 billion by 2029 and $1.4 trillion in infrastructure obligations, Open AI cannot afford to lose the smartest model title that fuels its subscription and enterprise revenue. By declaring a code red, Altman has signaled that the era of uncontested dominance is over, forcing Open AI to transition from a pioneering lab into a focused, defensive tech giant fighting for its survival in a saturated market.

questions.question: What event triggered OpenAI to declare an internal "Code Red" in December 2025?
questions.answer: The Code Red was triggered by a sudden loss of market momentum due to the rapid ascent of Google's Gemini 3, which began outperforming ChatGPT on critical benchmarks and was gaining users while ChatGPT's growth plateaued.

title: TRAILER: The Malaria Challenge: a participant’s experience through a malaria ‘challenge’ study
transcription: Hello, my name is Angela Manasian. I lead on the malaria vaccine clinical trials program here in Oxford, in partnership with Professor Simon Draper, our lab and clinical team, and in collaboration with the Oxford Vaccine Group. The purpose of this documentary is to introduce you to the concept of a human malaria challenge study, where we deliberately infect healthy adults with malaria. This is something we've been doing in Oxford for more than 20 years. We do this to answer fundamental questions about the body's response to malaria. We also infect volunteers who have been given an experimental vaccine against malaria in order to give us an early indication of whether the vaccine is likely to work. And ultimately, these sorts of studies should help us to make better vaccines. You will hear from one of the doctors who runs our studies, Dr. Jennifer Van Heerden. You will also hear from one of our study volunteers who was deliberately infected with malaria, and she will give you a sense of her personal journey through our study. Going forward, we hope that our vaccines will build on the success of the current licensed vaccines, and the results from our human challenge studies will play an important part in this process. So don't just take my word for it. Listen and watch carefully and then make up your own mind as to whether human challenge studies are important for malaria.

title: Mexico City Legislature: Physical Clash Erupts Between Lawmakers
transcription: Tensions boiled over in a Mexico City Congress on Monday, leading to a physical confrontation between lawmakers from opposing political parties. This incident, which unfolded during a live television broadcast, involved members of the right-wing National Action Party, PAN, and the ruling leftist Morena party. The spark? A heated debate over proposed reforms to the city government's transparency oversight agency. According to reports, the PAN legislators, who are in the minority, approached the main podium to protest what they saw as a violation of legislative rules by Morena, which holds the majority. Video footage captured the chaotic scene, showing lawmakers shouting, shoving, and even pulling hair. The opposition party's goal was to physically block voting on the budget. But here's where it gets controversial. The PAN representatives accused the ruling party of using force to silence dissent, claiming they had taken the podium peacefully. On the other hand, Morena representatives rejected accusations of wrongdoing, arguing that the opposition had disrupted proceedings. And this is the part most people miss. The incident highlights a deeper issue, the increasingly polarized political climate. The PAN and Morena parties have very different views on how the city should be run, and this clash shows how those differences can sometimes lead to physical altercations. Following the incident, the PAN lawmakers exited the chamber, allowing Morena legislators and their allies to continue the debate. What do you think? Was the opposition justified in their actions, or did they overstep their boundaries? Did the ruling party overreact, or were they simply trying to maintain order? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Cambodians in South Korea Protest Thai Military Strikes
transcription: More than 2,000 Cambodians in South Korea staged coordinated protests Saturday, denouncing what they call Thailand's brutal military aggression against Cambodia and demanding an immediate halt to hostilities. Demonstrations took place in Seoul and Gwangju, where protesters carried banners and chanted slogans, urging Thai forces to respect international law and abide by the Cambodia-Thailand ceasefire signed in Kuala Lumpur. In Seoul, more than 300 demonstrators marched near the Thai embassy and submitted a petition calling for an end to the violence. In Gwangju, over 2,000 Cambodians gathered in one of the largest overseas rallies since the latest escalation of border clashes. Organizers pressed Thailand to comply with humanitarian law and honor the peace agreement witnessed by US President Donald Trump and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, ASEAN current chair. The rallies followed earliest demonstrations on December 13th across several South Korea cities, reflecting growing concern among overseas Cambodians communities over the conflict's humanitarian toll.

title: Take Off startup summit gathers global investors to Istanbul

title: First-Ever Footage: Killer Whales and Dolphins Hunt Together | Dalhousie University
transcription: So what we discovered was that uh two species, the resident killer whales and Pacific white-sided dolphins seem to be cooperatively foraging on uh salmon, and most likely adult chinook salmon off the coast of BC. So we think this is important for a couple of reasons. The first is that interspecies interactions are commonly observed um around the world. So we see whales and dolphins or different species of whales that interact with one another. But understanding the actual mechanism or the reason why we're seeing both species interacting has largely been speculative. And that's because a lot of the behaviors that are occurring are underwater and we just can't see what's going on. But then once we put the suction cup tags on the whales that had cameras and acoustic recorders, then we could actually see that not only were the killer whales following dolphins at the surface, but they would follow them to depth, down to around 60 m, where it would become really dark and we could just see the silhouettes of the dolphins at the head of the whale. And so what this told us was that the whales are, you know, working together to target uh large salmon for the killer whales to capture. It's important because if there's maybe another mechanism or a way to help facilitate um the resident killer whales to find their food, then that might be advantageous for the population. But we need to collect more data to try to figure out like, is this really prevalent? Like, how often are resident killer whales cooperatively foraging with Pacific white-sided dolphins? And that's something that we've yet to determine. To see that things were perhaps a bit more complex than we initially understood is is always exciting because like we just, you know, you scratch the surface with a lot of the research that you do, and then every now and then you get kind of lucky and something unexpected happens. And so this is one of those kind of lucky things.

title: Japan alerts citizens about possible megaquake

ああ、滑りやすいから気をつけてくださいね。 はい、はい。
Japan's government is assessing the extent of damage after this 7.5 magnitude earthquake struck North Japan earlier this week. The event was followed by multiple aftershocks and led officials to issue a warning of a possible megaquake to come in the area. Officials stress there's only about a 1% chance of a megaquake and the warning is just to encourage preparedness, but since there's a lot of chatter and misinformation online right now since that warning was issued, we want to clear things up. What is a megaquake and why is Japan at risk? Well, the friction from tectonic plates shifting against one another releases energy through the Earth's crust. We feel that as the ground shakes. That energy can also displace large amounts of ocean water that create tsunamis. Japan is surrounded by four tectonic plates, which make it vulnerable to earthquakes in general. The country experiences an average of 1500 a year, according to the University of Tokyo, but most of those quakes are very minor. Now, a megaquake has a magnitude of 8.0 or higher, which is 10 times stronger than a magnitude 7.0 quake. The 2011 quake that hit northern Japan was a 9.1, which along with its accompanying tsunami resulted in more than 19,000 deaths. If a megaquake happened in the area impacted by this week's earthquake, up to, you see the number right here, almost 200,000 lives could be lost and economic damage could reach almost 200 billion dollars according to government analysis. It could also cause a tsunami with a wave up to 98 ft tall. Now, it's important to stress that officials aren't saying a megaquake is imminent, but they are issuing this guidance as a warning of its possibility.

The process combined on location filmmaking using high resolution 360 degree cameras and custom XR development to deliver a cohesive, immersive experience. Unlike traditional virtual tours viewed on a browser or mobile phone, this experience was built for VR first, not adapted from a 2D workflow. It takes full advantage of immersive technologies that are impossible to replicate on flat screens, including hand tracking for natural interaction, stereoscopic visuals for depth and presence, and spatial audio that grounds users in the environment. The Innisfree Garden Tour demonstrates that when immersive tourism is approached as a true XR experience, rather than a passive viewing tool, it becomes more accessible, more engaging, and more memorable for users. title: Jamie Carragher Slams Mohamed Salah: “A Disgrace” | Liverpool Drama Explained । USA TODAY NEWS
transcription: Jamie Carragher has finally broken his silence on the Mohamed Salah saga, calling the star's recent actions a disgrace. The Egyptian forward has sent shockwaves through Liverpool after claiming he's been thrown under the bus by the club. Salah has been left on the bench for the last three matches and didn't play a single minute in two of them, prompting questions about his future at Anfield. Following the 3-3 draw with Leeds, Salah claimed he had no relationship with manager Arne Slot and suggested that the weekend clash with Brighton could be his last for the club. Liverpool responded by leaving him out of the traveling squad for their upcoming Champions League fixture against Inter Milan, signaling a serious rift between player and club. Carragher, speaking on Sky Sports Monday Night Football, didn't hold back. He said Salah's post- Leeds comments were not just an emotional outburst, but a calculated move by him and his agent to maximize pressure on the club. Carragher reminded viewers that Salah had done something similar a year ago, playing on fans' emotions when Liverpool were top of the league. He suggested that now, after a poor result, Salah is once again trying to manipulate the narrative to his advantage, potentially undermining both the manager and the team. One line stood out to Carragher, thrown under the bus. He emphasized that Salah has twice in 12 months tried to throw the club under the bus, going after owners who have paid him handsomely for years and targeting the manager during a rough patch. Carragher argued that a player of Salah's caliber should be helping Liverpool in one of their worst runs of form since the 1950s, rather than creating off-field drama. The interview even went viral for a humorous moment when Carragher asked if he had ever criticized Salah on the pitch, only to be reminded by co-host David Jones that he had recently commented on Salah's legs. Fans reacted instantly, some laughing at Carragher being caught off guard, while others praised Jones' quick wit. Salah's action seem to have backfired. Instead of rallying the team, his comments risk alienating both fans and teammates. Liverpool are facing a critical stretch of games, and now more than ever, they need unity from their stars. Salah is undeniably a Liverpool legend, but when influence turns toxic, the club may have to consider moving on to protect team morale and results. The saga serves as a stark reminder that even the greatest players must prioritize the team over individual grievances if they hope to achieve lasting success.

title: Ice hockey explained | A battle of warriors on ice 🏒
transcription: Fast action at breathtaking pace. Step into the world of ice hockey. Skaters are like warriors. They wear helmets, pads, and gloves for protection. Goalies, even more. They wear a mask, thicker pads, and extra body protection to absorb hard shots. Two teams play five skaters aside, which includes three forwards and two defensemen, fighting to put the puck past the opposing goaltender. The ice is divided into three zones, each with its own purpose. In the defensive zone, protect the net and prevent goals. You move through the neutral zone with quick passes and fast skating. Then fly into the attacking zone with the net as the target, setting up plays and taking hard shots to increase scoring chances. Break the rules and you go to the penalty box, usually for two minutes, sometimes four or even five. The team with a power play has more players on ice, using special strategies to create scoring chances. Games consist of three 20-minute periods. If scores are tied, an overtime period is played. Here, the first team to score wins. If no team scores, a shootout will decide the winner. Only in the gold medal game, teams play three on three overtime until a goal is scored. The immersive experience gives attendees a rare insight look at how Tesla's AI systems, including Autopilot and the Optimus robot, interpret the world in real time. At the center of the showcase is Tesla Vision, Tesla's camera-based system that powers its cars and robots. Using millions of hours of real-world driving footage, the system learns to identify traffic patterns, pedestrians, and road signs without relying on radar or lidar. This same AI is now being used in Optimus, Tesla's humanoid robot, which has recently learned how to run and handle objects independently. The exhibit simulates what Tesla's AI sees, offering a window into both the company's approach to full vehicle autonomy and advancements in robotics. RSVPs are now open but space is limited and Tesla notes entry isn't guaranteed, likely due to high demand for the behind-the-scenes look into its evolving tech. You are listening to you on news.

title: Adidas Men's Daily 4.0 Skate Shoes - Full Review
transcription: Let's take a look at these Adidas men's daily shoes and these are nothing fancy, just the way I like. They just look like a basic skate sneaker with a flat bottom and a wide rubber outsole. They come in a few color choices and these are the black, white, gum option. Even though they're really gray, not black. But they're not quite as basic on the inside as they appear at first. I've owned Vans and Converse Chuck Taylor All Stars and other similar shoes, so I'm definitely familiar with flat, unyielding slabs of rubber with a reinforced toe that's covered on top with a single layer of structure-free canvas. And these kind of look like that at first, but they're really not. They're actually super comfortable with a thick padded insole and the sides and top aren't just a single layer of canvas. They have some cushiness that feels really nice and padded. I'm recording this in the winter time, so I appreciate the fact that they actually have some insulation under my feet keeping the cold away from the ground below and around the sides and top from the air. The back heel area has an insert that keeps the structure upright and it won't fold like a lot of shoes in this category. And the canvas isn't as basic as you'd think. It feels like it has some kind of coating that provides some rigidity, and it makes them perhaps a little tougher and slightly less vulnerable to getting wet or dirty, but they're definitely not waterproof. Let's put these alongside a pair of Vans. Both are the same size 10 and a half. You can see the Adidas are just a little longer, but you don't really feel it much when you're wearing them because I think most of that length is coming from the padding in the back behind your Achilles and behind the heel. So it pushes your foot forward just a little more than the vans, which have nearly no padding at all in the back. And I'll also mention that they're a little bit wider and honestly, they're a lot more comfortable. But overall, these have been really surprising to me for how good they feel on my feet. And of course, I really like the way they look and I hope this short video has helped you decide whether to buy a pair of these Adidas men's daily shoes, and thanks for watching.

title: Pressure mounts on Indonesia to declare a national disaster after floods • FRANCE 24 English
transcription: Those displaced by floods are still fighting for their survival. Here in Western Sumatra, these rice farmers just escaped rising waters and deadly conditions as they were about to be swallowed up. Now they decry a lack of aid. To repair this house, to fix this road, that road, the river crossing, we're just left hanging if there's no assistance. We can't pass through, so where are we supposed to go? The torrential rains that fell on Sumatra cut access to many roads, complicating relief efforts. Several days after the start of the crisis, some isolated areas are now getting low on food and drinking water. The relief efforts are inadequate and the regency was not capable of handling this flood and landslide disaster alone. Though more than 1 million people have been displaced, the Indonesian government has so far ignored calls for a state of national disaster to be declared. Those demanding it say the measure would free up resources and improve the coordination of aid. Meanwhile, the government insists that crisis management is done by the provinces and that the 30 million US dollars in emergency funds should be enough, while also promising additional funding if needed. Indonesia has only declared a state of national disaster three times. First, during the 1992 earthquake, then in 2004 when a tsunami killed over 160,000 people, and finally during the COVID-19 pandemic. Some analysts are saying that the government is refusing to do so again to avoid any perception that it can't handle the crisis.

title: Luge explained | The fastest sport at the Winter Olympics  ✈️
transcription: Feet first, no brakes. Racing over 150 km an hour down the ice track. Step into the world of Luge, the fastest sport in the Winter Olympics. The way we push ourselves at the start can determine the race. We rock back and forth to accelerate forward. Then, paddle with spiked gloves to gain extra speed. From here on, we lie on our backs, feet stretched in an aerodynamic position to reduce drag. We steer with gentle pressure from our legs and shoulders. Steer too hard and we can lose speed. Steer too late, we can lose the line. When done right, we look still, even under 6Gs of pressure. There are five events at the Winter Olympic games. In men's and women's singles, it's one athlete, four runs, and the fastest total time wins. In men's and women's doubles, two athletes ride stacked with the heavier on top. We get two runs, and the team with the fastest total time wins. Team relays combine women's singles, men's doubles, men's singles, and women's doubles in one race, and in this order. Once we complete our leg of the race, we slap a pad at the bottom, triggering the gate to open for our teammates until all four sleds cross the finish line. We train for years to make the sport look effortless. See how fast we go at the Olympic Winter Games Milano Cortina 2026.

title: Robots dance, clean and rescue toy cats at expo in Japan | REUTERS
transcription: From demonstrating its rescue capabilities during disasters to busting a move and serving up drinks. The latest advances in humanoid robot technology are on full display at this year's International Robot Exhibition in Tokyo. The Kaleido 9 is using this toy cat to showcase how it could save people during a disaster. Yoshimoto Matsuda, managing executive officer of Kawasaki Heavy Industries, said the robot is meant to be deployed to disaster areas where access for humans is difficult. We aim to create robots that are robust and reliable for deployment in places where humans cannot work or where they need to work alongside robots. That's why we insist on human-sized robots, so existing equipment like fireproof suits and protective gear can be used without modification. Our vision is not about robots performing repetitive tasks in factories or improving precision, but about working on site, improvising, and using the same tools as humans. Kawasaki spent about a decade developing the robot, which is still in the testing phase. The bot showed off how it can be a lifesaver in other ways, including performing domestic duties like raking up leaves and throwing out the trash. Across the exhibition hall, a dance-off is taking place. This robot was manufactured by Chinese robotics developer Unitree, but programmed and calibrated by Japanese robotics company GMO. Tomohiro Uchida of GMO said the dance moves show just how far robotic development has come. About a year ago, humanoid robots were still very stiff and jerky. People couldn't imagine them functioning in real-world settings. But in the past six months, or even the last three months, the software has been rapidly updated. And now they can perform a variety of movements. So we wanted visitors to see what kind of movements are possible now. As part of that demonstration, we had it perform a dance. It appears to move quite fluidly now. Uchida added that he sees humanoid robots as a solution to help fill gaps in what he called a declining labor force in developed countries.

title: Why the Internet is MAD at the Sony a7 V
uploader: The VONG Opinion with Jason Vong
transcription: And for those of you with a full-time job and not perpetually online, the internet has been screaming how Canon, Nikon, Panasonic, Fujifilm and hell, even Apple is winning because they're allowing users to shoot in open gate, which means the camera is recording the entire sensor, usually a square or close to square format. So there will be enough room for us to use the footage in either horizontal or vertical orientation. Perfect for pros who have to deliver in both because advertising on phone screens have been increasingly popular and open gate saves us from doing double the work, shooting horizontally, then vertically, or doing that awkward vertical crop from a horizontal footage. God, this vertical crop is just too close. Bleh! I hate it. What's even worse is Canon and Nikon are starting to equip their mid-range cameras, the R6 Mark III and the ZR to shoot raw videos, which means users can change the ISO and white balance cleanly in the edit. Arguably very handy. But is it necessary? Now, Sony is choosing to have their gates closed, and I've expected that. No way the A7 Mark 5 would get open gate or even raw video for that matter. At least not before the next A7S or the next FX camera. You know what I mean? Keep in mind, this is a mid-range camera. It's not meant to have the newest cutting-edge features until its bigger brothers do. And raw video is nice, but what's not nice is the insane file size that comes with it. In order for us to manipulate the ISO and white balance in post cleanly, requires a lot of data. The new Canon R6 Mark II requires approximately 10 gigabytes per minute for a 7K 30p raw video. So if you want to shoot an hour's worth of footage, you're going to need a little more than 600 gigabytes of memory. Yikes. For the pros of pros, you guys might not mind it, but most people wouldn't need this much power, nor even have the resources to handle this much power. Would it have been nice to have? Absolutely. But Sony decided to hold back. They'll do it someday once they're pressured enough to do so, but for now, the A7 Mark 5 does not and will not have any form of open gate raw. Perhaps the A7 Mark 6, likely in 2028.

title: Thousands protest in Bulgaria ahead of final parliamentary vote on controversial new budget plan
transcription: A controversial new budget draft was withdrawn on Thursday morning after thousands of protesters took to the streets of Sofia to oppose it the night before. The government had proposed to increase social security contributions and double dividend taxes in an ambitious new budget, which would have set a new spending record at around 46% of GDP, as well as dramatically increased public debt. Wednesday evening's rally was organized by the opposition coalition and is estimated to have drawn around 20,000 people. Protesters gathered outside the National Assembly building, where lawmakers convened to examine the proposed budget. They formed a massive human chain around the parliament building in an effort to block all exits and prevent MPs from leaving the premises. Police say the protests, which were declared as peaceful, quickly escalated and turned violent, announcing that three police officers were injured. Authorities say some protesters threw firecrackers and glass bottles at deployed officers and attempted to overturn a police van. The protest came ahead of a final parliamentary vote to gain approval and just a few weeks before the Balkan nation is set to enter the Eurozone.

title: Fighting for Freedom in Hungary: András’ story

For many years, every day, me and my colleagues woke up and did our job with the threat of being arrested and charged with a criminal offense. Smear campaigns, attacks on the street, intimidation, all were the result of orchestrated propaganda by the government. As an openly gay person, I am banned from speaking at any public assembly, at any demonstration, regardless of what I'm going to talk about. One legislation that really hurt my feelings was the legislation that said that LGBT people might be a threat to the healthy upbringing of children. Today, as a gay person, not even as a single parent, could I adopt a child, which is, um, not just outrageous, it is extremely humiliating. What happened to us over the past 15 years, did not only happen to us, it also happened to all of you in Europe. It all started when those in power single out usually the most vulnerable groups in society and try to portray them as the enemy within. That should be the first sign that you need to watch for. I want to live in a country where you can have frank, decent conversations, even disagreements without taking a huge risk. Now is the time to actually act and to show that destroying democracy and undermining human rights have clear consequences in the European Union.
