title: Viral “Humanoid Robot” Moment at Iran Tech Expo — What Really Happened?
transcription: 2025 is packed with incredible humanoid robots. But this viral clip from Iran's Kish Invex tech exhibition proves that not everything that looks robotic is actually advanced. The video starts off looking legit, bright expo lights, a cybersecurity booth, and two humanoid robots, dressed in white suits covered with binary code. They wave, pose, greet visitors, and move in stiff, mechanical ways, just convincing enough to make people wonder if they're looking at a new AI demo. But something feels off. The robots blink too much. Their movements are more cosplay than engineering. And those giant purple sunglasses, a bit too stylish for a supposed next-gen android. Still, the crowd plays along. People ask questions, shake hands, take photos. The performers stay in character, talking in monotone voices. Hello, how are you? Can you move like us? What kind of work can we do for you? And then, the moment that broke the internet. The male robot turns revealing a white plastic shopping bag hanging from his shoulder. A normal, everyday bag on an advanced humanoid machine. Instant laughter. Someone shouts, I thought it was a robot. There's a man inside. And just like that, the illusion collapses. It wasn't a breakthrough robot. It wasn't a secret prototype. It was just two dedicated performers promoting a booth, until one simple prop exposed everything. And the funniest part? This clip spread faster than many real robotics announcements. Because in a world filled with hype, sometimes the internet just loves a good not-a-robot moment. This is Robo Frontier, where we cover the real breakthroughs and the hilarious ones too.

title: STOP! Don’t Buy the Redrie HK33 Drone Before Watching This!
transcription: Hey everyone, welcome back to Brutal Reviews. Today we're checking out the Redry HK 33 drone, you know, the one listed as GPS drone with 4K camera under 249G, 45 minutes flight, brushless motor. Yeah, all the usual buzz words. 18% of buyers basically said, nope, trash. So, let's talk about why. Issue number one, the 4K camera is not 4K up. Let's start with the classic. Users say the footage looks more like 720p upscaled than actual 4k. soft image, shaky video, and colors that look like they were shot on a budget phone from 2013. title: HEETCH - CHOOSE UBER (Case Study) | Campaign
transcription: Each is a local ride-hailing app in Paris. Kind of like Uber. What sets us apart? We go way beyond, serving places Uber usually won't go. And this summer, with 15 million tourists coming for the Olympics and the stadiums all around, it was the perfect opportunity for us to make a lot of money. So, a crazy choice we had to make. Shifting our focus on tourists for short-term profit, or keep helping the locals. In other words, choosing between profit and loyalty. And choose we did. Each presents, choose Uber. We literally decided to advertise our biggest competitor. And send tourists directly, excessively, and deliberately to Uber. So we could stay available at all times for our regular local clients. Just for the two weeks of the Olympics. Everywhere in Paris, in 12 languages, with a QR code leading to the Uber app. To take the madness even further, we invited influencers to amplify the message. Choose Uber. Choose Uber. And Parisians gave the love back by making their own videos. Choose Uber. The results? A ridiculous 3% jump in short-term foreign clients during the 15 days of the Olympics. But a massive 37% jump for French clients during the same period. Our best July, August and September sales months for the past nine years. They stood out against Uber, the global giant, creating a sort of David and Goliath moment. And our biggest shift ever versus Uber in terms of brand preference. By choosing loyalty over money, we gave locals a perfect and long-term reason to choose Each.

title: The Bonelli’s Eagle filmed & photographed from a hide in Extramadura
transcription: The Bonelli's eagle in the wild landscapes of Extremadura, Spain. This impressive raptor is one of Europe's most iconic and most elusive birds of prey. The Bonelli's eagle is known for its powerful build, striking plumage, and remarkable agility in flight. With its pale underparts, bold dark patches on the wings, and intense gaze, it is unmistakable once seen up close. This species typically prefers rugged terrain, rocky hillsides, cliffs, Mediterranean forests, and open plains where it hunts with extraordinary precision. Its main prey includes rabbits, partridges, pigeons, and sometimes even other birds of prey. Bonelli's eagles are territorial and often form long-term pairs, returning to the same nesting sites year after year. Although once widespread, the species has declined in many parts of Europe due to habitat loss, disturbance, and reduced prey availability. Spain, and especially regions like Extremadura, now hosts some of the most important remaining populations. Conservation efforts in recent years have helped stabilize numbers, but the Bonelli's eagle remains a near-threatened species, deserving continued protection. Capturing this magnificent bird in its natural habitat is always special. I hope you enjoy these moments as much as I did while filming them.

questions.answer: Its main prey includes rabbits, partridges, pigeons, and occasionally other birds of prey.

questions.answer: The Bonelli's Eagle is classified as a "near threatened" species. Its population has declined due to habitat loss, disturbance, and a reduction in the availability of its prey.

title: GUNS N' ROSES Announces 2026 World Tour; Two New Songs to Arrive in Early December
transcription: In the latest rock metal news, after a sprawling 2025 world tour that saw Guns and Roses return to Europe, the Middle East, Asia and Latin America, the powerhouse rock icons have announced they will hit the road again in the spring and summer 2026. This 2026 tour will see Guns and Roses visit Mexico and Brazil before headlining additional European markets as well as stadiums across the US and Canada. The upcoming run includes a special performance at Los Angeles's Rose Bowl, marking a historic return to the venue for the first time in over 30 years. In conjunction with the Nighttrain fan club presale, Guns and Roses will release two new songs, Nothing and Atlas via Geffen Records on Tuesday, December 2nd, marking their first releases since 2023. These new songs join The General and Perhaps as vital additions to setlists, otherwise featuring all the classic hits and deep cut fan favorites from GNR's early catalog. 2026 tour dates will kick off on March 28th in Monterrey, Mexico, Tecate Pal Norte, and will conclude on September 19th in Atlanta, Georgia at Truist Park. title: G20 Summit 2025: Critical Minerals for Global Economic Growth and Resilience
transcription: The Global South's mineral wealth, a game changer for economic growth, but at what cost? The G20's 2025 Summit in Johannesburg, South Africa has ignited a crucial conversation about the role of critical minerals in shaping our future. But here's where it gets controversial. Can these resources truly drive inclusive growth and resilience, or will they perpetuate existing inequalities? In a bold move, the G20 has unveiled its critical minerals framework, aiming to transform these essential resources into catalysts for sustainable development. The plan? To empower mineral rich nations, particularly in the Global South, to move beyond simply exporting raw materials. And this is the part most people miss. The framework seeks to address the systemic challenges these countries face, from underinvestment and limited technology to socio-economic and environmental hurdles. As the world undergoes rapid economic transformations, think sustainable energy transitions, digitalization, and industrial innovation, the demand for critical minerals is skyrocketing. However, the G20 declaration highlights a stark reality. Many producer countries, especially developing nations, are struggling to capitalize on this opportunity. The framework offers a voluntary, non-binding road map to foster sustainable, transparent, and resilient mineral value chains. This includes boosting investment in exploration, promoting local processing, beneficiation, and strengthening governance for responsible mining practices. Here's the catch. While the framework promises to preserve the sovereign rights of mineral rich countries, it also raises questions about equitable benefit sharing and environmental stewardship. Will local communities truly reap the rewards or will multinational corporations dominate the landscape. The G20 encourages collaboration among governments, private sectors, investors, and local communities, but how will this play out in practice? Prime Minister Narendra Modi emphasized the importance of international cooperation in addressing global challenges from climate change to food systems. India's commitment to a human-centric, sustainable, and inclusive future aligns with the G20's vision. But as the summit concludes, one question lingers, can critical minerals truly become a force for broad-based development, or will they remain a source of raw material exports leaving the global south behind? What's your take? Do you believe the G20's critical minerals framework can deliver on its promises, or are there inherent flaws in the approach? Share your thoughts in the comments. Let's spark a conversation that could shape the future of global resource management.

title: Ramaphosa closes G20 Summit, passes presidency to US for 2026 - nbc
transcription: As the G20 summit drew to a close at Nazrec, global attention shifted from the formalities of leadership transition to an unexpected diplomatic snag, one that became clear even before the ceremonial gavel could change hands. The handover of the gavel has yet to occur after President Ramaphosa's government declined to present it to the US Chargé d'Affaires in Pretoria, Mark Dillard. Ramaphosa made no mention of President Donald Trump or the recent tensions between Washington and Pretoria as he concluded the 2025 summit. Instead, he called for unity, adding that the G20 must demonstrate to the world that it has the capacity to confront and overcome global challenges. And together, we can ensure that no one is left behind. I now say that this gavel, this gavel of this G20 summit, formally closes this summit and now moves on to the next President of the G20, which is the United States, where we shall see each other again. The Trump administration has not publicly commented on the G20 leaders summit since Saturday. The newly adopted G20 declaration also reaffirms that members will cooperate under the US presidency in 2026 and reconvene in the UK in 2027 and Korea in 2028. Blanche Corses, NBC News, Johannesburg, South Africa.

title: WATCH | Macron reflects on historic G20 summit, climate change, and Sudan
transcription: You should not underestimate the impact and the importance of having the first G20 summit in our history on the African continent. And by itself, it's a great achievement. And uh, and I think South Africa can be proud of this achievement. Second, this is as well a summit uh where African Union has a seat, which is very important achievement as well in the recognition of Africa as a whole and Africa as being part of of uh of these nations to decide for themselves and for the future. Second, the main topic of the G20 is much more about uh climate, economy, and uh and trying to regulate and find the a common tools for our economies and not um the vivid and geopolitical crisis. It's never been the core of our agenda even if in side events we can we can meet on that. Uh this G20 consolidated some of of very important points decided during the past few years, especially on debt restructuring, which was an important part of the discussion this morning, and this is very important in real terms for the African countries because a lot of them, too many of them are overwhelmed by the debt service and have to sacrifice health, education because of that. So, delivering a common restructuring is critical and G20 is the right framework. Why? Because you have China, Europeans, all the key creditors around the table. Now, as for the crisis, let me tell you that Sudan is not forgotten by France. We organized several conferences in support of Sudan and trying to find a way to give to the civil society its fair place and to push and re-engage with the different parties to ceasefire. Now, the the main objective in Sudan, and I think all those involved in the in in them, in this conflict have to follow the same line, is clearly ceasefire, resuming the humanitarian health and setting as we did in 2019, a peace where civil society could take its its place and its role. And I I you know, I do remember the civil society being in Paris in 2019 right after the Sudanese Revolution. And and this young woman were so impressive, so powerful. and we owe them so much. title: 1814 - The London Beer Flood -  How a Brewery Flooded an Entire Neighborhood!
transcription: On the 17th of October 1814, a strange and destructive event took place at the Moe and Co. S Horseshoe brewery, located at the junction of Tottenham Court Road and Oxford Street in London, England. The brewery contained several enormous wooden vats, some of them 22 feet tall, filled with porter, a dark London beer that was extremely popular during that period. On that day, the hoop of one of the huge vats suddenly broke, causing the vat to burst and release its contents. The force of the escaping beer ruptured the stopcock of a second large vat, which also began to discharge. Several other vats were damaged in the chain reaction. In total, between 580,000 and 1,470,000 liters of porter flooded out, smashing through the brewery's rear wall, which was 25 ft high. Behind the brewery stood the St. Giles's rookery, one of London's poorest and most crowded slum districts. Once the wall collapsed, a wave of porter about 15 ft high swept into New Street and Great Russell Street, destroying homes and flooding basements. Everyone inside the brewery survived, but according to the coroner's report, eight people in the surrounding neighborhood were killed either by drowning, injuries from collapsing walls, or being trapped in flooded rooms. Eyewitnesses described the area afterwards as looking like the aftermath of an earthquake. Rumors later spread of people collecting the spilled beer, widespread drunkenness, and even deaths from alcohol poisoning in the following days. However, these stories appear exaggerated. The corner ruled that the disaster was an act of God, meaning the brewery was not held legally responsible and paid no compensation. The incident contributed to the decline of large wooden fermentation vats, which were eventually phased out across the brewing industry. The horseshoe brewery was later demolished. Today, the Dominion theater stands on the former site of the brewery. Thank you for watching. Please feel free to like, comment, subscribe, and tap the notification bell for more quick, informative content.

title: The largest polar bear ever
transcription: Have you ever wondered just how big can a polar bear really get? Today, we're diving into the story of the largest polar bear ever recorded, a true giant that shattered records and left scientists stunned. Let's rewind to 1960 in the icy region of Kotzebue Sound, Alaska. A group of hunters came across a truly enormous male polar bear and what they found would go down in history. This bear wasn't just large, it was colossal. When officially measured, the bear stood 11 ft 1 in 3.4 m tall when upright and weighed an unbelievable 2,209 lb. That's over 1 ton of arctic muscle and fur. To put that in perspective, that's heavier than a Toyota Corolla and taller than a basketball hoop when standing on its hind legs. Most adult male polar bears weigh between 900 and 1,500 lbs. So this monster of the North was far beyond the normal range. Scientists estimate it was likely in its prime and had access to an exceptional hunting territory, probably feeding on plenty of seals and possibly even beluga carcasses. Its skull alone was record-breaking, measuring 16.25 inches long and 11.75 inches wide, making it one of the largest carnivore skulls ever documented. The bear was later taxidermied and displayed. It serves as a powerful reminder of the extremes nature can produce and of the polar bear's status as one of Earth's ultimate apex predators. But here's the twist, as climate change continues to shrink arctic ice and reduce hunting grounds, polar bears are getting smaller on average. Experts warn that giants like the 1960 bear may never be seen again. What do you think? Could another bear like that still exist out there, hidden in the Arctic's endless white? Hit that like button, subscribe, and drop your thoughts in the comments below.

title: G20 summit opens in South Africa without Trump, Ukraine takes centre stage
transcription: Well, this G20 summit is unique for a few reasons. First of all, it's the first time in the 26-year history of G20s that leaders are meeting on this continent, the first time in Africa. It's also unique because it's the first G20 where the leaders of the three biggest economies are not present. No Russia, of course, no China, and the United States President Donald Trump, he's not here. He's boycotting this summit because he believes a genocide is being perpetrated against the white farmers of South Africa. He's wrong, that's a false claim, but that's uh that's Trump's belief. And yet, even though Trump is absent, he's really dominated the first few hours of the summit because of this peace plan that he wants to force on Ukraine. That peace plan was leaked yesterday, 28 points in it, and Trump has said that unless Zelensky, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky accepts this peace plan by Thursday, the US may be looking at withdrawing military aid. For Zelensky, he says this is the most serious moment in Ukrainian history. Uh the peace plan would call for Ukraine to give up large chunks of the eastern part of its country to Russia. It would call on the Ukraine military to be weakened, and it would call on Ukraine to swear off uh joining NATO. Those are all non-starters for Ukraine. They're also non-starters for many of Ukraine's allies, Canada included. And so, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney is stepping away from the summit activity to meet with European Council President Antonio Costa, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, French President Emmanuel Macron, and UK Prime Minister Keir Starmer. They'll all be stepping away to talk about how they can support Zelensky through this week ahead, what to do if in fact the US decides to pull military aid. Uh the Ukraine and the war uh war there has forced its way onto a summit which ostensibly was going to be about development, the Global South, uh new trade ties, etc. There will be that talk, but again, Ukraine has forced its way onto the agenda of this G20 summit. David Aken, Global News, Johannesburg.

You know, it's been done a few times before but not on the scale we're doing it. The name actually spawned from the music. You know, we have a, you know, a lot of music and uh, you know, some of it's, I think it's going to fit well with, you know, video games. So we're hoping to kind of, you know, we're here at E3, hoping to kind of land some uh, some tracks on some video games. Just every kind of distributor here in the world. So this is the place to be for that, definitely. Record label sucks, so we started our own. Alchemedia spawned from dealing with record labels that don't want to hear what you have to say, just want to take your demo and throw it in a room with a thousand other demos and it never get heard. title: Fire breaks out at COP30 as conference closes | BBC News
transcription:
That's the final day of the UN's climate change summit, COP 30 in Brazil. Yesterday, the conference had to be evacuated after a fire broke out inside the venue. More than 190 countries have been at the summit in an attempt to strengthen international efforts to address climate change. And on this final day, the delegation from Colombia say that more than 30 countries have signed a letter opposing a draft text because of it fails to refer to the phasing out of fossil fuels. Here's our climate editor, Justin Rowlett. 

The fire is really burning very intensely, burned a huge hole in the roof. The summit was halted yesterday afternoon when a fire broke out in the venue. The intense blaze was swiftly brought under control, but it meant yet another delay in these already fraught talks. They are as much about who isn't here as who is. Secretary General, what message do you want this conference to send to Donald Trump? We are waiting for you. Hope is the last thing that dies. He urged the summit to take bold action. One thing is clear. We are down to the wire and the world is watching Belem. But when the Brazilian President, Lula de Silva flew in, signs of agreement were proving elusive. These talks are being held behind closed doors. The most contentious issues, how to bridge the yawning gap between what countries say they'll do and what the science says is necessary to avoid the worst effects of climate change and how to get rich countries to deliver on promised cash to help poorer countries play their part. The big challenge as always at these talks is that the countries here can't force the others to actually do anything. So if a country doesn't want to phase out fossil fuels rapidly, for example, they don't have to, which means that the outcome of these summits is inevitably always a compromise. And if that compromise isn't ambitious, well, there will be questions about how effective this entire global process is. Justin Rowlett, BBC News, Belem.

title: VisionPro Glasses Review - Legit or Scam Product?
transcription: Yeah, so, Vision Pro Premium glasses claim to be this all-in-one multifocal solution that gives you perfect vision at every distance while being super lightweight and unbreakable. But a lot of people are still wondering, is this product actually legit? Let's break it down and make sure you watch this video till the end to get the full picture. The first concern comes from Trustpilot reviews. When we checked them, the feedback was overwhelmingly negative. People said the glasses were cheap, poorly made, and didn't work even though their eyesight matched the advertised range. Shipping took forever, refunds were a headache, and they were asked for unnecessary photos before getting their money back. Not a great start. Another concern is the buy one get one free offer. Sounds tempting, right? But this kind of aggressive discount is often used by low-quality brands just to push quick sales. Good and trustworthy brands rarely use gimmicks like this, so it definitely raises eyebrows. The third concern is their claim that the glasses are approved by ophthalmologists. But when we checked, nothing. No doctor names, no certificates, no endorsements, zero real proof. If something is medically approved, it always comes with verifiable details, which were missing here. The fourth concern is the promise of perfect near, intermediate, and distance vision. Sounds amazing, but we didn't find any scientific evidence, lab tests, or trials that support this claim. Without real proof, these statements feel more like marketing than reality. The fifth concern is the big statistics they advertise. 91% saw immediate improvement, 94% said the glasses were super durable, 92% felt more comfortable from the first minute. But again, no sources, no studies, nothing. When numbers have no proof behind them, they're basically meaningless. So, is Vision Pro Premium glasses legit? Based on everything we found, they really don't seem reliable. The bad reviews, the missing medical proof, the unrealistic claims, and the pushy discounts all raise major red flags. With so many customers reporting poor quality and refund issues, it's safer to avoid this brand and stick to trusted eyewear companies instead. Thanks for watching till the end. title: Albanese arrives in South Africa for the G20 summit | ABC NEWS
transcription: World leaders are gathering here in Johannesburg for this weekend's G20 leaders summit, the first to be held on African soil. Anthony Albanese touched down earlier, welcomed by an honor guard and traditional dancers. Now, this should be South Africa's big moment to showcase its economic and diplomatic potential, but it's been overshadowed in the lead-up by the boycott of Donald Trump. The US president refusing to attend this weekend's summit over debunked claims that the South African government is violently persecuting white farmers. Up until today, the Trump administration was refusing to send any government officials, but South Africa's president Cyril Ramaphosa has indicated there has been a change of heart and the US now wants to participate in some form. For his part, Anthony Albanese insists this G20 summit is as relevant and important as ever. The G20 is such an important gathering. It's the most important gathering for which Australia is a member. It represents 85% of the global economy, 75% of global trade. It's important for us to engage because one in four of Australia's jobs depends upon trade and it is important therefore that I represent Australia at forums like this, advancing Australia's economic interest and supporting Australian jobs. Before the summit begins, the Prime Minister will honor three prominent Australians for the roles they played in ending apartheid here in South Africa, paying a visit to Freedom Park, where the names of former Prime Ministers Malcolm Fraser, Bob Hawke and former diplomat Bruce Hage have been inscribed on the wall of names, a memorial to those who fought for South Africa's freedom and democracy.

title: Intel Panther Lake: Low-Power, Multi-Tasking Demo
transcription: All right, Joe here at ITT. We're showcasing how we're bringing that Lunar Lake level efficiency with the scaled performance of Arrow Lake to our upcoming Panther Lake product. What you're seeing here are live power readings collected at the system level in this multitasking scenario. We have an active Teams meeting, Excel, PowerPoint, a browser here with 10 tabs open, actively watching a video. I know none of you in the tech world would ever think of doing this, but occasionally it happens. And we're using Hardware Info Pro here to show where that work is being done. On the Lunar Lake system and on the Panther Lake system, you'll see that work being contained to the low power island. But what you'll see here on Panther Lake is you still have all that additional core power that you'd expect from an Arrow Lake class system available. So all this compute cluster, which is not being needed right now for all this work being done, is still available for all your multi-threaded needs. title: John Cena’s Epic RAW Farewell at Madison Square Garden | WWE Recap । USA TODAY NEWS
transcription: Last night at Madison Square Garden, John Cena said goodbye. Not just to the world's most famous arena, but to his time on Monday Night Raw. And while it was bittersweet, it was also flat-out awesome. The show opened with his music hitting, and this time, the crowd actually got it right. No more John Cena sucks chants, just pure, loud, thank you Cena energy. Cena soaked it in, taking a few minutes to revel in the love before starting a heartfelt promo about what it all meant to him. Of course, no Cena farewell would be complete without a little chaos. Dominic Mysterio interrupted, and Judgment Day rallied around him, outnumbering Cena. Naturally, backup arrived in the form of Sheamus and Rey Mysterio, and suddenly, we had a six-man tag team match. At first, I thought it was a bit odd to go six-man instead of a one-on-one moment for Cena's farewell, but by the end, it worked perfectly. It was the kind of feel good story WWE does best. Good guys win, Cena hits every signature move, and you could see him having a blast with the other veterans. The crowd loved every second of it. Raw overall delivered after that. We saw the return of Dolph Ziggler, Roman Reigns and Brock Lesnar joining the men's War Games match in an intense main event brawl segment. AJ Lee made a shocking impact by costing Becky Lynch the women's Intercontinental Championship and Gunther had a standout match with Giovanni Evans. WWE treated Cena's farewell like the special occasion it was, and the entire show felt elevated. Rumors are already swirling that John Cena will headline the 2026 WWE Hall of Fame class, which makes you wonder if he was offered that honor backstage last night. Vince McMahon might not have been the right choice to induct him given his history, but who steps up now? Triple H is likely inducting Stephanie McMahon, so he's probably out. Could it be Randy Orton, CM Punk, or maybe a veteran legend like Kurt Angle or the Undertaker? Whatever happens, it'll be historic. Madison Square Garden provided the perfect backdrop for a proper farewell. Cena's energy, the crowd's love, and the celebration with his peers reminded everyone why he's one of the most iconic performers in WWE history. That night wasn't just about a goodbye, it was a celebration of a career that shaped an entire generation. And while the Hall of Fame speculation adds intrigue, last night was about one thing. Honoring Cena, the man, the performer, the legend. Fans got to witness a truly memorable Raw, and WWE delivered a show that will be talked about for years. Shout out to Netflix for giving us front row access to the magic.

In January 2005, Aniston and Pitt announced their separation with their divorce finalized in October of that year. Pitt and Jolie started dating months later, eventually tying the knot in 2014. They split in 2019 and after a messy divorce, and finalized their split in 2024. Pitt and Jolie share six kids together. Maddox, 24, Pax, 21, Zahara, 20, Shiloh, 19, and twins Knox and Vivian, 17. Aniston, for her part, married Justin Thero in 2015, but the pair called it quits in 2018. She's now dating Curtis, 50, and the couple made their relationship Instagram official in September. title: What’s New in Filmora 15: AI Extend, Dynamic Captions & Source-Timeline Preview

Now you can edit all your generated text clips directly from the text menu. No need to click through each caption one by one. You can also apply templates instantly from the template menu and make further adjustments in the basic settings panel. Like emphasizing active and keywords to make them stand out. With this update, you'll also find a set of new text effects under the animation tab, perfect for giving your captions more emotion and personality. Once you are happy with your dynamic captions, apply them to the rest of your timeline by selecting Apply to all in the bottom right corner. And that's a wrap. title: AMD FINALLY Remembered About This! FSR Redstone

The same way that on the Nvidia side of things, DLSS isn't just one feature. Rather, it includes everything from just regular upscaling to frame generation, to also ray reconstruction. And FSR Redstone will be a pretty similar thing, combining four different technologies. Those being ray regeneration, super resolution, frame generation, and new radiance caching. While some of them FSR already offered, others, like for example, ray regeneration are only just getting started, being introduced in Black Ops 7 as the first official title to actually support it. And the full reveal of what games will actually support this technology will of course come with the big announcement on the 10th of December. But then there's the question of who exactly can even run these things? Well, unfortunately, it's rather exclusive, because only Radeon 9,000 series graphics cards will be able to run FSR Redstone features. So, if you're running anything older or anything from other companies, then you can't experience any of it. Remember the days when FSR just ran flawlessly on any graphics card from any company? I remember that. But of course, as things get more complex and more hardware level features are required, then things can get obviously a bit confusing with what generations of what graphics cards can actually run all of these different upscaling features. title: The Hidden Psychology of Club Penguin Avatars | Club Penguin Zero
transcription: Most worlds end once, but this one has died and returned more times than anyone can count. Every time the snow melts, the servers close, and then somehow someone brings it all back. When we return, we aren't just logging in. We're re-entering a piece of ourselves that we thought we'd outgrown. When we built these penguins, we didn't just pick colors or clothes. We built versions of who we hoped to be. The confident one in red, the quiet one in blue, the dreamer, the explorer, the one who finally fit in. We were shaping identity before we even knew the word for it. There is a psychological theory called the Proteus effect. It says when you change your avatar, your behavior changes with it. Maybe that's why the shy kids led the conga lines here. Maybe that's why the lonely ones hosted parties every night. It was safer to be bold when you were just made of pixels. In here, we could be someone else. And sometimes, that's the truest version of who we are. Every snowball was a conversation, every emote was a way of saying I see you in a language that nobody taught us. Connection didn't need a voice chat, just timing, intention, a small gesture across the screen. We were learning empathy without knowing its name. The dojo was the only place where stillness felt like progress. No coins, no leaderboards, just patience. For once, the goal wasn't just to win, it was to understand a rhythm and yourself. It's 2025, and somehow we are here again. Different people, same avatars. The penguins grew up, but they returned anyway. Maybe because this world never judged us for who we were or who we were trying to become. Every home we built here was a fragment of comfort. We arranged these rooms like we arranged our hearts, cluttered, colorful, and desperately personal. There's something tender about rebuilding a world no one asked you to bring back. Club Penguin Zero isn't about nostalgia. It's about proof that versions of ourselves we once loved still exist somewhere, waiting under the snow. We return to remember. We stay to rebuild. I've been delayed but I will be there around that time.

title: Taipei metro reveals “vault-like” doors installed after 2001 Typhoon Nari | Taiwan News | RTI
transcription: Curious commuters recently noticed a massive vault-like door near Exit 5 of Taipei Metro's Nanjing Fushing Station, sparking online speculation about its purpose. Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation clarified that the heavy, sealed structure is a flood barrier system, a vital defense mechanism designed after the devastating floods caused by Typhoon Nari in 2001. During that storm, floodwaters inundated the Blue Bannan Line and even swamped Taipei Main Station, reaching depths of up to 2.3 m. The disaster led Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation to design and install multiple waterproof systems across the network. If flooding threatens, this watertight door, 30 cm thick, can be closed to prevent water from entering the platform level, said CTS reporter Chang Hsiaoyun, while demonstrating the mechanism on site. According to Huang Yi Chao, a section chief from the Taipei City Department of Rapid Transit systems, the doors were introduced after engineers realized that flooding could easily overwhelm stations entrances. We decided to place basic waterproofing at the entrances and add full seal floodgates at station interfaces, he explained. The Taipei Rapid Transit Corporation uses several types of flood barriers, including swinging, vertical, and sliding models, to block water from penetrating underground areas. Although forecasts predict less rain from this week's Typhoon Fung Wong than from Nari, with expected totals around 300 mm over 2 days, city officials said the metro system remains on high alert to ensure uninterrupted service. Filip Stawski for ICRT News.

title: Running feels easier! Slow runners marathon training
transcription: Hello. It's Monday evening and uh I've just done a 30-minute easy run. Um there was five of us on the run tonight. I wasn't Billy no mates. It was really good. But it's just struck me. Like I would never, I would never normally run two days in a row, let alone a long run on one day followed by another kind of easy run, recovery run, I guess. But I have. I did four miles yesterday, which I really pushed, pushed myself and I got a PB on a segment. And then we've just done two and a half miles, um, so just tweaked it over 30 minutes, um, this evening, like a easy run, a recovery run. And I kept going. I can actually keep going and push myself to keep running a lot further than I would have, if that makes sense. Like, the old me, like training for this year's marathon, if I was starting to feel it, tired or like achy calves or something, I would have said, 'No, I need to walk.' And I would have done like a run-walk, run-walk thinking that I needed the walk. But tonight, I just kept going. So, don't get me wrong, we had, I think there were three, we had three walks up some quite steep, sharp inclines. So they were short walks, but they got us up a sharp incline, rather than running up and getting absolutely knackered and then have to really get your breath back. We walked three of them. Um, so probably no more than about 30 seconds a piece. Um, but I kept going. Like all the other times when I felt like, oh I need a walk, I need a walk, I'm tired, I can't do this. Just kept going and didn't allow myself the opportunity to walk half as much as I would have done like even a few months ago. So I'm very pleased with that. Um it was a good run. Like I said, there were five of us. It started off quite chatty and then, as is normal, kind of the the longer we were running for, um, obviously the chatting died down a bit. But yeah, it was really, really good. I enjoyed that. It was nice company. Um we all had our flashlights on our chests and what have you. Um and we just went and got it done. title: Japan Rebukes Chinese Envoy’s Beheading Threat to PM Takaichi
transcription: A Chinese diplomat in Japan threatened to cut off the head of Japan's Prime Minister. The threat comes after Sanae Takaichi made comments on Taiwan-related issues. The Japanese government strongly protested the diplomat's remarks, calling them extremely inappropriate. The Chinese envoy deleted his terror-like post on X shortly afterward. Former Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe had once warned that a Taiwan emergency is a Japan emergency. Shinzo Abe's remark suggests that a Chinese attack on Taiwan would directly affect Japan's security. The new Prime Minister Takaichi re-emphasized this statement with more clarity on Friday. She said that a Taiwan emergency could pose a threat to Japan's existence, implying that Japan could take military action if China attacks Taiwan. Shre Jen, the Chinese Consul General in Osaka, posted on X on Friday saying, quote, "The filthy head that recklessly sticks itself in must be cut off without a moment's hesitation." On Monday, Japan's Chief cabinet Secretary called the post extremely inappropriate and urged Beijing to take appropriate action. However, the Chinese Foreign Ministry defended the envoy's remarks during his Monday press briefing. Although Shre Jen deleted the terror-like post, he continues posting similar messages on X. These included posts saying, quote, a Taiwan emergency is a Japan emergency. It's a fatal path that some stupid Japanese politicians are trying to take and that dialogue is no longer possible. The US Ambassador to Japan weighed in, saying the Chinese diplomat had threatened Japan's Prime Minister and that Beijing's behavior once again shows misconduct. Prime Minister Takaichi says she has no intention of withdrawing her remarks on Taiwan. A major Chinese offensive against Taiwan would disrupt global supply chains, which rely on the Taiwan straight for 99% of trade, while also strengthening China's military position in the region. Takaichi, who took office last month, is the first Japanese Prime Minister to outline a specific scenario that could justify military intervention.

title: COP30 climate summit starts in Brazil but the U.S. sent no high-level representatives
transcription: All right, the COP 30 climate summit officially opened in Brazil yesterday with the UN urging nations to work together to curb global warming. CBS News foreign correspondent Ramy Inocencio joins us from our London news room to talk about this. Hey there Ramy, good morning. How tall is the task facing delegates at this year's conference, especially considering a big emitter like the US isn't represented there. Yeah, tall in one word, Errol. Good morning. Uh the upshot here is that really it's not looking hardly as good as agreed to back from 2015 during the Paris climate accord, based on all the new greenhouse gas emission plans that the world's most powerful governments have submitted in Rio. The Earth's global average temperature is right now predicted to rise by 4 and a half degrees Fahrenheit. This is above the levels before the industrial revolution. The goal though is lower. It's been a max rise of 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit again agreed to 10 years ago. But add to this the fact that the leaders of China, of the US, as you said, and of India are not attending this week, and that is a hit to uh morale and any chances for some kind of positive breakthrough. They are also the world's top emitters of greenhouse gases. China 32% in 2024, the US about 13%, India at about 8%. and just a little bit of context here. Um if you think the earth is getting hotter where you are, that's because it is. Uh Earth's average surface temperature last year was the warmest on record since keeping began in 1880. Uh you can see there that's in Celsius 1.28, that's roughly 2.7 degrees Fahrenheit. And then the 10 most recent years have been the warmest on record. Uh Errol, that's not to say even though it feels like it that that there's a lot of failure here. They say that it's not an absolute failure. This is coming from the UN and that 30 years of talks has helped to lower emissions in fact, something like 12% to 10%, but obviously there's much more work to do especially when the goal is a 60% decrease from pre-industrial levels. title: Typhoon Fung-Wong Approaches Taiwan Amid Heavy Rain Warnings | WION Climate Tracker
transcription: Typhoon Fung Wong, a category 5 storm, has weakened into a severe tropical storm as it moves away from the Philippines, leaving a trail of destruction and chaos in its wake. The typhoon is moving northwest towards Taiwan, where it could make a landfall on Thursday. Now, according to the state weather bureau's latest bulletin, the typhoon is located 370 km west to northwest of Calayan. Now the storm is packing maximum sustained winds of 110 km/h and gusts of up to 135 km/h, moving north to northwest. Authorities have said that the typhoon is expected to bring occasionally gusty conditions over most of Luzon, the Western Visayas, Negros Island region, and northern Samar. Reports claim that the typhoon, which made landfall in northeastern Aurora province on Sunday night, has so far claimed the lives of 18 people. More than 1.4 million people moved into emergency shelters or the homes of relatives before the typhoon made landfall. And about 240,000 remained in evacuation centers on Tuesday. In the town of Dipaculao, torrential rains triggered massive flooding, submerging numerous roads and farms and washing away parts of a national highway. Many homes were completely flattened and countless trees were downed in the storm, with debris scattered across a wide area. According to authorities, the typhoon knocked out power in 276 municipalities across the country and forced many schools and workplaces to close. Fierce wind and rain flooded at least 132 northern villages, including one where some residents were trapped on their roofs as floodwaters rapidly rose. Our house was standing right there and was swept away when the storm and strong waves came, but we were still able to evacuate. We don't know how to restart our lives now because it's so hard to lose our house, especially since we have no money to live on.

title: Kendrick Lamar tops Grammys 2026 nominations, Lady Gaga and Bad Bunny follow, and no Taylor Swift?
transcription: Grammy season has officially begun and the nominees are serving hits on hits on hits. The 68th annual Grammy Awards are set for February 1st, 2026, and the Recording Academy just dropped the full list of nominations. Spoiler alert, it's Kendrick Lamar's world and we're all just streaming in it. That's right, Kendrick leads the pack with nine nominations, thanks to his critically acclaimed album G&X, which dropped last November. Right behind him, Lady Gaga, who scored seven nominations, breaking her own record from way back in 2010. Her latest album, Mayhem, clearly lived up to its name in the best way. But this year's Grammys aren't just about the icons. Rising star Leon Thomas made major waves with six nominations, including Best New Artist. Sharing that six-nod spotlight are Sabrina Carpenter, Serban Ghenea, and Bad Bunny, who if you forgot, is performing at the Super Bowl just one week after the Grammys. No rest for Benito. And people still question his halftime show credentials? Please. Other big names in the mix, Tyler, the Creator, and Doechii with five nods each. Justin Bieber with four, and Bruno Mars, Miley Cyrus, and Selena Gomez rounding out the list with a few well-earned mentions. Oh, and get this. Timothée Chalamet just scored his first Grammy nomination for the Bob Dylan biopic soundtrack, A Complete Unknown. That's right, from the Oscars to the Grammys, Timmy is collecting trophies like vinyls. Now, if you're wondering, where's Taylor Swift? Don't panic, Swifties. Her latest album, The Life of a Showgirl, came out just after the eligibility window closed. But don't worry, she's practically a lock in for the 2027 Grammys. The 2026 Grammy Awards will take place live from the crypto.com arena in Los Angeles on February 1st. A host hasn't been announced yet, but with a lineup this stacked, all eyes are going to be on the categories. Who will take home the gold? We'll find out in February. title: Anthropic's Code Execution GAME CHANGER Cuts LLM Tokens by 98%
transcription: Your AI agents are burning tokens like crazy and it's not your prompt's fault. It's the architecture. Anthropic just dropped the biggest update yet, MCP code execution, and it changes everything about how agents work and can save up to 98% tokens. I'll explain what's new, why MCP needed this upgrade, and I'll show you a real demo that anyone can run locally. Typically, every MCP server exposes 10 to 20 tools. Every tool comes with function description, parameters, types, examples that translates into tens of thousands of tokens. All irrelevant for 90% of tasks. And this is where accuracy drops because the model is drowning in noise. It keeps confusing tools, mixing parameters, hallucinating schema fields, and failing mid-workflow. This is the new mental model behind MCP. Instead of dumping every tool definition into the model's context window, tools appears as a file system. To get the exact estimates, I generated a synthetic cloud watch style data set that looks exactly like what real DevOps engineers deal with. So, it has data for 150 EC2 instances. Each instance has 50 to 150 CPU data points. What the script does is loads the entire data set as raw text. This means all 18,000 data points become part of the prompt. The LLM has to read the entire JSON block. This turns into 355,000 tokens, which is almost double of what the token limit of the LLM is, and ultimately the LLM is choked. It throws a quota exceeded error where the limit is just 125,000 tokens. Now, let's take a look at the MCP style flow, where the model doesn't touch the data set. We filter the data set locally. The local Python finds the high CPU instances. Only the tiny summary is passed into the model. Gemini responds instantly. Token usage drops from 355,000 to 2096. That's more than 98% token savings. And this is the magic. The LLM sees only the result, not the 18,000 data points. This is why MCP code execution is such a big deal. Instead of forcing LLMs to parse huge tool definitions and giant JSON blobs, we let the model write code on which it is exclusively trained on, and we only give it the tiny slice of data it actually needs. Let me know in the comments what you think about MCP code execution. See you in the next video.

questions.question: What is the core problem with traditional AI agent architecture that the speaker highlights?
questions.answer: The speaker explains that traditional architectures burn excessive tokens by loading all tool definitions (descriptions, parameters, examples) into the model's context window, even if most are irrelevant. This causes the model to get confused, mix up parameters, and fail mid-workflow due to being overwhelmed by noise.

questions.question: According to the demo described, what was the token usage before and after implementing the new MCP style flow, and what was the percentage saving?
questions.answer: The token usage dropped from 355,000 tokens to 2,096 tokens, which represents a token saving of more than 98%.

questions.question: How does the new MCP code execution approach differ from the old method?
questions.answer: Instead of putting all tool definitions and raw data into the model's prompt, the new approach treats tools like a file system. The model writes code to filter and process data locally, and only the final, tiny result is passed to the LLM. The LLM sees the result, not the massive raw data.

title: Bruno Mars, BLACKPINK’s Rosé share sweet online moment after Grammy nods
transcription: Bruno Mars, Blackpink's Rosé share sweet online moment after Grammy nods Rosé and Bruno Mars hit track, Apt, receives three nominations for the 2026 Grammy Awards. Bruno Mars and Blackpink's Rosé celebrated their multiple Grammy nominations with a sweet move. The Recording Academy on Friday, November 7th, announced nominations for the anticipated annual music awards show's 2026 ceremony, which included a number of super hit tracks and albums and incredible artists. For the upcoming Grammys, Bruno Mars and Rosé's chart-topping song Apartment received three nominations, including Song of the Year, Record of the Year, and Best Pop Duo/Group Performance. Taking to his official Instagram handle, the 40-year-old American singer shared a heartwarming post to celebrate the prestigious nominations. Expressing gratitude to the Recording Academy, the Talking to the Moon singer penned, I thank you at Recording Academy. The post included a sweet photo capturing a joyful moment between Bruno and the Pink Venom singer, both smiling radiantly as they leaned into a friendly side hug. Rosie, look at that, penned Bruno Mars, tagging Rosé's account. The Die With a Smile hitmaker's post was re-shared by Rosé on her official Instagram stories with a couple of pink heart and a holding tears back emojis. On her stories, the South Korean songstress expressed her overwhelming emotions about the major recognition, posting the posters of her three nominations separately, each accompanied by the captions, I am still processing this, this, and and this. Bruno Mars and Rosé's Apartment. Apartment, released on October 18th, 2024, is the lead single from Rosé's debut album, Rosie, for which she collaborated with Bruno Mars. The track was a commercial success and spent 12 weeks atop the Billboard Global 200.

President Donald Trump, who had earlier said he would skip the meeting later this month, has now confirmed that no US official will attend on his behalf. At the heart of the fallout is Trump's claim of human rights abuses against the ethnic white minority Afrikaners in South Africa. The US president claims the South African government is seizing land from white farmers who still own most of South Africa's farmland. econômicos But identifying solutions to contain global warming is far easier than finding the political will to reduce dependence on oil on a global scale. The ADAAS model is a structured approach that guides your audience through the journey of communication. Are you ready to learn the secrets of successful communication? Let's get started. Use powerful headlines, striking images, and focus on the benefit for your audience to grab attention. Once you have attention, you must spark interest. This is where you engage your audience further. Reveal the hook by making your message relevant to your audience. This is about you. Engage interest with facts, relatable stories, and highlight how your product or idea solves their problem. Now, transform interest into desire. Your audience should want what you're offering. Your goal is to form the I want it response. Make them feel a strong desire for your offering. Connect emotionally, visualize the outcome, show social proof, and use restrictions to drive desire. The action stage is about getting your audience to take the desired next step. Provide a clear call to action, CTA. Tell them exactly what you want them to do. Make taking action as simple as possible. Remove any obstacles that might stop them. Satisfaction is about ensuring your audience is happy. After the action is taken, turn a client into a fan by building long-term relationships. Go beyond the sale to ensure their satisfaction. title: Savannah Ghosts: The Most Elusive Animals Ever Filmed | African Mysteries 1518
transcription: Picture this. The African Savannah at dusk, golden grass waving and shadows creeping across the landscape. Now, forget the lions and elephants for a second. Today, I'm diving deep into the real ghosts of the Savannah. These are the animals even seasoned rangers barely glimpse, the ones whispered about around campfires. Let's start with the Aardvark, a creature so shy it's called the Phantom of the night. With its piggy snout and rabbit ears, it snuffles through termite mounds under the cover of darkness, vanishing before dawn. Next up, the pangolin. Imagine a living pine cone on legs, armored against predators but not against poachers. They curl up tight, and spotting one in the wild, that's a lifetime achievement for any wildlife lover. But the Savannah's secrets go deeper. Ever heard of the serval? These long-legged cats can leap 10 feet straight up to nab a bird mid-flight, yet their golden coats blend perfectly with the grass, making them nearly invisible. And then, the black-footed cat. Don't let its cuteness fool you. It's Africa's deadliest hunter by success rate, yet most locals have never seen one outside a photograph. Filmmakers and scientists spend months, sometimes years just trying to catch a glimpse. Every now and then, trail cameras give us a fleeting look, reminding me that the Savannah still holds mysteries. So next time you think you know Africa's wildlife, remember, the ghosts of the grasslands are always watching, always a step ahead. What would you do to see one of these legends in real life? Let me know in the comments and keep exploring, because the best secrets are still out there, waiting to be unveiled.

title: Satechi On-the-Go Bluetooth Mouse Review: The Perfect Compact Mouse for Travelers
transcription: The Satechi on the go mouse is a really cool compact mouse that pairs really well with an iPad or a laptop. And as the name implies, it's designed for those who are on the go. It's a very slim and sleek profile with a couple of great features built in. I do want to say thanks to Satechi for sending me this to review. They got no input in this content. This is based on my thoughts on this mouse, what I think it's for, and if I think you should go for a different option instead. When I first got this out of the box, I was really impressed with just how small it is. It has a USB-C port on the top for recharging. There's also a DPI button on the top of it that changes the tracking speed on the mouse and can slow it down. The scroll wheel feels really good and you can also click in on the scroll wheel. And then on the bottom of it, you have the Bluetooth pairing button and you also have the off-on switch. What's cool about this is you can easily change from one device to the next just by pressing through the Bluetooth button. And if you want to set up a new device, all you got to do is go to the slot you want to use, press and hold the pairing button, and then the light will start to blink to show you it's in pairing mode. Get in on your device, go to the Bluetooth settings and you can hit connect. So Satechi really designed this to be compact and minimal and it definitely has a pretty low angle for your wrist, but I found it's still pretty comfortable. It's also ambidextrous so you can change the left and the right click depending on your OS. So if you're left-handed, this mouse is going to be a great option for you. You can get it either in the black or the sand color and it's got this leather feel on the top of it. So it feels like a really premium mouse while coming in at a very reasonable $30, which I feel like is a great price for a mouse that has USB-C recharging and the ability to pair to multiple devices. So this is really great if you want to take it on the go with you because the size is so small, it can easily go in the back of your laptop bag. It pairs really nicely with Satechi's new on-the-go keyboard setup, which is cool because it's actually a whole stand for your iPad. So you can use this to turn your iPad into a little mini laptop setup. And then if you want to use this with a computer, you can always just flip it over and pair it with your computer as well. A couple of other things about this, you do get up to 80 hours of battery life on it, which I think is pretty good, and it's of course very easy to recharge with the USB-C port on the top. Charge it with any of your other chargers. So overall, I think this is really a good option if you are on the go a lot and if you want something compact that can easily stow away in your bag. Also, if you're going to get the whole on the go setup, this pairs really nicely with it, it matches perfectly, and it kind of fits that same design of just making a mini setup that can go with any computer or a tablet. Really the biggest con of this is the smaller size means it's not going to be quite as comfortable as some larger options. I definitely miss the side scrolling on a bigger mouse, but I would say that's really not the point of this. The point of this is to have a sleek, compact, and minimal mouse for the user who needs a mouse and travels a lot. So, overall, I think the on the go is a great option for your travel setup. If you're interested in buying one of these, I do have links to buy in the description below. Like this video, subscribe to the channel so you don't miss out on any upcoming content.

title: World leaders gather in Brazil for COP30 climate summit
transcription: A bold plan by Brazil inviting the UN climate conference to Belém, barely equipped to host tens of thousands of guests. For the first time in history, a climate cope will take place in the heart of the Amazon. Brazil's president launched an international fund to help countries slow deforestation and to protect tropical rainforests like the Amazon, but hasn't yet raised the 25 billion dollars to kick it off. 10 years on from the Paris pledge to limit global warming to 1.5 degrees, a sobering message. President Lula, you have called this the COP of truth. I could not agree more. And the hard truth is that we have failed to ensure we remain below 1.5 degrees. The world is still warming, global emissions still rising, supercharging storms like those lashing the Philippines and Vietnam this week. But there is significant progress in that decade, says Guterres. Clean energy is winning in price, performance, and potential. What is still missing is political courage. COP 30 convenes with a climate skeptic in the White House, and for the first time, no high-level US delegation. Prime Minister Carney, formerly the UN's climate finance envoy, isn't here. His office says because of the budget vote. Our attention has been drawn to other threats and crises that can seem more pressing. These talks will need to break through the tariff wars and divisive politics. Brazil's president says the era of fine speeches and good intentions is over. People are demanding action. Canada's delegation arrives next week, including both the current environment minister and the former one. Susan Ormiston, CBC News, Belem, Brazil.

title: Chaos at Paris Concert: Protesters Disrupt Israeli Philharmonic!
transcription: Why do 100% of concertgoers expect peace, but some nights, drama takes center stage instead? What happens when culture collides with protest? Paris found out the hard way. Last night, the Israel Philharmonic Orchestra planned to fill Paris with classical brilliance, but the real fireworks weren't on stage. Mid-performance, pro-Palestinian activists unleashed flares inside the packed auditorium, sending smoke swirling where only music should have soared. Security scrambled, the audience froze, and the elegant hall was suddenly a battleground of ideals and orchestral chairs. The protest, demanding a boycott, halted the music not once, but three times. Imagine Beethoven interrupted by emergency sirens, tuxedos clashing with tearful shouts. Four protesters were arrested, but the show, somehow, went on, thanks to nerves of steel from the musicians. French officials condemned the chaos, reminding everyone, violence and art don't mix, no matter the cause. The Philharmonie de Paris says it'll press charges, drawing a hard line between creative freedom and confrontation. High culture met high drama, and Paris was left asking, when politics burst into the concert hall, who really gets heard?

title: Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 — Specs, Features & Early Impressions
transcription: Meet the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40. Xiaomi's newest budget friendly cleaner that promises big suction power and smart navigation, all at a surprisingly reasonable price. Now officially available in Europe and the UK, the S40 is priced at 169.99 pounds in the UK and 199.99 euros in Germany. And yes, that includes free shipping. It might look simple, but this compact robot hides some serious tech under the hood. At its core is LiDAR navigation, the same laser-guided system found in higher-end models. It carefully maps your home for efficient room-by-room cleaning. The design is minimalist, and the charging dock, compact and discreet. Perfect for small apartments or tight spaces. But the real star here is power. With 10,000 pascals of suction, the Xiaomi S40 easily tackles dust, crumbs, and pet hair, even from carpets. Its specially designed main brush minimizes tangles, and the side brush is hair-resistant, saving you from the usual maintenance headaches. On a single charge, it can run for up to 180 minutes. That's enough to cover most homes in one go. The 520 ml dustbin isn't massive, but considering its compact design, it gets the job done. Just remember, there's no self-emptying feature, so you'll need to empty it manually every few sessions. As for mopping, let's keep expectations realistic. The S40 drags a damp cloth behind it for light cleaning, ideal for removing surface dust or minor spills. But there are no rotating pads or deep scrubbing action here. Think of it as a finishing touch rather than a full mop replacement. For the price, the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 strikes a smart balance. Strong suction, efficient navigation, and essential functionality without the luxury price tag. It's the kind of robot that simply gets the job done, quietly, efficiently, and affordably. If you're after a dependable cleaning companion that won't break the bank, the Xiaomi Robot Vacuum S40 might just sweep you off your feet.

title: SpaceX Launches 28 Starlink Satellites: Falcon 9 Booster Lands Successfully (Video)
transcription: Get ready for a thrilling journey into the world of SpaceX and its ambitious Starlink project. SpaceX just launched another batch of 28 Starlink satellites, and the story behind these launches is truly out of this world. Imagine, if you will, a world where every time SpaceX sends up a new set of these broadband satellites, you get a little richer, or at least a little more well-nickled. That's right. SpaceX has been busy and their Falcon 9 booster, known as 1093, has had quite the adventure. This particular booster, after its eighth flight, successfully separated its stages, performed deceleration burns, and then gracefully landed on a drone ship in the Pacific Ocean, all within 8.5 minutes of liftoff. Talk about precision. But here's where it gets controversial. Booster 1093, now riding the drone ship named Of Course I still love you back to port, will be refurbished and readied for future launches. Some might question the environmental impact of such frequent launches and refurbishments. While B1093 was making its way back to Earth, the Falcon 9's upper stage continued its mission, carrying the 28 Starlink satellites to their deployment point in LEO, low Earth orbit. These satellites will join the ever-growing Starlink mega constellation, currently consisting of over 8,800 spacecraft providing wireless internet to customers worldwide. Today's launch was the 142nd Falcon 9 mission of the year, with a whopping 102 dedicated to expanding the Starlink network. That's a lot of launches and a lot of satellites. And this is the part most people miss, SpaceX's commitment to reusable rockets and sustainable space exploration. So, what do you think? Are these frequent launches a sign of progress or a cause for concern? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments. We'd love to hear your perspective on this exciting, yet complex, aspect of space exploration and its potential impact on our world.

title: World leaders gather in Brazil ahead of global climate summit • FRANCE 24 English
transcription: A warm welcome from President Lula for world leaders gathering in Brazil ahead of COP 30 next week. There are muted expectations for the conference without a high-level US presence in attendance, and as a key goal from the Paris Agreement is set to be missed in the next decade, with aims to limit global warming to 1.5° Celsius appearing to fail. Brazil's foreign minister stressed the importance of the moment. The COP meeting holds fundamental importance at this moment, and during this meeting, we will launch several initiatives. The most significant of these is an innovation. It is the TFFF, which stands for the Tropical Forests Forever Fund. Also on the agenda, COP 30 will be talk of transitioning away from fossil fuels, aims to raise a target of 1.3 trillion to assist developing countries to tackle climate change, and plans to boost the global capacity for renewable energy. The conference is being held in Belém, a gateway city to the Amazon rainforest. The symbolic location has proved controversial. Brazil has been criticized for building a new highway to reach the city, as well as recently giving the green light for oil drilling near the Amazon river. NGOs and protest groups are also gathering ahead of the conference, hoping to apply pressure on the attending dignitaries. We're going to ask the Brazilian government, the world, the leaders of other countries to respect indigenous people, to respect indigenous lands, and to recognize the indigenous lands that have yet to be demarcated. title: LA Dodgers Star Kiké Hernández Trolls Drake During World Series Parade  ‘October's Very Own'
transcription: LA Dodgers star Kiké Hernández trolls Drake during World Series parade: October's Very Own. As if losing a gut-wrenching Game 7 weren't bad enough for Drake and the Toronto Blue Jays, the hits kept coming during the Los Angeles Dodgers' World Series parade on Monday. Outfielder Kiké Hernández had some fun at Drake's expense and took a playful shot at Drizzy when addressing the Dodger Stadium crowd on the mic. It's October's very own, he said, which felt as if he was ripping a WWE promo. Hernández later made a witty reference to lyrics from Drake and Future's 2015 hit, Big Rings. This really big team that has a lot of really big rings, he said. The Dodgers have captured three World Series titles since 2020 and became the first franchise to go back-to-back since the New York Yankees in 1999 and 2000. Drake was in attendance for a couple of the World Series games in Toronto, and even after the torturous extra-innings loss in Game 7, the six god thanked the team for a dream season. Congrats to the Jays for a dream season and a legendary World Series fight, he wrote to his IG story. After the Jays took a 3-2 series lead following Game 5, Drake even had some fun trolling Dodgers superstar Shohei Ohtani with a pair of posts to his IG story. However, it came back to bite Drake once the Dodgers won the next two games in Toronto, including a classic Game 7 by a score of 5-4, which ripped the hearts out of Canada's team, which was inches from capturing its first title since 1993. The Dodgers poured salt in the wound for Drake when referencing lyrics from Kendrick Lamar's scathing, Not Like Us anthem in a team photo on social media after clinching the World Series on Saturday night. They still not like us, the Dodgers wrote.

transcription: Charles Coste, the world's oldest living Olympian and a celebrated cycling champion, has passed away at the age of 101. The French presidency confirmed that Coste died last Thursday, leaving behind a legacy that spanned more than a century of dedication to sport. Coste first rose to international prominence at the 1948 Olympic Games in London, capturing the gold medal in the men's team pursuit at the historic Herne Hill Velodrome. Alongside teammates Pierre Adam, Serge Blusson, and Fernand Decanali, the quartet, known as the ABCD team, won by nearly 40 seconds over Italy, marking the largest margin of victory in Olympic cycling history. His accomplishments didn't end there. Coste went on to compete professionally with the Peugeot team, claiming victory at the prestigious 1949 Grand Prix des Nations, where he defeated Italian cycling legend Fausto Coppi. Over his career, he rode in two Tours de France and four Giros d'Italia, retiring from professional cycling in 1959. After hanging up his wheels, he pursued a new path as a sales inspector for La Blanchisserie de Grenelle, Europe's largest laundry, demonstrating the same discipline and commitment off the track that had defined his athletic career. More than 70 years after his Olympic triumph, Coste returned to the spotlight as one of the final bearers of the Olympic flame for the 2024 Paris Games. In a moving moment during the rain-soaked opening ceremony, he wheeled himself into the stadium dressed entirely in white, lighting the torches of French Olympic gold medalists Teddy Riner and Marie-José Pérec. That moment symbolized the passion and spirit of transmission that drove him, Riner said. Charles Coste embodied dedication, respect, and love for sport in all its forms. Emmanuel Macron's office praised Coste as, until his final breath, the tireless messenger of a certain idea of sport, highlighting not only his athletic achievements, but also his enduring role as an inspiration to generations. Following the passing of Hungarian gymnast Ágnes Keleti earlier this year, Coste had held the distinction of being the oldest living Olympic champion, a testament to his longevity and influence in sport. From pedaling a wooden tricycle as a child near Toulon to becoming a national and Olympic hero, Charles Coste's life was defined by dedication, excellence, and the pursuit of greatness. France and the global cycling community have lost a legend, but his achievements and the inspiration he provided will be remembered forever. The President of the Republic and his wife pay tribute to the memory of this champion who left his mark on the history of his sport and of the nation, Macron's office said, offering condolences to Coste's family and cycling enthusiasts worldwide.

title: How Did Journalists Cover The Berlin Wall's Construction? - I'm a 60s Baby
transcription: How did journalists cover the Berlin Wall's construction? Imagine waking up to a city suddenly divided overnight. That's exactly what happened on August 13, 1961, when the Berlin Wall began to rise. Journalists were quick to report this startling change, capturing the shock and confusion felt by Berliners. News outlets described how barbed wire and barricades appeared suddenly, cutting East Berlin off from West Berlin. Reporters used vivid words like barbed wire, steel barriers, and military presence to paint a picture of the tense scene. Radio stations, especially from the American sector, played a vital role. Stations like Radio in the American Sector provided live updates, warning people about the new restrictions and urging caution. Journalists on the ground described soldiers reinforcing the wall with steel barriers and East German troops patrolling the border. Newspapers in the West published eyewitness accounts, emphasizing how families were separated and freedoms restricted. They highlighted the speed of construction and the human toll of this sudden division. West Berlin's leaders, including the mayor, expressed outrage and called for support from Western allies. These statements were widely covered, showing the political tension. The East German government initially denied plans to build a wall, with leaders like Walter Ulbricht claiming there was no intention to do so. As the wall went up, journalists reported on this contradiction, illustrating the propaganda battles happening alongside the physical construction. International coverage also focused on the broader Cold War tensions. Reports described US troop movements and the famous tank confrontation at Checkpoint Charlie later that year. Journalists framed the wall as a symbol of communist oppression and the deep ideological divide between East and West. During the 1960s, coverage was full of urgency and emotion. Reporters told stories of fear, hope, and resilience of Berliners living through one of the Cold War's most defining moments. They combined eyewitness accounts with political analysis, capturing the era's style of reporting. This coverage helped the world understand the significance of the Berlin Wall's construction and its impact on global politics.

title: 2025 New York Marathon: Hellen Obiri wins her second New York marathon title
transcription: Now to great news. It was a historic day on the streets of New York City as a 2025 New York City Marathon produced one of the most dramatic finishes in the event's history and a powerful Kenyan showcase. Benson Kipruto edged out rivals in the closest men's elite finish ever, while Hellen Obiri led a commanding Kenyan podium sweep in the women's race. 26.2 grueling miles across all five boroughs, the 2025 New York City Marathon came down to a heartbeat. Kenya's Benson Kipruto produced a breathtaking finish, surging at the tape to edge compatriot Alexander Mutiso by just 16 hundredths of a second, the closest men's elite finish in the event's history. Both athletes were credited with the same official time of 2 hours, 8 minutes, and 9 seconds, marking the first time a New York City Marathon elite race, men's or women's, has been decided by less than a second. potentially working against Sifan Hassan, she has no idea what's coming. Right, she doesn't. On the women's side, it was a Kenyan total dominance. Hellen Obiri led a stunning Kenyan podium sweep and smashed a 22-year-old course record by more than two minutes, clocking 2 hours, 19 minutes and 51 seconds. The reigning Boston and New York champion reaffirmed her status as one of the world's greatest marathoners, combining tactical brilliance with raw endurance. From Kipruto's nail-biting sprint to Obiri's record-breaking run, the 2025 New York City Marathon will be remembered as a celebration of endurance, excellence, and Kenya's unshakable pride on the global stage. title: How much security is at the New York Marathon?
transcription: The operation is led by the NYPD alongside private security firms and other city agencies. There are police on nearly every block, drones in the air, sniffer dogs, and police boats guarding the harbor. Bag checks are common and large bags are banned around the finish area. There are also plain clothed police officers embedded in the crowds. After the tragic events of the Boston Marathon bombings, New York City significantly increased surveillance with thousands of cameras covering the course. Evacuation plans and emergency routes are mapped for every segment of the race. Thankfully, these are almost always just precautionary. There are over 1,500 medical personnel supporting the marathon, including doctors, nurses, EMTs, and volunteers. Medical tents are placed roughly every mile or two with major field hospitals near the finish and higher risk areas. Mobile medical teams patrol in fast response cars. Defibrillators are kept at regular intervals and especially in dense spectator zones. Each runner's bib holds essential info for rapid identification. They fill out any medical conditions and emergency contacts so medics have access to that instantly. Thankfully, most issues are minor though: cramps, dehydration, and exhaustion. Because the medical layout is so dense, response times are often under a minute.

title: Insta360 X4 Air : First Look - Review Full Specifications
transcription: Earlier this year, Insta 360 introduced the latest X5 action camera and later followed with the X5 Satin white limited edition variant, which we reviewed last month. Now, the action camera manufacturer Insta 360 has launched a new 360° action camera in its X series, the Insta 360 X4 Air. The company has advertised the X4 Air as the lightest ever, 8K 360° action camera in the brand's roster. Dimension-wise, it measures 46 x 113.8 x 37 mm, 1.81 x 4.48 x 1.45 in, and weighs just 165 g, 0.36 lbs, which is almost equal to the smartphone's weight. By contrast, the original X4 has the same dimensions, but it's slightly heavier than the X4 Air, weighing in at 203 g, 0.44 lbs. Insta 360 has incorporated dual 1/1.8-inch CMOS sensors into the X4 Air, which further helps to capture footage with better detail and more vivid colors. Like the X5, the action camera also ships with Insta 360's intelligent exposure algorithm, adaptive tone. Speaking of imaging capabilities, the CMOS sensor outputs at 29 megapixels with an F 1.95 aperture and a 6.4 mm equivalent focal length. It can capture 360° videos at up to 8K 30 FPS. Despite boasting a compact form factor, Insta 360 has managed to squeeze in a 2010 mAh battery into the X4 Air, and the brand claims that it offers up to 100 minutes of runtime when recording footage at 6K 24 FPS.
