title: How Arsenal Are Trying to Fix Their “Library” Reputation | Emirates Atmosphere Transformation
transcription: How Arsenal are looking to improve their atmosphere. Arsenal are enjoying an excellent start to the season, four points clear at the top of the Premier League after nine games, as they fight to lift the title after three successive second place finishes. But concerns remain about the atmosphere at Emirates Stadium. Chance by some opposition supporters, which refer to the Emirates as a library, have highlighted what can be perceived as a lack of noise at the ground. It is not an issue only affecting Arsenal, with a number of supporters from traditional big six clubs regularly posting on social media about how the lack of atmosphere at home matches can be disappointing. For Arsenal, there are reasons why there may be a perceived drop in atmosphere at the Emirates, including a rise in expectations from fans. However, Arsenal have not won the Premier League since 2004 and last lifted a trophy in 2020 when they won the FA Cup. In the past couple of seasons, manager Mikel Arteta has made a point of speaking about the importance of the fans in the stadium and wanting to generate the best atmosphere in the world at the Emirates. Arteta regularly now delivers messages to supporters in his pre-match news conferences. One of the visible changes that came this season was that Arsenal removed the cover from the players tunnel. This was done so Arsenal players and, crucially, the opposition can hear the noise before kickoff. It has also meant that supporters in that area can connect with players. And there have been numerous pictures of players high fiving and interacting with fans as they go in and out of the tunnel. We need to ignite the atmosphere so they can play every single ball with us, because it makes such a difference. Arteta said when asked about the change. We want to play and win things. title: Man disguised as woman allegedly recorded women in Maryland gym showers
transcription: The Tacoma Park man accused of posing as a woman to secretly record women in gym locker rooms being held without bond tonight. Well, the defense attorney asked the judge to consider a less restrictive option than being held without bond, arguing that while the crimes are problematic, they're not violent. Now, police first learned of the suspect on October 10th after a woman at One Life Fitness in Germantown reported a man entered the woman's locker room and recorded her in the shower. Investigators later identified the suspect as 44-year-old Chikunidi Tati of Tacoma Park, arresting him on October 9th at the Planet Fitness in White Oak. Police say that Tati was at the gym for seven hours without working out. He would then put on a wig and pretend to be a woman to enter the locker room where he would film his victims. He would then hide his disguise while leaving to avoid detection. He's now facing up to a year in jail on multiple counts of peeping Tom and visual surveillance of a private area. One of the biggest factors that a judge is looking at when determining bond is dangerousness. So in this case, the judge determined that there was no less restrictive means to ensure the safety of the community. People need to be able to feel safe when they are at the gym showering. So this defendant will remain held without bond until trial, which will be in district court on December 15th. Now, an interpreter was in court to translate as the suspect speaks Lingala, the native language of the Congo. title: Spain marks year since deadly Valencia floods
transcription: Spain held state-led memorials marking the one-year anniversary of the Valencia floods that killed 237 people, with a national ceremony in Valencia attended by King Felipe and Queen Letizia, regional officials, victims' relatives and large public demonstrations. At the state funeral, relatives, accompanied by the monarchs, laid a wreath in national colors and the names of victims were read aloud. King Felipe urged authorities to investigate the causes and circumstances of the tragedy to draw lessons and bolster emergency responses. Emotions ran high. A relative publicly blamed regional leader Carlos Mazón for failings that contributed to the loss of life, and some attendees shouted demands for his resignation as the ceremony closed. Outside official proceedings, tens of thousands joined torchlit processions and silent marches across Valencia and nearby towns. In a symbolic act, 229 emergency foil blankets, one for each person killed in the Valencia region, were placed in public squares to highlight the scale of the loss. Families and residents continued to press for accountability amid ongoing court inquiries into Mazón's conduct and whereabouts during the emergency, prompted by reports that he spent hours at a lunch when he was expected at an emergency meeting. Mazón denies wrongdoing and says he remained informed by phone but has declined to release details or the restaurant bill. The floods were produced by a DANA, Depresión Aislada en Niveles Altos, weather event that unleashed torrents of rain and sudden flash flooding, in some places delivering the equivalent of a year's precipitation within hours.

title: Lake İznik’s Sunken Church: Why Did This Basilica Sink Beneath the Water?
transcription: The lake gave no sign. For centuries, the waters of Iznik rippled softly against the edge of a city once called Nicaea, birthplace of Christian creed, stage for imperial councils, and grave to forgotten martyrs. Nothing in the breeze, the current, or the reflection hinted at what lay beneath. But in 2014, a drone camera flew low over the water and found a church sleeping just below the surface. 50 meters from the shore, in water barely 3 meters deep, rose the submerged skeleton of a Basilica. Its stone walls followed a familiar pattern, three aisles, east-facing aps, a square narthex, a structure from the early 5th century CE, built shortly after the first Council of Nicea had rewritten the rules of heaven. Scholars now believe it was dedicated to St. Neophytos, a young martyr said to have been killed on that very shoreline, stabbed and abandoned in the shallows for refusing to renounce his faith. The Basilica's shape suggests reverence, but its fate speaks otherwise. In the year 740, an earthquake shattered the region, temples fell, walls cracked, and this church, already fragile on marshy ground, collapsed into the lake and vanished from memory. No chronicler recorded its loss, no pilgrimage map marked its name. For 1,300 years, it lay beneath the water like a cathedral entombed in silence. But even underwater, the clues remained. In 2025, excavators confirmed its identity as the church of the Holy Fathers, possibly built near or over the site of the council itself. Around it, archaeologists found burials, eight tombs lined with terracotta tiles tucked beneath the nave and apse. Infants, children, adults, laid in sacred shadow as if hoping to sleep close to a martyr's bones. And just beyond the ruin a pendant surfaced, its face worn but still clear. St. Nicholas carried by a pilgrim and dropped in reverence or fear. Yet the past here is layered. Beneath the Basilica, some believe are the foundations of a forgotten Apollo temple. Others whisper of a Senate palace where emperor once spoke of salvation. And still others suspect the site predates all of them, a shrine built atop a necropolis, where holiness was measured by how long the dead had waited. No inscriptions remain, no relics speak. Only stones pressed flat by silt and time, held in place by the lake's stillness. But when drought comes, as it has in recent years, the water recedes, the basilica rises again. Columns break the surface, the apse returns to light. For a brief moment, the church is no longer drowned, just exposed. Plans exist now for an underwater museum. Glass walkways suspended above the nave, viewing chambers, lit vaults where visitors may pray or simply witness. But for now, it remains where it was found, submerged, weightless, intact. A sanctuary that did not fall from grace, but was carried into it.

title: 6.1 Earthquake Shakes Istanbul, Turkey: Buildings Collapse, Residents Fearful
transcription: A powerful earthquake has rocked Turkey, leaving a trail of destruction in its wake and sending shock waves through the nation. But this time, the tremors hit close to home, shaking the very heart of Istanbul. The ground shook with a 6.1 magnitude force, causing buildings to crumble and citizens to flee in fear. The quake's epicenter was located in Sindergi, Balikaysar province, a region no stranger to seismic activity. And here's the part that hits hard. The quake struck at a shallow depth of approximately 6 kilometers, amplifying its impact on the surface. The quake's timing, just before midnight, added to the chaos. As the earth rumbled, people rushed from their homes, seeking safety in the open air. Three buildings, already weakened by a previous earthquake, met their demise, collapsing in a heap of rubble. Thankfully, no immediate casualties were reported, but the psychological toll is undeniable. The tremors were felt across Istanbul and nearby provinces, including Bursa, Manisa, and Izmir. The quake was followed by a series of aftershocks, keeping residents on edge. And this is where it gets controversial. The region has experienced smaller quakes since August, but the lack of major incidents may have led to a false sense of security. The aftermath reveals a community in distress. 22 people suffered injuries from panic-induced falls, a stark reminder of the physical and mental trauma earthquakes can inflict. Sindergi's district administrator, Dugan Karanku, assured the public that no fatalities had been identified, but the search for survivors continued. As rain poured down, the situation grew more dire. Mosques, schools, and sports halls opened their doors, offering refuge to those too terrified to return home. The memory of the August earthquake, which claimed a life and injured many, was still fresh in people's minds. Turkey's position on major fault lines makes it particularly vulnerable to earthquakes. The nation has endured devastating quakes in the past, including the 2023 earthquake that took over 53,000 lives and left a trail of destruction across 11 provinces. But this recent quake serves as a stark reminder that even smaller tremors can have a significant impact. So, what can be done to better prepare for these unpredictable forces of nature? Are current safety measures sufficient, or is it time to re-evaluate and adapt? Share your thoughts below, and let's spark a discussion on how we can build a more resilient future.

When you go to certain places, they're so rich in culture. And when you go to Brazil, the depth of that culture is something you feel in every person you meet. It's such a very, very diverse country. title: NVQLink: Unlocking Quantum-GPU Supercomputing
transcription: There are many ways to build a quantum computer. Each uses qubits, quantum bits, as its core building block. But no matter the method, all qubits, whether superconducting qubits, trapped ions, neutral atoms or photons, share the same challenge. They're fragile and extremely sensitive to noise. Today's qubits remain stable for only a few hundred operations, but solving meaningful problems requires trillions of operations. The answer is quantum error correction. Measuring disturbs a qubit, which destroys the information inside it. The trick is to add extra qubits, entangled, so that measuring them gives us enough information to calculate where errors occurred without damaging the qubits we care about. It's brilliant, but needs beyond state-of-the-art conventional compute. That's why we built NVQLink, a new interconnect architecture that directly connects quantum processors with Nvidia GPUs. Quantum error correction requires reading out information from qubits, calculating where errors occur, and sending data back to correct them. NVQLink is capable of moving terabytes of data to and from quantum hardware, the thousands of times every second needed for quantum error correction. At its heart is CUDA-Q, our open platform for quantum GPU computing. Using NVQLink and CUDA-Q, researchers will be able to do more than just error correction. They will also be able to orchestrate quantum devices and AI supercomputers to run quantum GPU applications. Quantum computing won't replace classical systems. They will work together, fused into one accelerated quantum supercomputing platform.

title: World's First Interactive AI-Enabled Fusion Reactor Digital Twin
transcription: For decades, fusion energy, the process that powers the sun, has been one of science's greatest opportunities. Cracking it would give us a safe, clean, and virtually unlimited source of power. Controlling plasma hotter than the sun's core means solving physics so complex that even the fastest supercomputers struggle to simulate it. At the forefront of this effort, General Atomics researchers and international partners at the D3D National Fusion facility are using AI to push fusion research forward. The team is building a fully interactive digital twin of the D3D Tokamak inside NVIDI Omniverse. It fuses sensor data, physics simulations, engineering, and AI models, creating a virtual reactor that can quickly inform decisions. Key controls can be explored in the digital twin to refine the science before running real experiments. These surrogate models trained on decades of real-world data sets and running on NVIDI GPUs deliver accurate predictions at unprecedented speed. This is a platform to optimize reactor designs, accelerate commercial fusion, and make the sun's power programmable.

title: How To Check If Apple Watch Is Cellular Or WiFi/GPS? Tell If Apple Watch Is Cellular Capable
transcription:
Hey everyone, welcome back to Wearholic. If you have ever wondered, is my Apple Watch cellular or GPS? This video will clear all your doubts. Let's quickly see how to check if your Apple Watch is cellular capable or Wi-Fi only, step-by-step. 
First things first. If you're buying a new Apple Watch, simply check the box packaging. It clearly mentions whether the watch is cellular or GPS. 
If you're buying a second-hand Apple Watch, ask the seller for the original box, so you can verify it. But if the box isn't available, don't worry. You can still find out whether your Apple Watch is cellular or GPS using a few simple methods. 
First, open the Watch app on your iPhone. Scroll down and tap on My Watch. If you see an option to set up cellular, or if there's already a mobile plan showing, congratulations. Your Apple Watch is a cellular model. If you don't see any cellular settings at all, that means it's a GPS only model. Pretty simple, right? 
Now, let's check directly on the Apple Watch. Press the digital crown button, go to settings. If you see options for 'add a plan' or your carrier name, then again, it's cellular capable. If that menu isn't there, it's just a Wi-Fi GPS model. 
You can also swipe up or from the control center. If there's a green dot icon or antenna bars, it's a cellular model. 
Another quick way, look at your watch's digital crown. If it has a red ring around it, that's a sign of a cellular model on most Apple Watches. Or, if you want to be 100% sure, open the Watch app, General, About, find the model number. Search that number on Apple's official website. It'll tell you exactly whether it's a GPS or GPS plus cellular. 
Even if your Apple Watch is cellular capable, remember, it still needs to be compatible with your carrier. For example, a US model may not work with Indian networks. So always check your region's carrier support page before activating the plan. So, now you know how to check if your Apple Watch is cellular model, GPS only or cellular capable but not activated yet. If this helped you, give this video a thumbs up, drop your Apple Watch model in the comments, and subscribe to Wearholic for more simple and practical wearable tech guides. Thanks for watching and I'll see you in the next one.

title: Paris Fire Dept. creates 'Young Hero Award' for recipient with courage beyond her years
transcription: The Paris Fire Department gave out their first young hero award this week, created because of the quick thinking of one girl. And it's not only what the recipient did to earn the honor, but how young she is that makes it so special. Katie Moore has the story. I'm so thankful that she was there that day. It was a normal shift for Cheyenne Roberts last Tuesday in Paris, babysitting Amelia Fitzgerald. She was folding clothes when the day took a turn for the worse and Robert started having a seizure. My phone was unlocked and she had grabbed it. She had called my sister. Amelia was acting off pure instinct and courage when she FaceTimed Robert's sister. My sister goes, you okay? She said, no. And then she she said, is okay? And she said, no. But here's where the story gets extremely remarkable. Amelia, can you say how old you are? Two. You heard that right. Just two years old. EMS responders say they've never heard of any story quite like this. You know, this is a job where we see a little bit of something different every day and I've got to say that this is a first one on me. Jesse Lusader says, if Amelia wouldn't have made the call, it could be a much different story. He says a lot of risk factors come into play with seizures like traumatic injury and concerns for breathing processes. For a child that young to have the presence of mind to not just pick up the phone, but let alone be able to place a call to us to be able to respond to help is pretty pretty remarkable. Now after getting the first young hero award, Amelia is proving heroes come in all sizes. And it's her love and bravery that changed everything and Roberts couldn't be more grateful. It's it's a blessing. It really is. like thankful that she had came into my life because I don't know what I would do without her. Thousands have marched in the streets demanding justice and the resignation of the region's president over his handling of the disaster. Roads transformed into raging rivers. Cars swept through streets and stacked like toys. Homes destroyed. Last year's floods in Valencia, Spain killed 229 people, and as the first anniversary approaches, the waters may have receded, but anger at the government remains. Thousands of protesters marched through the streets demanding Valencia's regional president, Carlos Mazon, resign over his handling of the disaster, Europe's deadliest floods in over half a century. We want Mazon and his entire government to resign for failing to take responsibility for a full-blown massacre. President Mazon has been criticized for not sending out alerts until after the flooding had already started. By the time they were, for many, it was already too late to leave. It's getting worse every day. You hear him speak and it's one lie after another. I have lost three people and they were all very young. All I ask is that justice be done. Protests in the immediate aftermath of the floods became heated. Even Spain's king was pelted with mud when he visited victims. And while this demonstration was more subdued, the message was just as strong, with ongoing inquiries yet to deliver the justice victims are demanding. Patrick Murrell, 10 News.

title: Notre-Dame hosts rare wedding for carpenter who helped rebuild it • FRANCE 24 English
transcription:
It's one of the world's most symbolic cathedrals and a dream setting for a wedding. In the past, Notre Dame in Paris has seen kings and emperors come and go, but on Saturday, it was a carpenter tying the knot with his partner.
de les recevoir. Soyez les bienvenus dans cette cathédrale. Parce qu'en fait elle accueille des lieux, elle accueille des mots qui te voilà.
Amidst the crowd visiting the cathedral, Martin and Jade exchanged their vows.
Jade, le tu... Oui.
The wedding was planned a long time ago, during the reconstruction of Notre Dame, but having it as a ceremony venue seemed impossible. For three years, Martin Lorentz worked on rebuilding the roof structure. With his fellow workmen, he cut the beams with an axe as they had been 800 years ago, sometimes working day and night before all the pieces were assembled at the top of the cathedral. 
So when he asked the Archbishop of Paris for permission to get married at Notre Dame, Monsignor Ulrich said yes, but only as a one-off. The result was 500 guests, including many carpenters.
C'est dingue de voir que ça se fait finalement et de retrouver les copains là. Je suis trop content. Vive les mariés !
At the end of the ceremony, tourists applauded the newlyweds, while the other carpenters made a guard of honor with their axes in hand.
I want to share my love, our love with the whole world, with everyone who needs it. It's the happiest day of my life. I don't think I can say anything else.
It's another beautiful chapter that adds to the story of Notre Dame.

title: Elon Musk’s Shocking Outburst: “Why Are You Gay?” — Clash with Trump Official Over NASA Contract
transcription: In a dramatic turn of events, billionaire Elon Musk has once again set the internet on fire. This time, by lashing out at a top Trump administration official over a lost government contract. The controversy began when Sean Duffy, the acting administrator of NASA and US Transportation Secretary, claimed that SpaceX, Elon Musk's company, is falling behind on its mission to return humans to the moon. Duffy even hinted that the US government might open the contract to other companies, sparking instant fury from Musk. Within hours, Musk took to his platform, X, formerly Twitter, and launched a series of posts mocking Duffy. He called him Sean Dummy, questioned whether someone with a two-digit IQ should be running America's space program, and then shared a meme with the caption, Why are you gay? That single post went viral instantly, not for humor, but for outrage. Critics accused Musk of being disrespectful, unprofessional, and even homophobic, saying such remarks cross the line for a public figure leading major government projects. Supporters, however, argue that Musk is simply fighting back against unfair government pressure and political bias. They point out that SpaceX has already revolutionized space travel and saved NASA billions through reusable rockets. But the timing couldn't be worse. The US government is reviewing its next phase of moon mission contracts, and Musk's public outburst may further strain his relationship with officials. What began as a corporate disagreement has now become a very public feud, blending politics, ego, and the high stakes of America's space ambitions. Whether Musk's bold defiance helps him or hurts him, only time will tell. But one thing's for sure, when Elon Musk speaks, the world listens, even if it's for all the wrong reasons.

title: The official Timekettle W4 tutorial
transcription: Take out the earbuds, remove the insulation sheet. and put them back to activate the device. Close the charging case. Reopen the charging case. The indicator lights of the earbuds will flash, indicating that they are ready to be connected. Launch the Timekettle app and select W4. Finish the Bluetooth setting following the steps shown on the page. Once the connection is successful, the indicator light stops flashing and the translation function is available. Select the one-on-one mode. Share the earbuds and set the languages and accents for each speaker to start simultaneous translation. Select the listen play mode. Wear the earbuds and put your mobile phone close to the sound source for real-time recording and translation. Select the language to be translated to hear the translated audio content via your earbuds and view the transcribed and translated text in real-time on your mobile phone. Click the speak button to talk. The earbuds will record your voice, and the mobile phone will play the translation result of your speech. Click the icon in the upper right corner of the homepage to quickly enter the history page. Click all at the top to filter translation records in different modes. Click to view and share translation records. Click AI summary at the bottom to generate the summary, which can be copied and pasted. Click on the AI section in the bottom tab. You can also open the history page and generate an AI summary. Offline translation is available under the one-on-one and listen play modes. Select the offline translation option and click download for the required language pack. Click to enter the one-on-one or listen play mode to activate the offline translation. Connect to the mobile phone via Bluetooth to listen to music and make phone calls. Users with wide ear canals can use ear tips to cover the earbuds before putting them on. Users with narrow ear canals can use ear hooks to stabilize the earbuds.

questions.question: What is the initial setup process required to activate the earbuds for the first time?

Thomas, thank you for joining us after tonight's goalless draw against Monaco. What were your takings of today's game?
Um, I think um, we're definitely learning in the Champions League. Um I think we were in away um against a very good Monaco side. I've said that before the game. It doesn't surprise me they hit a good level today. I think it was a relatively even first half. Uh second half, Monaco was better than us. We didn't hit the performance level we wanted. Uh we didn't play with that intensity we want, um which is which is the big thing. And then I think there was just too many individual errors, passes um that that where we didn't didn't hit the level we want to. Um and sometimes that happen. Um and that what, yeah, which we didn't do today.
As you say, a really tight game and you need big moments either end of the pitch. Today we got that from Vicario in goal. made nine saves, kept a clean sheet today. That really positive performance from him.
Yeah, it's it's a kind of contrast to to the last game against to Villa where we I think we played with great intensity and I think we we very competitive performance and basically gave nothing away and Mick didn't have a save. And then this uh this game we didn't play with enough enough intensity especially the second half. and we needed Vic nine times, which of course, uh we like to defend better, which is is is too much in general. Uh but sometimes you need that for a keeper. It is it's it's football that can happen. So, Vic was fantastic today.
As you said there, away in the Champions League is is never easy, it's always a real challenge. One of those cliches of if you can't win if you can't win, don't lose. and that sort of came in tonight. We saw players sliding in, making blocks. As you say, Vicario's performance, that's that's a real plus.
Yeah, I think, you know, definitely the team definitely wanted to to defend the goal and and did everything they they could to do that and I think sometimes you can't hit a um a high enough level which we didn't do today and then then then we need to take a point uh and a clean sheet, um which is which is good on a on a day where we didn't hit a high level.
Yeah, I was just going to ask how does that point feel over three unbeaten now in this competition, two two of those away from home.
I think I think the point we'll be more happy with in the end, I think. Um I think right now in the moment, I'm I'm disappointed with our performance especially the second half. Uh but I also need to understand, we need to understand that the the learning of playing in the Champions League uh and playing against teams that is very very competitive. Playback your video in GoPro's Quick app to automatically smooth any bumps or shakes with HyperSmooth video stabilization. With a built-in long-lasting Enduro battery, Lit Hero lets you record longer than ever. And if you manage to scratch or crack the super strong Gorilla Glass lens on the go, you can simply swap it out with a twist to keep on rolling. Make your camera even tougher with the bumper-like protective sleeve and easier to find in the water with Floaty. Lit Hero comes with built-in mounting fingers and 1/4-20 mounting threads, and it's magnetic latch mount compatible, giving you three ways to quickly and easily swap your camera between mounts and accessories. Lit Hero only costs a fraction of our flagship camera, yet packs iconic GoPro performance from razor sharp image resolution to automatic highlight videos sent to your phone. title: Physiology of Fever by E. Freiman | OPENPediatrics
transcription: Fever is an elevation in body temperature mediated by hypothalamic pathways in the central nervous system. The hypothalamic thermoregulatory center controls body temperature through three mechanisms. One, controlling heat production mainly in the muscles and liver, two, controlling heat dissipation from the skin and lungs, and three, setting the normal body temperature. Fever is a physiologic process where the hypothalamus sets a higher body temperature set point in response to endogenous signaling. The body then rebalances heat production and dissipation to elevate the body temperature to the new set point. This is why patients with new fevers often feel cold and experience rigors. Their current body temperature, although elevated above true normal, lies below the newly elevated hypothalamic set point and leads to the subjective feeling of cold.

RTX kit is our suite of rendering technologies to create photorealistic worlds. One of these technologies, RTX Mega geometry scales up geometric complexity to achieve the highest quality ray tracing. title: Shrapnel hit CHP vehicle during Marine Corps demonstration at Camp Pendleton

Eyewitness news reporter Carly Gomez is here with us now, and what we're finding out about what happened here, Carly. Yeah, Joey, Sophie, the California Highway Patrol has now published an internal report after finding shrapnel from an explosive that was fired over the five freeway and into one of their CHP patrol cars. This all coming after a back and forth disagreement between Governor Newsom and the Marines via X over whether to shut down the freeway for the Marines' 250th anniversary celebration. While the Marines stated they would not shut down the freeway Saturday during live firing from navy ships onto land, the CHP elected to stop traffic out of caution that someone could get hurt. CHP says around 1:46 p.m., an explosive ordinance prematurely detonated overhead from White's Beach about three quarters of a mile south of Las Pulgas Road, striking their vehicle where CHP was supporting traffic breaks. The Marine Corps was notified on scene and then canceled firing additional ammunition. Now the California Highway Patrol is recommending an after-action review into the planning, communication as well as coordination between federal, state, and local government. Now Governor Newsom posted on X saying, we love our Marines and owe a debt of gratitude to Camp Pendleton, but next time, the vice president and the White House shouldn't be so reckless with people's lives for their vanity projects. Now a section of the five freeway was closed multiple times for about four hours creating backups for miles north and southbound. Luckily, nobody was hurt. A spokesperson for J.D. transcription: Here's how to get the best fit with your AirPods Pro 3 so you can experience ideal sound quality, optimal noise cancellation, and accurate performance from the heart sensors. Your AirPods Pro 3 come with medium-sized ear tips already attached. First, try on your AirPods with the medium-sized ear tips attached and positioned so that the heart sensors are facing forward. Gently press your AirPods in your ears and rotate the stems toward your face. The fit should feel snug and secure, and the heart sensor on the side of each AirPod should make good contact with the skin on your ear. If the fit is too loose or causes excessive pressure in your ear, try another ear tip size. You can remove an ear tip by gripping it with your fingers near its base where it's attached to the AirPod and pulling straight out using steady pressure. If you need more grip, use a clean, lint-free cloth to help you remove the ear tip. If you need a different grip, roll the edge of the ear tip inside out, then grip both sides of the ear tip firmly with your fingertips and pull straight out using steady pressure. To attach an ear tip, align it with the oval-shaped connector on the AirPod. Then, push it onto the connector until you hear it click into place. Repeat this process if needed until you achieve the optimum fit. You can also take an acoustic seal test using your iPhone to confirm you're getting the best sound quality and noise cancellation. In your AirPods settings, scroll down to the Fit and Comfort section. Then tap Test Acoustic Seal and follow the prompts. And that's how you get the most out of your AirPods Pro 3.

transcription: The new iPad Pro now runs on a chip that might be too powerful for a tablet. Like, share, and subscribe, because this upgrade changes what an iPad can actually do. This is not just the M4 with tweaks. The new M5 chip inside is Apple's boldest move yet. With 10 CPU cores, 10 GPU cores, and every single GPU core having its own built-in neural brain for artificial intelligence. Apple says these performance cores are now the fastest in the world. Not mobile fast, but fast. Period. That means video editing, 3D design, or AI image generation can happen at desktop speeds on a tablet. And that power is not just on paper. The M5 delivers three and a half times the AI performance of the M4, one and a half times faster 3D ray tracing, and 1.2 times faster video rendering in Final Cut Pro. That is a serious leap in real world use. For creators, this iPad now outputs 120 hertz to external displays with adaptive sync or VRR. That means no more stutters and no more screen tearing. Your animations will look buttery smooth. Even the wireless side got smarter. The new N1 chip handles next generation Wi-Fi, while the C1X modem boosts mobile connectivity. And with Apple's new 40 watt dynamic power adapter, you can hit 50% charge in under half an hour. The 256 GB and 512 GB models now come with 12 GB of memory, up from 8, so multitasking feels instant. And the best part is that despite all these upgrades, Apple did not raise the price. The 11-inch starts at $999 and the 13-inch at 12.99. But here's the real question. If this is what the M5 can do in a tablet, what happens when Apple puts it inside the next MacBook Pro or Vision Pro? The future of Apple silicon might have just started here.

title: Cheetah: The Speed King of the Savannah | A Wildlife Documentary
transcription: The cheetah, a sinonyx jubatus, is a large cat known as the fastest land animal in the world. It has a slender, aerodynamic body built for speed with long legs and a deep chest. Adult cheaters have tan or pale gold fur covered with small, solid black spots all over their bodies, except for the white throat and belly. One distinctive feature is the black tear marks that run from the inner corners of their eyes down to their mouths, which help reduce glare from the sun and aid in focusing on prey. Cheetahs can reach speeds of 93 to 104 km/h, 58 to 65 miles per hour in short bursts covering distances up to 500 m. Cheetahs reside mainly in various habitats across Africa and Central Iran, such as Savannas and arid mountain areas. They play an important role in their ecosystems by controlling prey populations and helping maintain balance. Unlike other big cats, cheetahs have semi-retractable claws which give them better grip, similar to track spikes on running shoes. They primarily hunt during the day and rely on their exceptional eyesight to spot prey from a distance.

title: Quiet Comets of 2025: C/2022 E3 & 240P/NEAT’s Subtle Journey | InnoVision Tech
transcription: The quiet visitors. Not every comet is a headline grabber. Some slip through the solar system as faint smudges, their passage noted only by dedicated observers. Among the seven visitors of 2025, two fall into this quiet category, C/2022E3 or Panstars and the periodic comet 240p/Neat. C/2022E3 reaches its perion on July 31st at a chilly distance of 3.82 astronomical units, or about 571 million km from the sun. At that range, it's not expected to brighten beyond a modest magnitude 10, visible only in medium-sized telescopes. Then there's 240p/Neat, which was discovered in 2002 and returns every 7.6 years. It makes its pass on December 19th at a distance of 2.12 astronomical units or 317 million km. Its performance will likely be even dimmer, a low key encore for those tracking its well-documented path. For both of these objects, the primary audience will be astronomers contributing data to the minor planet Center, where every verified observation helps refine orbital calculations. Even these faint comets provide crucial data on things like nucleus rotation and the slow development of their comas. They are the workhorses of cometary science, providing a baseline of normal activity against which the brighter comets can be compared.

questions.question: What are the names of the two "quiet visitor" comets mentioned for 2025?
questions.answer: The two comets are C/2022 E3 (also called PanSTARRS) and the periodic comet 240P/NEAT.

title: TCL NXTPAPER 11 Plus vs 14 Review – Which Tablet Is Right for You?
transcription: I have with me right now the TCL NXT Paper 14 and the TCL NXT Paper 11 Plus. and over the past couple of months, I have been testing out these two tablets. So, I just wanted to give you guys my honest thoughts on them, see how they stack up against each other. And overall, give you guys just a few things to consider before you settle on one of the two. The first and most obvious difference between the two is obviously going to be the screen size. The 11 Plus is lighter, faster, and more portable. It's got an 11 and a half inch 2.2K display and runs on NXT Paper 4.0 technology. Not only that, but it also has a 120 Hz refresh rate, and that refresh rate is going to be super important, especially for someone that values a lot smoother and more seamless browsing experience. When you compare the two, the 11 Plus is smoother for navigation, animations, and stylus interactions, while the 14 is geared more towards reading, writing, and large format use. The 11 Plus comes with a stylus, supports pressure assist, and unlike the Paper 14, it comes with a few different AI features like text assist and writing assist. You're also getting an 8 GB RAM and 8 GB of virtual memory storage, as well as 256 GB of regular storage, which is on par with the Paper 14. One key difference with the 11 Plus is that it's getting a faster MediaTek G100 chip, all packed into a slim and lightweight body just under 500 grams. The battery sizes on the two tablets will differ slightly as well. The 11 Plus comes with an 8,000 mAh hour battery while the 14 comes with a 10,000 mAh hour battery. Honestly, although the 11 Plus did come with a smaller battery, I found that the difference in battery life with just normal practical use was pretty negligible. I typically got around two days of moderate use out of both tablets and well over a week of standby time. Now, if you're someone that values screen real estate a lot more, the NXT Paper 14 definitely delivers. This tablet has a huge 14.3-inch display, also comes with a 2.4K resolution. However, it only has a 60 Hz refresh rate. In terms of software, it's running NXT Paper 3.0, which focuses more on a paper-like and anti-glare look, and it's definitely perfect for sketching or reading. You still get the stylus with 4,096 pressure levels, plus a flip case and multi-window multitasking. Overall, I thought there was a lot more of a heavier emphasis on productivity and multitasking with the Paper 14 opposed to the 11 Plus. And that probably had to do with the bigger screen and the ability to switch through different tabs fairly easily. The 11 Plus was definitely meant to be a lot more portable and an easier alternative for students that didn't want to take around a bulky laptop to class. The key takeaways that I got from this experience is that the 11 Plus is more balanced for hybrid use. It offers a high refresh rate, a more advanced display generation, lighter weight, AI features, and a comfortable size for one-hand or mixed usage. On the other hand, the 14 is better suited if your priority is to have a larger canvas. It's really good for reading long documents, viewing diagrams, or large pages, multitasking, or using it more like an actual tablet or digital notebook. You'll ultimately be trading off portability and smoothness for a more immersive experience. All in all, I do think both tablets do have their pros and cons, and ultimately, it kind of just boils down to how you want to use it and how you envision it in your day-to-day life. All things considered, I definitely still recommend both tablets as really strong contenders against the competition.

title: 82-Year-Old Woman Attacked By Bear In Japan
transcription: Surveillance video captured the moment an elderly woman was attacked by a bear. It happened in a residential neighborhood in the Akita prefecture in Japan. The 82-year-old woman was reportedly out for a morning walk when the bear attacked her in a parking lot near a railway station. Surveillance video from a nearby business recorded the incident, in which the woman can be heard yelling in horror. The bear didn't stick around long after the woman seemed to dodge its attempts to jump on her. Then she stood there and watched as the animal retreated to a wooded area. To vote online, look for an email from your broker. For most shareholders, you can either search your inbox for a message from ID@proxyvote.com and follow the instructions in the email. Or, you can take the shareholder voting materials you received in the mail and locate your control number. For most shareholders, it will be a unique 16-digit number. Visit proxyvote.com to cast your vote. Even easier, most of you can vote by QR code. On those same shareholder voting materials you receive by mail, scan the unique QR code provided. Follow the instructions as shown to cast your vote. If you prefer to deal with your so-called smartphone, vote by phone. Find your unique control number on the insert in the shareholder voting materials you received by mail. Call the phone number on the insert to cast your vote. While these instructions apply for most shareholders, please follow the specific instructions you have received. If you have not received voting instructions, please contact your broker. If you need further help voting your shares, or you have any questions, please call our proxy solicitor, Innisfree M&A Incorporated. Advertisers and publishers can also collaborate to discover and reach audiences and measure advertising impact while respecting customer privacy. title: Faint Comets Nobody Sees | The Quiet Visitors of 2025 | Stellar Tech
transcription: The quiet visitors. Not every comet is a headline grabber. Some slip through the solar system as faint smudges, their passage noted only by dedicated observers. Among the seven visitors of 2025, two fall into this quiet category. C 2022 E3 or Panstars, and the periodic comet, 240p NEET. C 2022 E3 reaches its perihelion on July 31st at a chilly distance of 3.82 astronomical units, or about 571 million kilometers from the sun. At that range, it's not expected to brighten beyond a modest magnitude 10, visible only in medium-sized telescopes. Then there's 240p NEET, which was discovered in 2002 and returns every 7.6 years. It makes its pass on December 19th at a distance of 2.12 astronomical units, or 317 million kilometers. Its performance will likely be even dimmer, a low key encore for those tracking its well-documented path. For both of these objects, the primary audience will be astronomers contributing data to the minor Planet Center, where every verified observation helps refine orbital calculations. Even these faint comets provide crucial data on things like nucleus rotation and the slow development of their comas. They are the workhorses of cometary science, providing a baseline of normal activity against which the brighter comets can be compared.

title: Biggest Bear Ever Recorded
transcription: Have you ever looked into the eyes of a wild bear, strong and majestic, and wondered what gives anyone the right to take that life away just for a trophy? Across the world, hunters chase after the largest bears, not for survival, not for protection, but for pride. These powerful creatures are targeted simply because they are big and because they look impressive on a wall. One of the largest bears ever recorded was a kodiak bear measuring over 13 feet, 4 meters tall when standing and weighing nearly 2,500 pounds, over 1,100 kilograms. Think about that, an animal that took nature generations to perfect, reduced to a trophy photo. But what's left behind when the gunfire stops? A broken ecosystem, orphaned cubs, and one less guardian of the forest. We can change this by spreading awareness to our young children and grandchildren, by choosing compassion, and by saying no to the cruel sport of hunting the largest bears. If you believe that every creature deserves to live free and unharmed, share this video with as many people as you can. Let's make the message loud and clear, protecting wildlife is everyone's responsibility. And if you stand with us, don't forget to hit like, subscribe, and turn on notifications. Together, we can spread a culture of kindness and respect for all living beings. Because the wild isn't ours to conquer, it's ours to protect.

title: Google Slides vs Keynote (2026) - Which One Is BETTER?
transcription: Google Slide versus Keynote, which one is better? Let's find out. Google Slide is a free cloud-based presentation tool that is part of Google Workplace. It's perfect for teams who need real-time collaboration, easy sharing, and seamless integration with Google Drive and Docs. It's lightweight, accessible on any device with a browser, and great for remote work. The tradeoff is that its design options are more basic compared to some other tools. On the other hand, Keynote is Apple's native presentation software included for free on Mac OS and iOS devices. It is known for polished templates, smooth animations, and high-quality design features, making it a favorite for visually stunning presentations. It also supports iCloud sinking and works offline, but collaboration is limited compared to Google slides and is restricted to Apple's ecosystem. Now, let's compare them side by side. Google slides prioritizes collaboration and accessibility across platforms, while Keynote focuses on design quality and smooth performance within Apple's environment. Slide is ideal for team projects whereas Keynote is better suited for individual or Apple-based users who want visually polished presentation. If you need flexibility, sharing, and cross-platform compatibility, go with Google slides. If design excellence and Apple integration matters most, Keynote is a stronger option. Your Tesla Model Y is designed to keep its clock accurate by automatically synchronizing with global positioning system satellites and cellular networks. This means for most drivers, the time will always be correct without any intervention. However, there are specific situations where you might want to make an adjustment or check the settings. We will cover both the automatic functions and how to make manual changes. Your Tesla Model Y relies on advanced technology to ensure its clock is always accurate. It uses signals from global positioning system satellites and its cellular connection to automatically update the time. This intelligent system usually accounts for changes like daylight saving time and when you drive across different time zones. For the best performance, always ensure your vehicle has a strong network connection, which helps it receive the most precise time data. While your Tesla usually handles time automatically, you can adjust it manually if necessary. First, tap the car icon on your touch screen to open the controls menu. Next, navigate to display or time and date settings. Here, you will find an option to set time, allowing you to manually adjust the hours and minutes using plus or minus buttons. You can also easily switch between a 12 hour and 24-hour clock format to suit your preference. When traveling, your model Y is designed to automatically update its time zone. If you notice the time is incorrect, a quick fix is to press and hold the time displayed on your screen for about 5 seconds. This often triggers a re-synchronization. If the issue persists, performing a soft reboot of your vehicle can help. Simply hold down both scroll wheels on your steering wheel until the touchscreen restarts, which usually takes about 30 seconds. Thanks for watching. title: Solomon Islands bid for UN Security Council  Non Permanent Seat
transcription: The Solomon Islands announced its first ever bid in 46 years for a seat on the Security Council, having registered its interest 11 years ago. Prime Minister Honorable Jeremiah Manele announced the country's bid when delivering his statement at the 80th United Nations General Assembly meeting in New York. He said Solomon Islands is ready to contribute to UN peacekeeping missions, reaffirming its commitment as a peace-loving member of the International community. Solomon Islands is seeking for the first time in 46 years a non-permanent seat in the UN Security Council for the period 2032 to 2033. We registered our interest 11 years ago. Let me thank countries who have confirmed their support for our candidature over the years. As a peace loving country, Solomon Islands is keen to contribute to UN peacekeeping missions this year. Ladies and gentlemen, we must do more for peace. Protect civilians, especially children and women. Prime Minister Manele also made the appeal for Solomon Island presence at the UN to be evaluated. He said the country remains underrepresented within the UN staff establishment. Madam President, Solomon Islands reiterates its call for an elevated UN presence. The time has come to review the UN regional architecture, to ensure it remains connected to the members that need it most. Solomon Islands remains underrepresented within the UN staff establishment. We call on the UN to consider convening in-country competitive recruitment exams in Solomon Islands. On Security Council reform, we seek a more democratic, expanded council that reflects today's geopolitical realities. The use of the veto by the Council continues to undermine peace, international law, and expose the vulnerable to harm. The veto must be eliminated as part of the reforms of the Council. We hope to see proposals shift into text-based negotiations

title: How To Stop Random Noises/Alerts On AirPods Pro 3 – Chimes, Beeps & Haptics
transcription: Experiencing random chimes, beeps, or haptic feedback on your AirPods Pro 3? These are often linked to firmware glitches, mode switches, or customizable features. The good news is, most of these can be resolved. Chimes or beeps usually indicate events like low battery or pairing, while haptic signal mode changes, such as active noise cancellation turning on or off. Random triggers can be caused by environmental factors, such as wind detection triggering mode switches, or software bugs like accidental Siri activation. To stop them, start by updating your AirPods firmware via settings, general, software update, ensuring your AirPods are connected. If problems continue, move on to the next section to further troubleshoot and stop these disruptions. Now that you know where these sounds come from, let's fix them. Open your iPhone settings and navigate to accessibility AirPods. Here, you can disable specific sounds like play sound on mode change to stop beeps when switching between ANC and transparency. For more aggressive solutions, try resetting your AirPods. Hold the force sensor on both earbuds for 15 seconds until the status light flashes amber, then re-pair them with your device. As of the latest updates, including iOS 18.1, you may also have an AirPods Control Center widget for quick alert management. If issues persist, consider third-party apps for fine-tuning haptic intensity or muting Siri prompts. By following these steps, you can minimize unwanted noises and customize your AirPods Pro 3 experience.

title: How to Upload a PowerPoint to Microsoft Teams Presentation Guide
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to share a PowerPoint presentation in Microsoft Teams. Whether you're leading a team meeting, conducting a workshop, or simply sharing information with colleagues, knowing how to efficiently upload and present a PowerPoint is essential. Let's dive right in. First things first, open Microsoft Teams on your desktop or laptop. You can log in using your account credentials if you haven't already done so. Once you're in the Teams interface, the next step is to navigate to the specific channel or chat where you want to share your PowerPoint presentation. This step is crucial because it ensures that the right audience has access to your materials. Channels are typically designated for departments or projects while chats might be with specific colleagues or smaller groups. Now, pay attention to the message box at the bottom of your team's window. Below this box, you'll notice an array of icons that assist with various functions. One of which is the paper clip icon symbolizing attach. Clicking this icon is your gateway to uploading external files into Microsoft Teams. It's both intuitive and efficient. After clicking on the paper clip icon, you'll see a range of options available. For our task, you'll want to choose the option labeled upload from my computer. Selecting this option will open your file explorer, allowing you to locate the specific PowerPoint file you wish to share. Take a moment here to ensure you select the correct file, as this will save you any hassle later on. Once you have selected your file, double click it or select open to begin the upload process. Uploading might take a few moments depending on the size of your presentation and your internet connection speed, so just be patient. During this time, it's always a good practice to ensure that your presentation is precisely as you want it before sharing. Check for spelling errors, correct slides and appropriate content. Once the file has successfully uploaded, it will appear in the chat or channel. To begin presenting it during a meeting, simply click on the file. This action will open your PowerPoint within teams, allowing you to present it seamlessly. Make sure to familiarize yourself with the presentation controls in teams, such as starting and stopping the presentation, navigating between slides and any interactive features your slide deck may have. By following these steps, you're now well- equipped to present a PowerPoint in Microsoft Teams. Remember, the key to smoothly executing this process lies in preparation and ensuring you're comfortable with Team's interface. Thank you for watching and happy presenting.

title: How To Use AirPods Pro 3 Touch Controls – Press, Hold & Swipe Tutorial
transcription: The AirPods Pro 3, released in September 2024, feature intuitive touch controls on the stems. These controls allow you to manage audio and calls without needing your phone. This tutorial guides you through press, hold, and swipe gestures to get the most out of your AirPods Pro 3. Controls are located on the stem. Press or slide gestures manage audio hands-free. Press gestures include single tap for play/pause, double tap to skip forward, triple tap to go back. Hold with a long press to toggle Active Noise Cancellation, Transparency mode, or turn off. Swipe up or down for volume control, swipe left or right to skip tracks. These controls are fully compatible with iOS 18+ and offer basic functionality on Android via Bluetooth. For iOS, you can even customize these gestures. Features include Active Noise Cancellation, Transparency mode, and more. Press gestures use quick taps on the AirPods Pro 3 stem. A single tap plays or pauses audio or answers and ends calls. Double tap skips to the next track, while triple tap goes back to the previous track. The hold gesture involves pressing and holding the stem for 2 to 3 seconds. This cycles through Active Noise Cancellation to block out sound, Transparency mode to let in ambient noise, and turning the feature off. Swipe gestures are new to AirPods Pro 3 and provide precise control. Swipe up or down on the stem to increase or decrease volume. Swipe left or right to skip tracks forward or backward. This is more accurate than previous models. Users can customize these gestures through the Bluetooth settings on their iOS device. For best results, keep the stems clean and ensure firmware is updated.

title: An experimental new way to design software
transcription: We've been experimenting with a new way for AI to build software. It's called Imagine with Claude. Imagine with Claude is still building software, but we've cut out the middleman. Instead of writing code that describes this text box, Claude just makes the text box. We've given it access to software tools that construct software directly and substantially faster. Here, Claude isn't writing code in the standard way. It doesn't have to plan it all out in advance. Instead, it generates new software on the fly. When we click something here, it isn't running pre-written code. It's producing the new parts of the interface right there and then. As you can see from the thought process, Claude is working out from the overall context what you want to see. The user has clicked on X, so that must mean they want to see Y. It then produces it, right before your eyes. On the surface, this might seem like only a subtle distinction from what you've seen before. And the example we've picked here is just for fun. But the underlying approach of this experiment is quite different. This is software that generates itself in response to what you need, rather than following a predetermined script. In the future, will we still have to rely on pre-made software, or will we be able to create whatever software we want as soon as we need it? title: AirPods Pro 3 Case Red Light While Charging – Meaning & What To Do
transcription: Seeing a red light on your AirPods Pro 3 charging case, it's a signal from the case's LED indicator about the charging or battery status. A solid red light usually means the case battery is critically low, below 10%, and needs charging. If you see a flashing red light, this often indicates a charging error, potentially due to a faulty lightning port, incompatible charger, or an internal issue. While charging, the light should turn amber/orange, indicating normal charging, and then green when fully charged. Basically, the red light is a diagnostic indicator to alert you of a problem with power or charging. If you encounter a red light, first try resetting your AirPods via the Bluetooth settings on your paired device. Next, clean the charging port with a soft dry brush to remove any debris that might be interfering with the connection. Then, use a different charging cable and adapter. Ideally, use Apple's USB-C to lightning adapter as the Pro 3 supports both lightning and USB-C magsafe. Also, ensure your AirPods Pro 3 firmware is up to date via your paired iOS device. If the red light persists, it might indicate a hardware fault. In that case, contact Apple support or an authorized service provider, especially if the device is still under warranty, which has been extended to two years in some cases due to reported manufacturing defects.

title: How To Tell If AirPods Pro 3 Are Original Or Fake – Serial Check & Packaging
transcription: As of September 2025, Apple hasn't released AirPods Pro 3. If you encounter them, they're likely counterfeit, possibly capitalizing on rumors or mistaking the second gen. To spot fakes, start with the packaging. Real AirPods Pro second gen boxes feature high-quality cardboard, precise laser etched logos, holographic seals and a serial number matching the earbuds themselves. Fakes often have blurry prints or incorrect fonts. Next, check the serial number on Apple's check coverage page or the support app. A genuine serial will show purchase date and warranty status. Fakes will show errors or invalid responses. Remember, spatial audio, active noise cancellation, and MagSafe charging are standard on genuine AirPods Pro second gen. Fakes often lack these or have poor performance. Be wary of deals that seem too good to be true. While serial number verification is crucial, counterfeiters are getting sophisticated. Some fakes now use AI to generate realistic serials. Always cross reference the serial check with a physical inspection. Genuine AirPods have a fit and finish perfection. Inferior build quality like mismatched components is a red flag. Examine the overall appearance and components for signs of counterfeiting. Look for poor soldering or mismatched components on the circuit board. Even packaging can reveal fakes through poor print quality or incorrect details. Test the sound quality. Originals have crisp highs and deep base, while fakes often sound tinny. Be aware of AI-driven counterfeits that replicate firmware and packaging with near perfection. By staying informed about these evolving tactics and carefully inspecting all aspects of the product, you can greatly reduce the risk of buying fake AirPods.

Social media quickly filled with images of Rome's cobblestone streets turned into rivers and ice, causing astonishment around the world. Meteorologists explained that the storm was caused by the sudden collision of warm Mediterranean air with a cold front that swept through central Italy, an increasingly common pattern associated with climate instability. Despite the chaos, no serious injuries were reported, although dozens of people were treated in hospitals for minor cuts and bruises. title: The Great Fire of London – Flames, Plague, and Rebuilding on Ashes
transcription: Imagine a city already reeking of plague, piled high with timber houses, and stuffed with gunpowder. Then picture one careless spark. That was London, 1666. A tinderbox waiting to explode. It all began in a tiny bakery on Pudding Lane. A spark caught, the flame spread, and within hours, London was an inferno. Roofs collapsed, fireballs lept across streets, and terrified families clawed through smoke trying to escape. The city's wooden homes burned like matchsticks, while the wind turned alleys into fire tunnels. People fled, carrying whatever they could, some clutching furniture, others dragging half-burnt livestock. Most with nothing but ash on their skin. The fire raged for four days. St. Paul's Cathedral, that proud symbol of London, crumbled in the flames. Warehouses full of oil, tar, and brandy exploded into firestorms. By the end, over 13,000 houses and 87 churches were reduced to charred rubble. And while the city burned, rumors spread like sparks. Foreigners were blamed, Catholics were accused of sabotage, innocents were lynched in the streets by mobs who thought the fire was a plot. But here's the real kicker. London wasn't just burning, it was already crawling with plague. The fire roared through neighborhoods where corpses still lay rotting in homes. Some whispered the flames were God's punishment, others that it was mercy, burning the pestilence out. In the chaos, law and order collapsed. Looters picked through burning ruins. Rioters murdered anyone they suspected of starting it. The city was a vision of hell where firelight made night look like blood red day. When the smoke finally cleared, 100,000 Londoners were homeless. Families slept in fields under the September rain. The city stank of ash, rot, and despair. Yet somehow, from the wreckage, London began to rebuild. Brick by brick, flameproof this time. The Great Fire didn't just destroy London. It reshaped it. It burned away the medieval heart of the city, replacing it with something new. But for those who watched their world turn to cinders, it was the apocalypse.

title: Report highlights 'series of weaknesses' in LA wildfire response

Questions still remains surrounding the chaos and confusion of evacuations and alerts in the January wildfires. A new report commissioned by the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors, now pinpointing where those issues began. Eyewitness News reporter Rob Hayes live in downtown Los Angeles with more on the results of this report. Rob? 
Yeah, it's been eight months since those wildfires ripped through Southern California. During that time, LA County officials say emergency response improvements have been made and more are on the way. But after seeing the new report, at least one supervisor says the county still isn't prepared. The new report raising the alarm about the failure to raise the alarm, at least early enough. That just is so strong. LA County's first independent after-action report takes a look at the county's emergency response to the deadly Eton and Palisades fires and highlights what it calls a series of weaknesses, including outdated policies, inconsistent practices and communications vulnerabilities. But it also leaves questions as to why thousands of residents in West Altadina were not given evacuation orders until hours after the flames had already been reported in that area. This McCrystal Group report highlights the fact that we are not prepared if God forbid we have another emergency like this. LA County's top elected officials addressing the report's findings this afternoon. 18 of the 19 people killed in the Eton fire died on Altadena's west side, which is several miles away from where the fire began. Why evacuation orders were delayed for West Altadina, according to the report, could not be blamed on one individual point of failure, but instead rests in part on inter- agency cooperation issues. It reads, outdated and inconsistent policies, protocols and standard operating procedures created ambiguity around evacuation authority and responsibilities. In many cases, decision-making roles were unclear. But LA County Fire Chief Anthony Maroni says changes and improvements are already underway. But he also points out the unprecedented weather conditions that fueled the fire. We are going to be better next time. However, this was hurricane force winds that unfortunately had an associated fire. We will never have enough firefighters to have a truck in front of each person's house.

title: How To Tell If AirPods Pro 3 Are Original Or Fake – Checks, App Tests & Packaging
transcription: Spotting fake AirPods Pro 3 starts with quick checks on packaging and build quality. First, examine the packaging. Original boxes have a clear plastic window showing the earbuds, and the serial number on the box must match the one inside the lid and engraved on the AirPods. Counterfeit packaging often has misaligned holograms or poor printing. Next, check the build quality. Authentic AirPods Pro 3 have smooth, premium silicone ear tips and a matte finish on the stem. Fakes may have glossy stems or uneven engraving. A tactile lid snap on the charging case and subtle haptic feedback when pressing the stem are also signs of authenticity. Remember to leverage the Find My activation feature. If they seamlessly register with Apple's network upon unboxing, it's a good sign. Connect your AirPods Pro 3 to an iPhone running iOS 17 or later. Navigate to settings, then general, about, and select AirPods. Authentic AirPods Pro 3 will display firmware version 7A206 or higher and provide complete battery health information. Open the Find My app to verify that spatial audio and personalized features function correctly. For an extra check, use third-party apps like AirBattery to verify compatibility, but be cautious as unofficial tools may pose a malware risk. Combining physical and digital checks gives you the best chance of identifying fake AirPods Pro 3.

title: How To Connect AirPods Pro 3 To Two Devices – Auto-Switching & Manual Switching
transcription: AirPods Pro 3 can connect to two devices simultaneously, but play audio from only one at a time. Auto switching enables seamless transitions between devices that share the same iCloud account. When you start playing audio on one device, the AirPods automatically switch from the other. This feature works best with Apple devices like iPhone and MacBook. The technology relies on the H2 chip for low latency processing and proximity sensors to detect the active device quickly. Important note, auto switching doesn't support simultaneous audio from both devices. There is a brief pause during each transition. For manual switching, when devices aren't on the same iCloud account or when you need more control, you can switch connections directly. On iPhones and iPads, access AirPods settings through the control center or Bluetooth settings. Simply select the device you want to connect to from the available options. The process is similar on other Apple devices like iPads where you navigate to Bluetooth settings to manage connections. For non-Apple devices, manually disconnect from the current device in Bluetooth settings and then reconnect to the desired one. Keep in mind that auto switching works most reliably within the Apple ecosystem. Frequent manual switching can reduce battery life by 5 to 10%.

title: Rescue work continues in Taiwan's flood-hit Hualien county
transcription: Rescue and relief efforts continued on Friday in Taiwan after Super Typhoon Ragasa flooded a lake above a small town on its remote east coast. Ragasa passed through the Philippines earlier this week before traveling west towards Hong Kong and Southern China. Its outer bands brought heavy rains to Taiwan's Hualien County. The heavy rains in Hualien caused a so-called barrier lake in the mountains to overflow on Tuesday and release a thick sludge of water and mud on the town of Guangfu, where rescuers on Friday waded as they looked for the missing. While the flood waters have receded, the dark gray mud continues to blanket large parts of the area, creating problems for residents and rescuers alike. At least 14 people have been killed and 11 were missing, prompting questions about evacuation orders that were potentially infeasible for the elderly to follow.

title: What Announcement Led To The Berlin Wall's Collapse? - History of Communism
transcription:
What announcement led to the Berlin Wall's collapse?
Imagine waking up one morning and hearing that the border you have been told is closed forever is suddenly open. That's exactly what happened on November 9, 1989, in East Berlin. A government official named Ginter Shabowski held a press conference and announced new travel rules. He said East Germans could now apply for permission to travel abroad without the strict restrictions they had known for decades. But here's the catch. He said the border would be opened immediately or without delay. No one expected such a quick change. People listening to the news thought it meant they could cross the border right away. Thousands of East Berliners flooded to the Berlin Wall, eager to see what was happening. Border guards, overwhelmed and unsure of what to do, eventually opened the gates. This spontaneous movement turned into a mass crossing, and the Berlin Wall, which had divided the city for nearly 30 years, was no longer a barrier. This announcement was part of broader reforms happening across the communist world. East Germany was feeling pressure from internal protests and from the Soviet Union, led by Mikhail Gorbachev, who was pushing for more openness and change. The East German government wanted to ease travel restrictions to calm unrest, but the public misunderstood the scope of the reforms. They believed the border was open for good, which was not exactly the plan. The fall of the Berlin Wall symbolized the weakening of communist control in East Germany and the entire Eastern Bloc. It showed that the socialist governments could no longer hold onto their strict borders or suppress demands for freedom. This event was a turning point that led to German reunification less than a year later, in October 1990. It also marked the beginning of the end for communist rule across Eastern Europe, as many countries experienced their own peaceful protests and reforms. So, the key moment was Ginter Shabowski's announcement during that press conference. It was a simple statement, but it sparked a chain reaction that changed history forever. It was the moment when the people's desire for freedom broke down the physical and political barriers that had divided Europe for so long.

title: I Filmed Eagle's Flight for 30 Days and Learned This ONE Thing
transcription: You know, when you've lived as long as I have, you start to notice things most folks miss. Take the eagle, for instance. Majestic, proud, an old soul of the skies. I've watched eagles for decades, and every time I'm reminded of the wisdom nature holds, if you're patient enough to see it. Now, the eagle doesn't rush. It waits, circling high above, reading the wind, the world below. There's a lesson there, I reckon. Sometimes it's not about how fast you move, but how well you understand your surroundings. When the time comes, the eagle strikes with purpose, never wasteful, always precise. I remember sitting by the riverbank, cane in hand, watching an old golden eagle teach its young to fly. The little one flapped, fluttered, nervous as a leaf in a storm. But the parent watched, steady, patient, letting the eaglet learn from its own trials. Eagles don't fear storms, you know. They ride the winds, using the storm to lift themselves higher. That's something I've tried to remember when life's thrown me a gale or two. Sometimes, you've got to face the wind, spread your wings, and trust you'll soar above it all. So next time you see an eagle overhead, take a moment, watch, listen. There's wisdom in those wings, and maybe, just maybe, a little of that old magic will rub off on you too. Thanks for listening to an old man ramble. Keep your eyes to the sky. You never know what you'll learn.

title: Africa played a collective role in the founding of the United Nations - President Mahama.
transcription: At this 80th session of the United Nations General Assembly, I'd like to speak about Africa's role in the future of this organization. However, it's impossible to do that without first considering the collective role that Africa played in its founding, which was small and relatively insignificant. Of the 51 member states involved in the founding of the United Nations in 1945, only four were African. Egypt, Ethiopia, Liberia, and South Africa. It is important to point out that the United Nations came into being in the aftermath of World War II because of the inability of its predecessor, the League of Nations, to avert a large scale global conflict, which had been its guiding purpose when it was founded in 1920 at the end of the World First World War. Out of the 42 founding member states of the League of Nations, only three were African. Liberia, the Union of South Africa, and Ethiopia. Egypt was to join later in 1937.

Syria today is rebuilding itself through establishing a new state, building institutions and laws that guarantee the rights for all without exception. Ahmed al-Shara swept to power in 2024 in a lightning offensive that ended the Assad family's 50-year rule. But his government faces major problems, a surge in sectarian violence, tension along the border with Israel, and an economy in tatters. To do that, he must allow inspectors into the country and provide details about its stockpile of enriched uranium. Iran has never sought and will never seek to build a nuclear bomb. We do not seek nuclear weapons. This is our belief based on the edict issued by the Supreme Leader and by religious authorities. Therefore, we never sought weapons of mass destruction. title: The EU Entry / Exit System (EES) Explained
transcription: From the 12th of October 2025, the EU will introduce new border checks known as the entry exit system, EES. As a part of its plans to strengthen border security, this is a new digital border system that will change requirements for British and other non-EU citizens traveling to the Schengen area, which encompasses all EU countries except for Cyprus and Ireland. It will also include the non-EU states, Iceland, Norway, Switzerland, and Liechtenstein. The entry exit system is an automated IT system designed to register non-EU nationals traveling for short stays of up to 90 days in every 180 days. It will be used every time an individual crosses the external borders of any of the following countries. When EES is introduced, you may need to create a digital record on your first visit to the Schengen area at the port or airport on arrival. This will involve submitting your fingerprints, having your photo taken, and your passport scanned at dedicated booths. This new system will be introduced in phases over the first six months, and will eventually replace the current system of manually stamping passports when visitors arrive in the EU. You will not need to provide any information before traveling. At the port of Dover, Eurotunnel and Folkestone and Eurostar from St. Pancras, EES will be carried out before departure, as is currently the case for border checks. EES may take a few extra minutes to complete, so be prepared to wait during busy times at the border once the system starts. You can check with your travel operator to find out whether EES will affect your journey. Once registered, your digital record will be valid for three years. If you enter the Schengen area again during this time, you will only need to provide one biometric, either a photo or a fingerprint, at the border when you enter or exit. For more information, visit gov.uk/entry-exit system.

title: AirBNB: how Shelly automated a guest's stay
