title: 🚨OFFICIAL✅ BARCELONA PRESENTS ITS SURPRISE SIGNING! NOBODY EXPECTED HIS ARRIVAL! BARÇA NEWS!
transcription: FC Barcelona faces crucial moments in planning its squad for next season, with important decisions regarding renewals and potential decisions that have caused a stir in the competition. Below, we analyze the key topics, Ferran Torres's contract situation and the possible addition of Xavi Simons to the team. First, we talk about Ferran Torres, known as Shark. In recent months, Barcelona has renewed the contracts of several players, but Torres has yet to receive any offers. After an extraordinary season, the leader has attracted interest from clubs in the Premier League, Serie A, and the Saudi Arabian League, which poses a risk to his continued presence at the club. Coach Hansi Flick highly values Torres and wants to keep him in the future. However, the board must decide whether to renew his contract or approve sale offers. The uncertainty surrounding his future generates a debate. Should Barcelona sell Ferran Torres or secure his renewal? In my opinion, the club should prioritize Torres's contract renewal. His performance, versatility, and commitment make him a valuable asset. Selling him now could generate revenue, but losing a rising player could be a long-term mistake, especially if Flick trusts him with his project. Now, let's move on to the surprising news, the possible signing of Xavi Simons to strengthen the midfield. Although no move in this position was expected, the uncertainty surrounding Frenkie de Jong's continued presence, whose contract had not yet been renewed, led Barcelona to consider this option. Xavi Simons, trained at La Masia and currently targeted by the club, could return following negotiations between Deco and his agent. Hansi Flick had already approved this signing, but much of his passion opposed it, arguing that the midfield was well covered by the current players. The question is whether the addition of Xavi Simons would be necessary. In my opinion, this approach would be unnecessary at this time. Barcelona has a solid midfield, with players like Gavi, Pedri, and other young talents who guarantee quality and depth. Simons, although talented, doesn't seem like a priority, especially considering his arrival could limit players' opportunities. Furthermore, the club should focus on resolving pending renewals, such as that of De Jong, before bringing in new players for a new position. Therefore, I am against this proposal, as resources could be allocated to other more pressing areas, such as defense or attack. In short, Barcelona should renew Ferran Torres's contract to consolidate its project and avoid signing Xavi Simons, prioritizing the stability and development of the current squad.

title: Talking Shop: Slam City Skates Nike SB Air Max 95
transcription: When I first heard about the uh, 95 coming into S I was like, I actually think the story's a lie. I didn't believe it. I really liked the colorway. I think the pink pop here, like matching the laces, is really sick. London street culture is kind of different. There's a lot of different kind of like sub genres and there's a lot of different styles so you can kind of take influence from each one, you know? This is definitely a uniform for this city. This is, this is what you need when you come to the city I think. I first started personally wearing them when I was a teenager. That was like my go-to shoe for a rave. Because like for heel flips, like obviously you got to put your foot like along the edge of the board. The the toe looks rough. Is that rough? Obviously standing on a skateboard, you know, this part part like wears away really easily. So having a bit more a bit more grip in that, you know, definitely helps. I feel like skateboarding and and sneaker culture borrow from each other a lot. Skateboarders, you're out in the street, you're seeing a spot and you're kind of looking at it in different ways and I feel like that's a very very similar thing to what's happened with the 95 is like, okay, we'll lower the footbed, we'll make it a bit more responsive. The right time to to add the 95s off of Andy's feet to my uh, to my to my collection. Slam has been around for almost 40 years. It means a lot of different things for different people in different timelines. The first time I stepped into Slam City Skates was in Covent Garden. I was like 13, 14. I started skating when I was 14, 15, and then around 16, 17, I was coming to London. I'd come up to like, I got to go to Slam, grab a sticker, slap it on my board, and then when I go back home, everyone be like, "Whoa, you went to Slam!" It's like a safe space. Found out friends had passed away whilst we're in the shop, found out, you know, people getting married, having kids. It was all in this community hub which offers so much more than just a shop. For the younger crowd, it's somewhere where they can go, they can chat about what's going on in skateboarding, but then to the older generation it's like a trip down memory lane. They're like, 'I went to Slam when I was, you know, 15 and that was in like 1992,' and I'm like, 'Bro, I was two years old.' If you walk into my store and you're like, I know nothing about skateboarding, but I want to get into it. That's the best thing for me.

title: NFL Training Camp - Raw Footage 8/6
transcription: I've watched a lot of raw footage from joint practices and teams getting ready for joint practices, and here are my biggest takeaways. It might not sound right, but Russell Wilson and Malik Neighbors are actually getting along pretty well. The two of them have been spending a lot of time together in the meeting rooms and outside of the facilities, and it's showing on the field. Russell Wilson is putting the ball where Malik Neighbors can get it, and Malik Neighbors is always going to go up and get it. Their chemistry is a lot better than people want you to believe, and I think it might actually work out. Who's winning the Colts QB battle? Neither of them. And that is the reason Anthony Richardson's going to start versus the Ravens and Daniel Jones is going to start versus the Packers. They're both going to play in a pre-season game and whoever looks better is going to end up being the starting QB. And if I'm putting my money on one of them, it's going to be Anthony Richardson. Yes, he makes mistakes, but he's also the one who's making the more explosive plays. What's happening at Colts-Ravens joint practice? The Colts defense is actually getting a lot more stops than you would expect against the Ravens offense. Mark Andrews is 100% Lamar Jackson's go-to target. It's not even a question. And Michael Pittman, Josh Downs, and Tyler Warren are going to be your big three receivers for the Colts. Treyveon Henderson might be a three-down back. He's looked excellent in pass protection. He can obviously run the ball, and not only is he catching passes, but he's getting wide open. Meanwhile, Rhamondre Stevenson is fumbling. And speaking of three-down backs, Ashton Genti is not going to be leaving the field for the Raiders. We all know that he's a fantastic runner, but he's actually looked really good in pass protection, and he's already become one of Geno Smith's favorite targets. And I think there is a very high possibility he's touching that ball 25 plus times a game. Bonus tidbit, don't forget about Donte Thorton Jr. He is absolutely tearing up training camp every single day. He is getting more and more work. Shedeur Sanders is gonna be the QB for the Browns in most of the preseason. But that's not what I want to talk about. I don't care if the QB is Joe Flacco or Shedeur. Either way, we are sleeping on David Njoku. This man has been catching so many passes. And I think people forget that he had 64 receptions, 505 yards and five touchdowns last season in just 11 games. And finally, Dolphins training camp is physical as fuck. And I'm telling you right now, I'm 20 minutes from the facilities and it is hot as balls out there. But it don't matter. Tua Tagovailoa is absolutely thriving. He's completing 70% or more of his passes. He is executing on third downs and in the red zone like he doesn't usually do. And he's only thrown one interception in all of training camp. And while I know our defense is going to suck, I'm very high on the Dolphins offense this year. A-bada-bing-bada-boom. Baby.

title: 'Exceptional' World War II film leaves viewers in tears and declared a 'masterpiece'
transcription: A World War II themed movie has taken audiences by storm, moving viewers to tears while earning widespread praise from critics and fans alike. Released in 2019, Jojo Rabbit has been hailed as a cinematic masterpiece, one that blends humor and heartbreak in a truly unique way. Directed by Taika Waititi, the film is a satirical coming-of-age story set during the final years of Nazi Germany. At its heart is Jojo, a 10-year-old boy who, indoctrinated by Nazi propaganda, idolizes Adolf Hitler, imagining him as his comical, imaginary best friend. But everything changes when Jojo discovers a Jewish girl hiding in his attic. This discovery forces him to question everything he believes, setting the stage for an emotional and often absurd journey of self-discovery. Viewers have described the film as a powerful blend of laughter and sorrow. One IMDB reviewer wrote, it was hilarious and heartfelt. The acting was superb, the story was thought-provoking. It was funny at times and heartbreaking at others. Another called the film moving, hilarious, tragic, admitting they had doubts at first but trusted Waititi's vision. The emotional roller coaster is real, they added, praising the film's originality and depth. I laughed and I cried, another fan confessed. This film was exceptional, one of the best I've seen this year. Waititi's comedic vision is brilliant, and the cast is phenomenal. The cast includes Roman Griffin Davis in his breakout role as Jojo, Thomasin McKenzie, Sam Rockwell, Rebel Wilson, Stephen Merchant, Alfie Allen, and Scarlett Johansson, with Waititi himself portraying a ridiculous, imaginary version of Hitler. Adapted from Christine Leunens' novel Caging Skies, Waititi initially drafted the script in 2011. Though the original version was much darker, it evolved into a black comedy that could balance satire with genuine emotion. Filming took place in 2018, and the movie premiered the following year to critical acclaim. Jojo Rabbit earned multiple awards, including the Academy Award for best adapted screenplay, making Waititi the first Marry filmmaker to win in that category. Audiences and critics have since labeled it a must watch film, especially for fans of war dramas told from a fresh and human perspective. From laughter to despair, Jojo Rabbit manages to confront the horrors of war through the innocent lens of a child, making it a standout film that resonates long after the credits roll.

We're operating in or around the noise margin of transistors. And as many of our viewers know, when you have the voltage, the power consumption will drop by a factor of four. The result is uh is again incredible battery life. Um customers can use that to either extend the lifetime of their uh of their product on a single charge so that users are having to charge less often. Alternatively, you can uh reduce the size of the battery in the product, allowing the product to be thinner and sleeker and more elegant to fit into a smaller enclosure. Um the other option is is keeping your current battery life but adding significantly more performance. title: What Birds Can You See In The Masai Mara? - Bird Watching Diaries
transcription:
What birds can you see in the Masai Mara?
Have you ever wondered what birds you might encounter in the stunning Masai Mara? This incredible region in Kenya is a paradise for bird lovers, boasting over 580 recorded species. The variety of habitats here, from open savanna to wetlands, supports an amazing range of birds. Let's start with the impressive birds of prey. The Masai Mara is home to many eagle species. You might spot the Tawny Eagle, Steppe Eagle, and Imperial Eagle soaring above. Other raptors include the African Hawk-Eagle and Verreaux's Eagle. If you keep your eyes peeled, you may also see the Bat Hawk and several types of buzzards like the Common Buzzard and Long-legged Buzzard. As you wander through the grasslands, look out for the large ground birds. The Common Ostrich is a prominent sight, strutting across the savanna. Near the rivers and wetlands, you can find various waterfowl. Keep an eye out for the White-faced Whistling Duck and the Northern Pintail among others. Wading birds are also abundant in the Masai Mara. Plover and lapwing species are often seen near water bodies. You might encounter the Little Ringed Plover and the Kittlitz's Plover. The Blacksmith Lapwing and the Spur-winged Lapwing are also common in these areas. In the wetlands, look for the Greater Painted-snipe and the African Jacana. These birds thrive in the lush environments created by the rivers and marshes. The diversity of birds here reflects the rich ecological variety of the Masai Mara. The different habitats, including riverine forests and acacia woodlands, provide food and nesting sites for many species. This makes the Masai Mara a vital area for bird survival and reproduction. The presence of various raptors indicates a healthy ecosystem with plenty of prey. For birdwatchers, the Masai Mara offers a unique opportunity to see a wide range of African birdlife in one location. Whether you are a seasoned birder or just starting, this region is a must-visit for anyone interested in birds. With its rich diversity and stunning scenery, the Masai Mara truly is a birding hotspot in Kenya.

title: MTA making changes to prevent flooding in subway stations

I think what makes people most nervous is when they're seeing water coming from above. There was water cascading from above, water spouting up from the sewer system. Water seemed to be coming from everywhere during the flash flooding two weeks ago at the 28th Street station in Chelsea. We have a risk of storm water overtopping the sidewalk and flowing into the subway. This protects against that. Eric Wilson, who oversees climate resistance and sustainability planning for the MTA, directing strap hangers to ongoing station upgrades and flood mitigation measures in the agency's capital plan. This elevated step, the most basic thing and the most effective tool. It's just a little bit of an elevation in the subway step that protects from storm water from running off from the sidewalk, from the street to the sidewalk, and down into the subway stairs. And the manhole covers at the 28th Street station that looked like mini geysers just two weeks ago during the storms, they have since been welded shut. And unnoticeable under this bench and bike rack, an elevated drain also designed to redirect water from flowing down into the subway system. These are our main surface mitigations. We do have the pumping system. And there are other water mitigation measures like catch drains from the street and drains along the tracks. title: How to change video aspect ratio in Adobe Express
transcription: How to resize a video in Adobe Express. If you created a vertical video and want to change it to horizontal, you can do it very easily in Adobe Express. There is a resize tool, which I showed in a different video, but now I want to show you how to do it inside a project you already have, so you don't need to download and upload it again just to use the resize tool. Open the video project you created. Now you have pages in the project. Each page is a separate video. So if you have different clips on different pages, you need to resize each one separately. If you did it by accident and you want all the pages to be in the same video with different dimensions, then you need to combine them all together. Starting with one page as an example. Click on the page of the video, then click on resize at the top of the scene window. Find in the list of options the new dimension you want to change to. You can change it to whatever dimension you like. But if you need it for socials, choose one of the ready-made dimensions listed there. You have the option to resize in the current project or create a new project with the new dimensions, while the original project stays untouched. Now, if you want to change the whole video and it's split into separate pages, you can open a new page or use one of the pages you already have. Then go to the timeline by clicking it. You'll see only the timeline for that one page. The others are separate from this video. For easier access, open the same project in a different window. Now, click the other pages, open the timeline, and copy all the scenes in that video clip. Then go to the other window where you opened the first video page, add a new scene, and paste the video here. Now click resize, and you can resize the whole video like you did for the single page. When you resize the video, you only resize the window that shows the video. If you want to see the full video again or change its position, you can resize it manually inside the new dimension or resize it back to the full video as it was before changing the dimensions. To make it easier when you want to create the same video in different dimensions, you can duplicate the page where you have the full video you want to resize. Click the three dots and choose duplicate page. Now you have the same video twice in the same dimensions. Click the new page and go to the timeline of that page, although you can change dimensions from here too without opening the timeline. Click resize and change the dimensions for that video. You can change the position of the video clips inside to show the right part of the scene. When you go back to pages, you now have the same video twice and you can download them as separate videos with different dimensions. If you'd like to learn more tricks using the video editing tools in Adobe Express, then watch this video next. Like and subscribe, and I'll see you next time.

title: The CEO of Meta, Mark Zuckerberg announces that developing superintelligence is "now in sight"
transcription: Alright, you ready? Hey everyone. I want to talk about our new effort, Meta Super Intelligence Labs, and our vision to build personal super intelligence for everyone. AI keeps accelerating, and over the past few months, we've begun to see glimpses of AI systems improving themselves. So developing super intelligence is now in sight. But there's this big open question about what we should direct super intelligence towards. A lot has been written about the scientific and economic advances that AI can bring. And I'm really optimistic about this. But I think an even more meaningful impact in our lives is going to come from everyone having a personal super intelligence that helps you achieve your goals, create what you want to see in the world, be a better friend and grow to become the person that you aspire to be. This vision is different from others in the industry who want to direct AI at automating all of the valuable work. At Meta, we believe in putting the power of super intelligence in people's hands to direct it towards what they value in their own lives. Some of this will be about improving productivity, but a lot of it may be more personal in nature. This is going to be a new era in some ways, but in others, it's just a continuation of historical trends. About 200 years ago, 90% of people were farmers growing food to survive. Today, fewer than 2% grow all of our food. Advances in technology have freed freed much of humanity to focus less on subsistence and more on the pursuits that we choose. And at each step along the way, most people have decided to use their new found productivity to spend more time on creativity, culture, relationships and just enjoying life. And I expect super intelligence to accelerate this trend even more. The intersection of technology and culture is where Meta focuses, and this will only become more important over time. If trends continue, I expect that people will spend less time on productivity software and more time creating and connecting. I think that personal devices like glasses that can see what we see, hear what we hear, and interact with us throughout the day are going to become our main computing devices. I believe deeply in building personal super intelligence for everyone. And at meta, we have the resources to build a massive infrastructure required and the ability to deliver new technology to billions of people. I am excited to build this future, and we've got a lot more to come soon.

transcription: I didn't come to Bali to film it. I came to feel it. These shots aren't produced. They're moments unfolding in real time right in front of me. Even the most beautiful of moments fade with time. That's why I always bring my camera. title: Can I Take a Self-Guided Tour at Harvard University? | Everything About Boston
transcription: Can I take a self-guided tour at Harvard University? Attention, everyone. A hot topic among visitors to Boston is whether you can take a self-guided tour at the prestigious Harvard University. As travel resumes and curiosity about historic campuses grows, many are eager to know their options for experiencing this iconic institution. If you are planning a trip to Boston and want to explore Harvard at your own pace, you are in the right place. Yes, you can take a self-guided tour at Harvard University. The university offers a free mobile application that provides a self-guided walking tour through Harvard Yard. This app highlights the history of important buildings, traditions, and notable alumni. It allows visitors to explore the campus flexibly and at their own pace. In addition to the self-guided option, Harvard also offers free student-led public walking tours. These tours last about 45 to 60 minutes and provide historical background, general information, and perspectives on student life. However, these tours are scheduled and requiring advanced registration. There are limits on group sizes and check-in is necessary. For those who prefer to explore independently, the mobile application is the main resource available. It is particularly useful for visitors who arrive late to the in-person tours. The Harvard University Visitor Center is located at the Smith Campus Center on Massachusetts Avenue in Cambridge. It is open Monday through Friday from 9:00 in the morning to 5:00 in the evening. This center serves as the starting point for tours and is a resource for visitors with questions about the campus. Harvard is easily accessible by public transit, making it a popular destination for those interested in Boston's rich academic and cultural environment. The self-guided tour app allows visitors to experience Harvard Yard and its surroundings while fitting well into a day spent exploring Cambridge and Boston. To summarize, self-guided tours are available via a free Harvard mobile application focused on Harvard Yard. Official student-led tours requiring advanced registration and have group size limits. The visitor center is the main hub for tour information and visitor assistance. Visitors arriving late to scheduled tours can opt for self-guided alternatives. This setup provides visitors to Boston and Cambridge with multiple ways to experience Harvard University, whether through guided or independent exploration.

title: Northeastern AutoRAN Demo - MWC 2025 - AI-RAN Coexistence
transcription: In this demo, researchers at Northeastern University show how the Auto run framework developed as part of a national telecommunications and Information Administration, NTIA, award for the wireless Innovation Fund can be used to automate AI run coexistence and testing. We will show how to enable AI and run coexistence, validate workloads continuously, and adapt compute resources to the task. This dashboard presents a system view with components that combine northeastern open 6G capabilities, Z touch network software, and key site testing equipment. It allows automated deployment of Orun components from high-level intents, including Ricks, CUs, DUs, on an AI run cluster deployed at Northeastern University with real RUs or testing software from Keyside. It also hosts a set of AI services, like this LLM run configurator. This Gen AI application runs on the AI run cluster and can deploy our test run components starting from high-level intents. For example, here we ask to deploy an Nvidia aerial and OIDU. While an LLM identifies the necessary configurations, we monitor GPU utilization on the top left. Once the LLM completes its task, the intent is translated into a deployment file, like the one that you can see here. This is automatically deployed in a pod in the Auto run cluster, as displayed in this animation. Automated tests can then be performed using Auto run and keysite software. Here we are displaying the keysite Atlas dashboard running a test on the DU. The test connects multiple UEs, as you can see on the keysite Corsim dashboard and DU logs. We then monitor system performance with a dashboard that shows uplink, cell, and downlight performance. Up to 25 UEs connect to the cell, exchanging 65 Mbps in downlink. At the center, we observe the total cell throughput and the GPU and CPU utilization. This test shows that the system, even if deployed on a virtualized cluster, can manage a high number of active users. At the same time, the GPU utilization is not 100%, showing the potential of AI and run coexistence. Here, specifically, we dynamically schedule different applications on different GPUs in the same cluster. This is an example. It is a chatbot where we can ask questions on the Orun specifications. As you can see, once again, the GPU utilization appears on the top left. Once we receive an answer, we can query the sources that can be used to verify whether the answer is correct or not, depending on the specifications. This represents another component of the Autorun framework, showcased at MWC 2025 as one of the AI run Alliance demos.

title: Harvard vs. Trump: What’s the Real Threat?
uploader: Under Color of Law with Shan Wu
transcription: A little bit of background. What they call the procedural posture of this case is that we are years away from a trial. I mean, Trump's claiming there was just a trial. It's utterly wrong. Um, big surprise. It's something they call summary judgment. That's the posture of the case and that's the vehicle for the judge listening to this. Now, you wouldn't necessarily know that from the mainstream media coverage as well because they're also saying the whole thing could be resolved right now, and it won't be. It's in a very early stage. And we haven't even gotten into the really laborious and time-consuming civil litigation process known as discovery, which can take years, consume thousands of hours of lawyers. So, in the summary judgment posture, what's important for us to keep in mind is what is the legal standard. And the name summary judgment suggests kind of what it is, which is it's a quick judgment based on the summary of the case thus far. What does that mean legally? Here's the legal standard to win. There cannot be any material facts in dispute and given that there are no material facts in dispute, one side wins just based on the law. Here's a little bit of me explaining this uh on a recent CNN hit. We'll just let you hear that for one one moment. It's not a trial yet. It's before trial and something called a motion for summary judgment. So the legal standard for that is actually very tricky. It means that for the judge to rule as a matter of law that somebody's going to win, they got to first find there's no real material facts in dispute. So obviously there's going to be a lot of maneuvering as to say, you know, what is a material fact, is it in dispute or not? So you can find that whole discussion um on our Undercover of Law YouTube channel, which I hope you'll also subscribe to, but you can take a look there for the full interview. The CNN graphic there does a good job of summarizing some of Harvard's main legal arguments, but misses a couple as well. If you apply the summary judgment standard, you might be inclined to think, gee, how can there be no facts in dispute? And you'd be right in a sense because most cases are about facts being in dispute. But that's where the lawyering comes in, the framing of the facts, so to speak. So here, the Trump administration, for example, is screaming that Harvard is anti-Semitic, which of course Harvard denies. But that dispute doesn't mean Harvard can't win on summary judgment because Harvard's point would be that that fact does not matter right now, whether there was any anti-semitism or not, because the Trump administration froze funds without ever getting to the point of proving that allegation. That allegation would be discrimination, of course, would be a violation of title 6 of the Civil Rights Act, which is what the Trump administration alleges.

title: Sony A7S IV in 2025: Game Changer or Generational Miss? (A7S III vs FX3 vs ZV-E1)
transcription: Welcome to my channel Techset Go. The way has been long and the silence frustrating, but now the buzz is getting louder. After years of nothing but speculation, it finally feels like Sony is preparing to launch one of its most important cameras yet. It's the A7S4. This isn't just another camera update. It's more than a spec bump. It's a response, a statement, a move that could redefine where Sony stands in the world of hybrid video creation. And it couldn't come at a more critical time. The A7S3 came out in 2020. Back then, it felt like the future. Full frame 4K at 120 frames per second, in-body stabilization, incredible autofocus, great color, solid low light performance. For YouTubers, filmmakers and content creators, it was exactly what they needed. But time moves fast. Since then, the camera world has changed. Canon, Panasonic, and even Nikon have been stepping up fast. Cameras now shoot raw internally. Some offer 8K, some bring hybrid designs that challenge even cinema cameras. And Sony, Sony has been quiet when it comes to the S-line, too quiet. The A7R series got updated, the A7C series expanded. The flagship A1 is due for its second generation. The FX line continues to grow, but the S series, Sony's video powerhouse, has been sitting still for 5 years. That's why everyone's looking at the A7S4 now, because Sony needs to answer back. So, what can we expect from this long-ided camera? Let's start with the sensor. Rumors say Sony is sticking with the 12 megapixel full-frame idea. That might sound underwhelming in a world where 40 and 60 megapixels are common, but that's exactly the point. Lower resolution means bigger pixels, and bigger pixels mean better light sensitivity. The S series has always been about low light. It's its identity. That's what creators love it for. Night shoots, concerts, city streets, documentary work, places where lighting is bad, but the story still matters. Now, will it be the same old sensor? Almost definitely not. title: SXSW EDU PanelPicker -  Rooted Leadership: Two-Gen Model for Growing Educators
transcription: What if the future of education leadership isn't a pipeline, but a root system? At all in education, we're proving what's possible when you grow leadership from within communities. This initiative is powered by Parent Educator Academy alumni. Our parents have already demonstrated leadership. It's inherent in who they are. Our work is just to give them the training and the support to continue to grow as leaders. Through our sustainable leadership initiative, we're transforming parents and caregivers into education professionals. Our two-week summer institute resulted in 100% of our parents receiving job offers. The long-term goal with this initiative is to continue to upskill our parent educators. We want them to have the tools and the strategies to be highly effective education professionals, and at the end of this four years, they can become the teacher of record and obtain a Spo certification and a degree. This initiative is about more than just jobs. It's a two-generational approach to to address our education workforce challenges while giving parents and caregivers access to social and economic mobility for their families. In this session, we'll walk you through the ins and outs of this model. How we went from parent engagement to leadership development, and how we partnered with the Roosevelt School District and the Arizona K-12 Center to develop a training that effectively meets our education workforce needs. You'll leave this session with a framework that you can adapt and strategies to build your own sustainable leadership from within your communities and ideas to rethink workforce development in a way that lasts. Let's stop building pipelines and start nurturing our community roots.

title: Trump's Epstein Mystery Deepens | New Epstein-Trump Footage Sparks Questions | TSW News #tswnews
transcription: Newly uncovered photos and video footage from the 1990s have reignited public interest and controversy over Donald Trump's long speculated ties to Zefrey Epstein. Among the fresh evidence, a 1993 photo of Epstein attending Trump's wedding to Marla Maples confirmed for the first time through contact sheets captured by society photographer David Jones. I wish now I took more of him with Trump, Jones admitted in an interview with CNN after noticing Epstein entering the Plaza Hotel that evening. CNN's archival drive also turned up unseen raw footage from a 1999 Victoria's Secret fashion show, where Trump and Epstein are seen laughing and conversing ahead of the event. The clip, filmed years before Epstein's crimes became public, adds to a growing collection of visuals, placing the two men together, including appearances at high society events in 1992, 1997, and 2000. often alongside controversial figures like Ghilane Maxwell and Prince Andrew. The revelations land at a politically sensitive moment. Trump supporters, many of whom have demanded full transparency in the Epstein case, are now expressing outrage at the Justice Department's delay in releasing sealed documents. Meanwhile, a 2003 birthday card allegedly signed by Trump, bearing a naked women's silhou and the line, May every day be another wonderful secret has surfaced in a Wall Street Journal report. Trump has denied its authenticity and sued the publication for libel. When questioned about the new photos, Trump hung up on CNN calling the outlet fake news. As a spokesperson, Steven Chung insisted the visuals are out of context frame grabs from public events and reiterated that Trump banned Epstein from Mar A Lago calling him a creep. Yet the frequency and informality of their past encounters suggests a closer relationship than previously acknowledged, especially before their reported falling out in the mid 2000s over a Palm Beach real estate deal. Adding to the intrigue, the Justice department has now reached out to Gillane Maxwell for a potential meeting amid backlash over Epstein files. Her lawyer has stated that she is willing to testify truthfully and even thanked Trump for his commitment to uncovering the truth. a statement that has further stirred speculation. As the photos circulate and pressure builds on the DOJ to unseal long- promised records, one thing is clear. The Trump Epstein connection, once dismissed as a footnote is back in the spotlight and raising more questions than ever. For more updates, subscribe to our YouTube channel TSW News. title: Amazon Just Bought Bee Should You Be Worried?
transcription: Hey, you remember when I said I backed B because it respected our privacy? Well, Amazon just bought B, that always listening AI assistant I've been talking about. But hold up. This is the company that let Ring share your video with police, sometimes without warrants, and employees snooping on privacy footage. So now Amazon owns the device that hears everything you say. That's wild. Let that sink in. You know what B does? Converts chats into text and memories into reminders. It helps you recall moments you'd otherwise forget. I've been saying it for years, there's a thin line between convenience and privacy. Everyone has to decide where that line is for themselves. Security has always been my priority. But I worry a lot that people will get swept up by the benefits and forget they're risking something. Once privacy is out, like opening Pandora's box, you can't put it back. That thought really scares me, especially right now. Here's what I've done and what you can do. I've reached out to the founders, Maria and Ethan, asking them to delete my B data before the Amazon deal closes. Why? Their original terms, privacy first, no audio stored, you control the data, were under their vision. Now it's Amazon? That shifts everything. Here's my advice. Delete your data through the app now before it transfers. After the acquisition, reread the new terms. Decide if you're okay with Amazon having access, even just transcripts. We all get to choose where our privacy line is. For me, it's control over my voice, not negotiable. One last thing. This isn't just about B. It's part of a bigger tech race. Amazon is doubling down on always on AI. Just like Apple, Meta, Open AI, with wearables becoming the next battleground. The convenience is tempting, instant reminders, memory help, hands-free assistance, but popping open that convenience could mean your private life ends up on display. Pandora's box gets opened and there's no putting it back. Here's what matters now. Delete your B data before the acquisition closes. Reread those new terms. Decide if you're okay with letting Amazon access your voice, even just transcripts. Your privacy, your choice. Like this or want more no fluff tech breakdowns? Hit like, subscribe and drop a comment. Until next time.

title: 64th annual World Eskimo and Indian Olympics wraps up
transcription: After four days of festivities, the World Eskimo Indian Olympics are wrapping up in Fairbanks. This year's event saw world records broken, a crowd a crown passed, and a community gathered to celebrate indigenous culture. Adrian Peterson and Alex Bengal were there today and give us a roundup of the week. The fourth and final day of the 64th annual WEO has arrived. Here at the Carlson Center in Fairbanks, this year's WEO games featured more than 20 competitive events from the four-man carry to the bench reach. Sportsmanship and camaraderie were displayed throughout the games as athletes faced difficult feats. Honestly, I think one foot and two foot are the most challenging if I'm going to be honest. I feel like you know, jumping and then kicking the ball is was a lot for me. Despite the strain and skill testing tasks, newcomers and veteran athletes alike found success during the games with one athlete beating his very own world record on the first day. You just got to have the confidence. Confidence, put the consistency in your practices. Oh, definitely work out a lot and you know, you're you're confident because how are you going to perform if you put in all the work? But the event was about more than sports. It was a chance for the community to get together and for people from around the state and the world to share their culture. Regalia contests with contestants ages 6 months and up showed off unique and elaborate use of hide and cloth. Regalia is really our way to be able to honor our the animals who allowed us to um hunt them. And then also our family, because like I said, it's a family effort. A lot of the patterns are specific to families. Throughout the games, the arena was filled with tables for people to display and sell handmade arts and crafts, made with love and care from all kinds of materials. It's also really healing for your soul, like just sitting there and just healing with your ancestors who were there before you. And a new Miss Wio was crowned Friday night, Jolie Carlson from Bethel and Quetlook. We're still here. We still have our cultures, we still have our traditions, we still have our languages, we know who we are. And it's all still intact and it will be for generations to come. A community gathering to keep culture alive and to pass their knowledge and skills on to the next generation. Adrian Peterson and Alex Bengal, Alaska's News Source.

title: FIRST LOOK: iPhone 17 Pro Max Hands-On Review!
transcription: The Apple rumor community is currently dealing with a fresh scandal involving a leaker who is attempting to make money off of conjecture rather than a new iPhone 17 feature or design. Imagine Buu, a well-known Apple leaker who amassed a following of over 75,000 followers on X, previously Twitter, mostly via repeating speculations, is now trying to sell iPhone 17 Max covers months before Apple makes the phone's formal announcement. The 10 designs of cases, which include transparent, tough, hybrid, and shield varieties, are priced between $39.99 and $54.99, and are advertised as ready to ship. What's wrong? These covers might not fit the actual iPhone 17 when it is launched because its design and dimensions have not yet been verified. The leaker's web store's ambiguous details increase the risk. Whether the cases are pre-orders or the estimated time of delivery are not specified. The promise that someone will contact them within 24 hours to confirm their purchase raises concerns for many customers. While some casemakers use CAD files or prototypes to gain a head start, early accessory launches based on leaks are not new. However, history demonstrates how dangerous this can be. For instance, manufacturers used to build large quantities of covers for an iPhone that was reported to have a teardrop design but never made it to market. Customers might easily lose their money on these items, which are gambles without official Apple data. According to Imagine Buu, the cases are created by a business called Leo, which can create personalized cases in 20 days and is said to have 21 years of experience. But without Apple's approval, even the slightest change to the design may make these cases pointless. In addition to the financial risk to purchasers, Imagine Boo's reputation is at risk with this action. Like Lee Supro, who previously made a bogus claim to have been inside Apple Park during a lockdown, and other discredited characters in the past, they appear to be using their followers for financial gain rather than offering confirmed leaks or insightful observations. Despite their imperfections, reliable sources like Ming Chi Kuo and Mark Gurman depend on verified research and intimate knowledge rather than resharing online rumors. Not making money off of leaks, many people do it on YouTube or blogs, but advertising and selling speculative goods with no assurance of truth is the issue. Pushing iPhone 17 covers before the phone is even available is inappropriate in this situation. Finally, what are your thoughts about it? So without being said, let me know your thought in the comment below. And if you are new here, please subscribe. Peace out.

title: How to record a Google Slides Lesson Presentation with audio and video [2025 Easy Guide]
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to record a Google Slides presentation with both audio and video. Whether you opt to use the built-in recording feature in Google Slides or prefer to work with a versatile screen recording tool like Screencastify or Loom, I'll guide you through the process step-by-step to ensure you can effectively capture your presentation. Let's start by exploring Google Slides built-in recording feature. First, head over to slides.google.com and open the presentation you want to record. Once you're all set with your slides, look towards the top right corner of the interface. You'll notice a record button, easily identifiable by its circle within a circle icon. Click on this to move into the recording options. Upon clicking, select record new video to prepare for capturing your presentation. Now you can click the red record button, signaling the start of your recording session. At any time, should you need a break or wish to restart from a particular point, you're in control. You can pause and re-record as needed. Once satisfied, you can stop the recording and save it directly to your Google Drive for easy access and sharing. While setting up, manage your camera and microphone settings. Decide if you want them on or off, adjusting the picture and picture to your desired size and position on the screen for a personalized touch. Next, let's shift our focus to using an external screen recording tool. If you're opting for this, you'll start by choosing a tool such as Screencastify or Loom. These tools are great if you want more flexibility and functionality. After selecting your tool, set up your recording area. Choose either the full screen or a specific window that's most relevant to your presentation. Double check to make sure both your microphone and camera are selected and ready to roll. When everything is set, commence recording your presentation and narrate as you go along. This way, the viewers can effortlessly follow your explanations alongside the visuals. Once you're done, simply stop the recording and save your video. It's worth mentioning some key differences and considerations between these methods. Using Google slides's built-in feature tends to be more straightforward as it's specifically designed for recording presentations with the camera and audio. On the other hand, screen recording tools stand out in terms of flexibility. They offer various recording options and sophisticated editing features that give you numerous possibilities to enhance your presentation, like trimming the video or adding annotations. Regardless of which method you choose, paying attention to audio quality is crucial. Always consider using a high-quality microphone to ensure your narration is clear and impactful. Finally, if you decide to use screen recording tools, you'll often find editing features built right in, which allow you to tweak and perfect your recording to a professional standard. Now you're equipped with the knowledge to effectively record your Google slides presentation. Enjoy the process and create something amazing.

Next, ensure that you have enabled Bluetooth on your Apple Watch. Also, make sure that AirPods or Bluetooth earbuds are in pairing mode. Steps to enter pairing mode differ from earbud to earbud. Finally, if nothing seems to work, then try resetting your AirPods. To reset the AirPods 4, you need to double tap three times on the status light till it flashes amber. title: ByteDance mass food poisoning case: Judge fines caterer S$7,000, criticises its complacency
transcription: A catering company was fined 7,000 Sing dollars after a mass food poisoning incident at a Bitedance corporate event. The judge slammed the company's complacency and gave a higher fine than what prosecutors sought. Yun Hai Yao, which runs the Yunan's restaurant chain, pleaded guilty to food safety breaches. Aslam Shah reports. The judge described the number of victims as staggering and criticized Yun Hai Yao for complacency saying it was fortunate that no one died. At court, Yun Hai Yao was represented by CEO Luther Tau who acknowledged the company's failure to manage its risk in their first corporate catering service. What began as a routine lunch for Bite Dance staff last July, turned into a serious health scare. After eating wok-fried diced chicken from Yun Hai Yao, 171 people fell ill with 60 hospitalized and 22 requiring overnight stays. Tests showed the chicken contained bacteria that caused food poisoning at over 2,000 times the legal limit. Inspectors also found live cockroaches at Yun Hai Yao's North Point City outlet where the food was prepared. Since then, Yun Hai Yao has permanently closed the outlet, stopped all corporate catering, retrained staff, and hired external food safety experts. The company issued a public apology and are in talks with Bite Dance about compensating those affected.

title: They Thought It Was Just a Gas Station — Until They Tasted the BBQ
transcription: At first glance, this looks like your average gas station on a quiet corner in Kansas City. But step inside and you'll find ribs, brisket, and a barbecue sandwich so legendary, it once made Anthony Bourdain's list of places to eat before you die. It all started with a man named Jeff Steny. Just a regular guy with a serious love for barbecue. In the early 1990s, he and his wife Joy began competing in barbecue contests around the country, under the name Slaughterhouse 5. They didn't just enter competitions, they dominated them. In 1993, they won the Grand Championship at the American Royal, the Super Bowl of barbecue. With their reputation growing, the Steny's decided to open a restaurant. But instead of some flashy new building, they picked something unexpected. A working gas station at 47th and Mission. Yes, they literally served brisket next to gas pumps. No frills, no fancy, just honest, slow-smoked barbecue. Orders started flying in. And in 2009, food legend Anthony Bourdain called Joe's one of the 13 places to eat before you die. What made it so special? Maybe it's the slow-smoked meats. Maybe it's the Z-Man sandwich, tender brisket topped with onion rings and provolone. Or maybe, it's the story. Joe's isn't just a restaurant. It's a reminder that greatness can come from the humblest places. That passion, patience, and a whole lot of smoke can turn a gas station into a bucket list destination. If you go, head to the original location, 47th and Mission. Get there early, lines form fast. Locals swear by the Z-Man and the burnt ends. And yes, it's worth the wait. Joe's Kansas City barbecue began with a dream and a smoker in a gas station. And it became one of the most legendary barbecue joints in America. Because sometimes, the best places are the ones you'd never expect.

title: How To Show All Event Details In Google Calendar [2026 Guide]
transcription: In today's video, I'm going to teach you how to show all event details in Google Calendar. This can be particularly useful if you need to collaborate with others, share all the intricate details of your schedule, or simply ensure that nothing gets overlooked. To get started, head over to your Google Calendar. You can do this by opening a new tab and navigating to the Google Calendar website. Once you have your calendar open, you'll notice a list of your calendars on the left-hand side under my calendars. What you'll want to do first is locate the specific calendar that you'd like to share. Now, once you've identified the right calendar, move your cursor over it. You'll see three vertical dots appearing next to it. Go ahead and give those dots a click. A small menu will pop up, and from this list, you'll want to select settings and sharing. This leads you to where you can adjust your calendar preferences to suit your needs. Once you're in the settings, scroll down a bit until you find the section labeled access permissions for events. This section is key to your task. Here, you'll need to check the box that says make available to public. As soon as you do this, a warning dialogue box will pop up. Now, don't worry, this is just a notification letting you know that you're about to make your calendar publicly accessible. If you're comfortable with that, simply go ahead and click okay to proceed. With that done, you'll see a small dropdown arrow next to the option you just enabled. Click on this arrow and you'll be presented with a couple of options. Select see all event details to ensure that anyone who has access to your calendar can view all the specifics of your events. To make sharing even simpler, you have the option to create a shareable calendar link. Just click on get shareable link, then click copy link. With this link, you can easily share your calendar with others whenever needed. Additionally, if there are specific people or groups you'd like to share your calendar with, you'll want to look for the shared with section. Click on add people and groups, and a new, new window will pop up allowing you to enter the email address of the person you'd like to share your calendar with. After you've entered their email, click on the permission drop down next to it. In the dropdown menu, select see all event details to allow them to view the complete details of your events. Finally, click on send to notify them about the shared calendar. And there you have it. By following these steps, you've successfully configured your Google calendar to show all event details, making it easier to collaborate and communicate with others. Thank you for watching.

title: Samsung Galaxy S25 FE – First Live Look & Major Upgrades!
transcription: So, after the previous renders from OnLeaks, we now have the first real life look at the much awaited Galaxy S25 FE. This shows one feature that it shares with the Galaxy S series, plus there are two big upgrades coming to the Galaxy S25 FE. Let's talk all about this. So, this live image of the Galaxy S25 FE is pretty much official, and here's why. It comes directly from the Wireless Power Consortium, the global body that certifies wireless charging devices. And yes, they've just officially certified the S25 FE for Qi2 wireless charging, a first for the FE series. Until now, this was something only Samsung's flagship S series offered. So for anyone who cares about faster, reliable wireless charging, this is great news. The live image itself also reveals a couple of interesting things. First, there's new deep blue color option. And second, the camera design now matches the upcoming Galaxy S25 Edge, making the S25 FE look a lot more premium this time around. We can't see the bezels here, but leaks says they're also getting noticeably slimmer, giving you more screen and a cleaner modern look. Overall, it looks like Samsung is finally giving the FE lineup some real flagship treatment. So, recently a user on X, Abhishek Yadav, shared some fresh Geekbench scores, including OpenCL and AI benchmarks, which pretty much confirm that the Galaxy S25 FE will come with the Exynos 2400 chip. At first, you might think Samsung is launching the same thing this year, right? Well, S24 FE and flagship S24 came with Exynos 2400e and Exynos 2400. But still, S24 had better battery life, even with just 4,000 mAh compared to 4,700 mAh on S24 FE. Performance on the S24 FE wasn't bad, but the battery life did fall short of the regular S24, even with a bigger battery. That's mainly because it used a toned-down version of Exynos 2400. So with the full Exynos 2400 this time, we should see a noticeable boost in battery performance. Some leaks says it could get 5,000 mAh battery. If true, we will see massive battery backup on S25 FE. Coming to biggest upgrade, Galaxy S25 FE is coming with a flagship grade flexible OLED display. And here's why that's actually a big deal. So, what does flexible OLED really mean? Unlike regular OLED panels, which are thicker and rigid, flexible OLEDs are much slimmer and lighter. That's exactly why the Galaxy S25 FE could be significantly thinner this year, reportedly just 7.4 mm compared to about 8 mm on the S24 FE. Interestingly, that makes it almost as slim as the S25+, which is just 7.3 mm. The result, a slicker design, lighter feel in the hand, and overall more premium look and feel. Something we rarely see in Samsung's FE series. As the day is getting closer, we're getting more and more reliable updates. So, stay tuned for more. I'll break it all down for you and make it clear about the S25 FE. Stay tuned for more updates. Peace out.

title: The best marketing at London Marathon 2025
transcription: The London Marathon from pure race to brand playground. Once upon a time, the London Marathon was a straightforward celebration of running. Thousands of runners shared a goal and a spirit for the sport. But fast forward to 2025, it's a whole different marathon. A stage where brands flex their creative muscles as much as the runners do theirs. Take New Balance, for example. They didn't just sponsor the marathon, they created an entire townhouse near Regent Street. Runners could customize their gear, attend motivational talks, and feel like part of an exclusive community. However, not all brand activations hit the mark this year. Nike's never again until next year billboard campaign intended to resonate with runners. Their sentiment post-marathon sparked significant controversy. The phrase never again is deeply associated with the Holocaust remembrance, and its use in this context was seen by many as trivializing a solemn vow. Nike issued an apology, stating that the intent was to motivate runners based on common phrases used in the world of running, but acknowledged the oversight and removed the billboards. This incident underscores the fine lines brands walk when integrating into cultural events. It raises the question, has all this branding overshadowed the essence of the marathon? There's no denying that today's races are as much about social media moments and brand storytelling as they are about the run itself. Every corner turned is another Instagrammable moment. Every mile marker is a brand opportunity, adding to the tapestry of brand engagements. Pure sport, for example, introduced a unique hotel room service. In the days leading up to the marathon, they offered a surprise delivery service to runners staying in London hotels. Participants who signed up via Pure Sports Instagram received recovery kits delivered directly to their rooms. These kits included hydration sachets, magnesium supplements, and marathon socks, essentials designed to aid performance and recovery. Yet, there is a flip side. These brand activations bring fresh eyes to the sport. They attract new runners and allow brands to push creative boundaries. The marathon is no longer just a race. It is a bit of a cultural phenomenon that merges sport, creativity, and community. And in the end, the London Marathon 2025 is a reflection of our times. It's not just about crossing the finish line, but also about the stories told along the way. And perhaps that's not such a bad thing after all. I'd be keen to hear your point of view on this. Do you feel that it is a big brand opportunity to spend some cash and make moves? Or is it for the reasons greater than that? Please do drop your comments below, and don't forget to like and subscribe for more stories into the world of sport and culture surrounding us.

title: The 1950s Soviet Humanoid: The VDNKh Robot | Stellar Tech
transcription: The heliopause is shocking. The VDNKH robot emerged from the Soviet Union's ambitious vision of a future where humanoid machines would work alongside humans in industry and daily life. Displayed at Moscow's exhibition of achievements of national economy in 1959, this early humanoid robot captured imaginations and demonstrated Soviet technological prowess during the height of the Cold War. Standing 1.8 meters tall, the VDNKH robot could execute 18 different commands via radio control, including basic movements, gestures, and responses to light and sound stimuli. Its sophisticated control system allowed operators to demonstrate complex sequences that mimicked human behavior, creating an illusion of artificial intelligence that amazed exhibition visitors. The robot's design philosophy reflected Soviet optimism about technological progress. Engineers envisioned a future where such machines would perform dangerous industrial tasks, assist in space exploration, and support human workers in various capacities. The VDNKH robot served as both a technological demonstration and a propaganda tool, showcasing Soviet innovation in emerging fields like cybernetics and automation. Performance demonstrations occurred every two hours on a specially constructed stage in front of the electrification pavilion. The robot's ability to see and hear through primitive sensors created an interactive experience that seemed decades ahead of its time. Audiences watched in amazement as the machine responded to commands and environmental stimuli with human-like movements. While primitive compared to modern robotics, the VDNKH robot played a crucial role in Soviet technological development. It inspired a generation of engineers and scientists while demonstrating that human machine collaboration was not just science fiction, but an achievable goal through dedicated engineering and innovation.

title: Balochistan Dark reality ethnic violence unveiled
transcription: I want to talk about something that's rarely discussed, but urgently needs our attention, Balochistan. Over the past year, the province has witnessed a shocking rise in violence, but what's truly horrifying is the pattern behind it. Baloch separatist groups, especially the BLA, aren't just fighting for political goals, they're targeting Punjabis. Innocent laborers, truck drivers, fathers and sons, pulled off buses and executed, simply for their identity. In August 2024 alone, over 70 people, most of them Punjabi civilians, lost their lives in coordinated attacks. This isn't just terrorism, it's hatred, rooted in language and ethnicity. And let's be clear, targeting the powerless, those who work far from home just to feed their families, is an act of pure cowardice. Yes, Balochistan is rich in resources, but poor in opportunity. Economic projects have brought outsiders in, creating tension. But does that justify murder? Absolutely not. The state, for its part, has promised action, but the cycle of violence, militant attacks, then harsh crackdowns only breeds more resentment. Ordinary people are caught in the crossfire, living in fear. So, what's the answer? Justice, yes, swift, fair justice, but also unity. We need to stand together, speak out against all forms of hate, and demand peace for Balochistan. Because as long as we let hatred divide us, nobody wins. Let's raise our voices. Let's demand an end to this tragedy. #StopBalochistanViolence.

First up, Dotonbori, Osaka's entertainment hotspot, famous for its glowing neon lights, street food, and bustling energy. It's the perfect place to taste Takoyaki and soak in the city's nightlife. One of the largest aquariums in the world, Osaka Aquarium Kaiyukan lets you walk through a stunning underwater world featuring marine creatures from across the Pacific Ocean. Step back in time at Osaka Castle, a historic icon of Japan, surrounded by cherry blossoms in spring. It's a beautiful blend of power and peace. Fashion lovers, this is your paradise. Shinsaibashisuji offers a mix of modern boutiques, traditional shops, and endless options for every style. Take a break in Osaka Castle Park, a tranquil escape with scenic views, perfect for a picnic or peaceful stroll around nature and history. Enjoy breathtaking views from the Kuchu Teien observatory atop the Umeda Sky building. See all of Osaka from the sky, especially magical at sunset. Feeling hungry? Head to Kuromon Market, also known as Osaka's Kitchen, where you'll find fresh local food, sushi, and street snacks that'll make your mouth water. Discover the spiritual side of Osaka at Sumiyoshi Taisha Shrine, one of Japan's oldest Shinto shrines, known for its iconic bridge and peaceful atmosphere. Minami, also known as Namba, is Osaka's beating heart, full of energy, fashion, food, and fun. It's where tradition meets modern life. An architectural wonder, the Umeda Sky building is not just for the views. It's also a great spot for photos, dining, and seeing the city sparkle at night. Travel back in time at the Osaka Museum of Housing and Living, where you can walk through recreated historical streets and learn how people lived centuries ago. transcription: Paul McCartney may be preparing to return to the stage in the United States, with subtle hints suggesting that another leg of his Got Back tour could be on the horizon, possibly beginning as early as this year. On July 9, McCartney sparked speculation with an Instagram story that featured an intriguing image, two guitar picks, one white and one blue. The white pick had his name printed in red lettering, while the blue one read Got Back in 2025 in white text. Alongside the image, he included a link directing fans to a sign-up page on his official website. The post has led many to believe that McCartney is teasing new US tour dates in 2025, signaling a possible continuation of his highly successful Got Back tour. Originally launched in April 2022, the Got Back tour began in Spokane, Washington, and saw McCartney performing across 16 American cities before concluding the US leg in June that same year. He then brought the show to fans in South America and Australia, eventually wrapping things up with a final European stretch. The tour concluded in December 2024 with two grand performances at London's O2 Arena. Concertgoers were treated to a vibrant mix of songs from across McCartney's career, including Beatles classics such as Can't Buy Me Love, Hey Jude, and Let It Be, as well as hits from his Wings era like Band on the Run, and beloved solo tracks including Maybe I'm Amazed. At 83, McCartney continues to command the stage with the same energy and charisma that made him a household name decades ago. The Got Back tour sold over 1 million tickets and reportedly earned close to 200 million in revenue, evidence that his appeal remains as strong as ever. With these latest clues, it appears that the legendary musician may be gearing up for yet another memorable tour across the US, much to the excitement of fans nationwide.

title: The VDNKh Robot, A Marvel of Early AI | Sci & Why
transcription: The VDNKH robot, the Soviet Android dream. Soviet engineers created humanoid robots in the 1950s that could perform 18 different commands, see, hear, and interact with amazed exhibition audiences. The VDNKH robot represented the Soviet Union's early venture into humanoid robotics and technological showmanship. Developed by young technicians under Boris Vasilenko's guidance, these robots were designed to demonstrate Soviet technological capabilities at the famous VDNKH exhibition center in Moscow. The most advanced model stood 1.8 meters tall and could execute 18 different commands via radio control, including movement, gesture recognition, and basic interaction. These robots featured primitive vision and hearing capabilities using sensors to detect light and sound for responsive behavior. The VDNKH robots performed every two hours on a special stage built in front of the electrification pavilion, drawing crowds of amazed visitors. Beyond their mechanical functions, these robots symbolized Soviet optimism about the future, representing a vision where automation would support human progress. The project combined engineering innovation with theatrical presentation, capturing public imagination about human-machine collaboration. Soviet robotics development extended beyond exhibitions. By 1980, the USSR operated over 6,000 industrial robots, representing more than 20% of the world's total. The country pioneered planetary rovers, developing the first lunar rovers and Mars exploration vehicles. While primitive by modern standards, the VDNKH robots played a significant role in robotics history, demonstrating early concepts of autonomous behavior and human-robot interaction that would influence future development.

title: 5 Real Creatures Caught on Camera That Will Freak You Out
transcription: Imagine capturing something on camera that you just can't explain. From eerie forests to murky lakes, these five mysterious creatures have been caught on film and have left everyone asking, What did I just see? Let's dive in. Our first footage comes from a hiker's camera deep in the Appalachian Mountains. As they set up camp for the night, their motion activated camera recorded something slinking through the trees. A tall, shadowy figure with glowing eyes. Some say it's just a trick of the light, but others are convinced it's a creature straight out of local legend. The elusive dark watcher. Next up is a mysterious sighting from Iceland's Lake Lagarfljot. A local fisherman was filming the calm waters when they spotted something writhing under the surface. a long, snakelike shape. The locals call it the Lugerfljot worm, said to be a relative of the Loch Ness monster. The footage is grainy, but it's hard to dismiss how real it looks. In the dense woods of Michigan, a dashcam video from 2017 caught something startling. A creature, half man, half dog, sprinting across the road at an impossible speed. Many locals believe it's the legendary dogman. A werewolf-like beast that's been part of Michigan folklore for over a century. Texas ranchers have long talked about the Chupacabra, a blood-sucking creature that preys on livestock. In 2018, a rancher's security camera captured a gaunt, hairless animal creeping around the property. Experts say it could be a coyote with mange, but some are sure it's the real Chupacabra. And finally, one of the weirdest and most debated videos, the Fresno Nightcrawler. Spotted in California, these leggy, stick-like beings seem to glide effortlessly across lawns at night. Are they ghosts, aliens, or something else entirely? No one knows, but the footage is undeniably strange. These are just a few of the many mysterious creatures that have been caught on camera. title: Turn Your Boarding Pass into the Viral Bald JD Vance Meme Now
transcription:
Are you hungry for the latest news and trends from the internet? Welcome to what's cooking on the internet. Your one stop shop for discovering the hottest digital delights. Hit that subscribe button and let's get cooking. 

Can a viral meme be a form of quiet protest or is it just a silly joke? I think it's a little bit of both. In a world where social media can turn even the most mundane moments into viral sensations, a new app from tech innovator James Steinberg is taking the concept of a meme to new heights. The app lets users change the background of their digital boarding pass to display a now infamous image of Vice President JD Vance as a bald, bearded baby man. It started as a joke, but it's raised some serious questions about freedom of political speech. Steinberg warns users to use at your own risk, but he's already seen hundreds of people use the app to create their own digital boarding passes. The idea for the app came after a Norwegian tourist, Mads Mikkelson, was detained by border control for hours and forced to unlock his phone, which contained the same meme. Mikkelson's entry into the country was denied, and he believed it was due to sensitivities over the doctored likeness of the V. E. Customs and Border Patrol later denied this, claiming that Mikkelson's admitted drug use was the reason for his ejection. Either way, the meme got a lot more traction, raising questions about freedom of political speech. An Irish politician even waved around a printout of the bald Vance meme in parliament while warning of American censorship and repression. In my opinion, it leads to a discussion at the heart of the issue, Steinberg says of his app. But what does this say about our society? Are we using memes as a way to comment on the absurdity of politics, or are we just using them as a way to distract ourselves from the real issues at hand? The project has the approval of Dave McNamee, the creative consultant and humorist in Los Angeles who kicked off the Vance Edits craze back in October of 2024. McName's edits, which included giving Van some more chiseled, Chad-like look, eventually racked up more than 200,000 likes and 16 million views on X. But the real question is, what's the point of all this? Are we using memes as a way to speak truth to power, or are we just using them as a way to mock and belittle those in power? As Steinberg's app continues to spread, it's clear that this is more than just a silly joke. It's a commentary on our society's obsession with social media, our willingness to use memes as a form of protest, and our desire to comment on the absurdity of politics. So, the next time you see a meme, remember, it's not just a joke, it's a reflection of our society's values and priorities.

title: Fix An Apple Watch Stuck On Charging Cable Screen
transcription: Is your Apple Watch stuck showing the charging cable and the red lightning bolt icon? Don't worry. In this video, I will walk you through the simple steps to fix it and get your Apple Watch working again. Let's get started. The charging cable with red bolt icon usually appears on the screen when you connect your Apple Watch to a charger. More often than not, you see the charging cable on the screen when your Apple Watch has detected the charger and is charging. You might see the charging cable on the screen for several minutes if your Apple Watch battery was completely drained. It might take up to 30 minutes for the Apple Watch to get enough charge before it can turn on. During this time, it is recommended that you keep the Apple Watch plugged in and wait for it to turn on automatically. If your Apple Watch has not turned on even after plugging it for more than 30 minutes, then you can follow these steps. Check its charger. First, let's make sure your Apple Watch is actually charging. Use the official Apple magnetic charging cable and plug it into a known good power adapter or USB port. Avoid using third-party cables if possible. Plugging your Apple Watch to your computer and charging it from there can also help. If a computer is not available, try plugging the charger into a different outlet or power brick. Adjust the charger's placement. Next, double check that your Apple Watch is aligned properly on the charger. The back of the watch should be flat against the charging puck, and you should feel a magnetic snap. Clean the charger and the watch. Dirt or debris on the charger or the back of the watch can prevent charging. Use a soft, lint-free cloth to clean both surfaces. Don't use any liquids. Force restart your Apple Watch. If your Apple Watch is unresponsive or stuck on the cable icon, try force restarting it. Press and hold the side button and the digital crown together for about 10 seconds until you see the Apple logo. This should force restart your Apple Watch and it should start charging again. If nothing has worked so far, try using a different Apple Watch charger. If the issue was a faulty cable or charger, your watch might start charging right away. If your Apple Watch still won't charge and stays stuck on the cable screen, then there might be a hardware issue. Visit an Apple store or go to your nearest Apple authorized repair center to get your Apple Watch fixed. And that's it. I hope one of these tips helped fix your Apple Watch charging issue. If it did, be sure to hit the like button and subscribe for more Apple tips and tricks. Thanks for watching.

title: GIANT SHARK Filmed in New York! Rare Footage of the World's Largest Shark
transcription: Our journey today took us to New York. There, our drone captured a rare scene, a giant shark emerging with its mouth wide open, filtering the ocean like an ancient vacuum. We quickly descended for a closer look, and to our surprise, it was him. The whale shark. The largest shark in the world. Despite its colossal size, reaching over 59 ft in length and weighing up to 44,000 lbs, the whale shark is a gentle giant. Its mouth, which can span up to 5 ft wide, isn't made for biting, but for filtering seawater in search of plankton, small fish, and the eggs of other species. Its skin, covered in white spots unique like fingerprints, is as tough as leather and protects it even from the boldest predators. It's a cartilaginous fish, not a mammal, though its name often confuses people. Swimming slowly, as if in a trance, it glides through the sea with immense grace. It can live for over 100 years, crossing entire oceans in search of food. Some scientists believe they use the Earth's magnetic fields as a guide. After watching its calm majesty for a few minutes, we powered down, gave it space, and let the giant continue on its way, as if it had never been there at all.

title: Logitech MX Master 4 : What’s Changing and What’s Staying?
transcription: So, it looks like Logitech's gearing up for a new drop. Yep. The MX Master 4 is on the way. And honestly, it's about time. The 3S is still a killer mouse, no doubt, but it's been holding down the fort for a while now. Even legends need a bit of a glow up, right? Now, the new one? It's not officially announced yet, but thanks to some early leaks and a few eagle-eyed folks online, we've got a decent idea of what's coming. And spoiler alert, it's not some wild redesign. This feels more like Logitech saying, hey, we heard you, let's polish this up a bit. The overall shape, still that same ergonomic magic that made the MX series so popular. But if you zoom in, there are definitely some tweaks. The main buttons look a bit more refined, less chunky, more seamless, and the thumb rest, that's getting a redesign too. Rumor has it there's a new button layout there, maybe even a dedicated gesture button and a beefed up thumb scroll wheel. Sounds small, but if you've used this mouse daily, you know how much those tweaks matter. And speaking of small upgrades that'll make life easier, the LED indicators moving. No more flipping the mouse or guessing battery levels. It's supposed to sit right on top now behind the scroll lock button. Finally. Internally, things are still a bit hush hush, but let's be real. People are hoping Logitech gives the sensor a bit of a bump. The 3S had an 8,000 DPI sensor, which is solid, but maybe we'll see something smoother, faster, maybe even better tracking on glass. Fingers crossed. Also, word is the material quality might get an upgrade. That would be huge. The old rubbery texture on the 3S, it feels great out of the box, but give it a year and it starts picking up shine, fingerprints, and just ends up looking kind of tired. Software-wise, Logitech Options+ is sticking around, which is great. It's what lets you remap buttons, set app specific functions, and use that magical flow feature to jump across multiple devices like a boss. If you're juggling a laptop and a desktop setup, you know how clutch that is. So, yeah, don't expect a complete overhaul here. The MX Master 4 is shaping up to be one of those thoughtful, let's refine this kind of updates, not flashy, but practical. And honestly, that's exactly what people who rely on this mouse every day are probably hoping for. Now we just wait for Logitech to hit us with the official reveal. Shouldn't be long. title: How To Charge Apple Watch Without Charger? No Magnetic Charger, Cable Or Wireless Charger Required
